TITLE: Boat rental cost Fort Lauderdale? (Pontoons, Cruisers & Yachts Compared)
Fort Lauderdale is known as the "Yachting Capital of the World." Getting out on the water here is a must. But before booking a charter, the big question is:
how much does a boat rental in Fort Lauderdale actually cost?
According to Lauderdale Adventures Owner, Jeremy Beller,
“It depends on your budget and requirements. There is a huge spectrum of vessels and prices available.”
Here’s a breakdown of all three — and what you actually get for your money.
Yacht Rentals in Fort Lauderdale
Yachts are the premium end of the Fort Lauderdale boating market. Fort Lauderdale hosts the annual Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show, the largest in the world. So, there’s no shortage of charter companies offering high-end yacht experiences.
Typical Yacht Rental Costs
Half-day (4 hours):
$1,500 – $5,000+
Full day (8 hours):
$3,000 – $15,000+
Luxury/superyacht charters:
$10,000 – $50,000+ per day
Pricing varies widely based on the size of the vessel (40 ft to 100+ ft), the number of crew members, fuel costs, and any add-on amenities like catering, water toys, or a chef on board.
What's Typically Included
Captain and crew
Fuel (sometimes billed separately)
Basic safety equipment
What's Usually Extra
Food and alcohol
Water toys (jet skis, paddleboards)
Gratuity for crew (typically 15–20%)
Dockage fees
Yachts make sense for corporate events, milestone celebrations, or groups who want a true luxury experience. That said, for most visitors and locals in Fort Lauderdale, a yacht charter is overkill — and the price tag reflects that.
Pleasure Cruiser Rentals in Fort Lauderdale
Pleasure cruisers sit in the middle of the market. They’re larger and more enclosed than pontoon boats but more accessible than full yacht charters. Think bowriders, center consoles, and mid-size cabin cruisers in the 25–40 ft range.
Typical Pleasure Cruiser Costs
2-hour rental:
$400 – $900
$700 – $1,800
$1,200 – $3,500
Many pleasure cruiser rentals are self-skippered (you drive), which means you'll need a valid Florida boating license or proof of completion of a boating safety course. Some companies do offer captained options at an additional fee.
Basic safety gear
Fuel allowance (overages billed separately)
Captain (often $150–$400/day)
Water sports equipment
Ice and coolers
Navigation into restricted areas
Pleasure cruisers are great if you're comfortable behind the wheel and want the freedom to explore on your own. The downside? You're responsible for navigation, safety, and following all local waterway rules — which can be stressful if you're not an experienced boater.
Pontoon Boat Rentals in Fort Lauderdale
Here's where things get fun — and accessible! Pontoon boats have become one of the most popular ways to experience Fort Lauderdale's waterways, and for good reason. They're spacious, stable, easy to enjoy, and they work great for groups of all kinds.

What's Included with Every Lauderdale Adventures Rental
Your choice of licensed, local Captain

You just bring your food, drinks, sunscreen, and towels — and your Captain handles everything else.
Tips for Getting the Best Value on a Fort Lauderdale Boat Rental
1. Book Early
Weekend slots, especially in peak season (November through April), fill up fast. Booking ahead locks in your rate and your preferred time.
2. Watch for Hidden Fees
Many boat rental companies advertise a low base rate but add fuel surcharges, docking fees, and equipment rental on top. Always ask what's included before you pay.
3. Consider What Your Group Actually Needs
A 6-person bachelorette party doesn't need a $10,000 yacht. A spacious, well-equipped pontoon boat with a captain who doubles as a guide, photographer, and DJ hits differently — and leaves money for waterside lunch and drinks.
4. Factor in the Captain
Self-skippered rentals require a boating license in Florida. If you don't have one, a captained charter isn't just easier — it's often legally required. Make sure you're comparing apples to apples when looking at pricing.
5. Check the Reviews
Fort Lauderdale has hundreds of boat rental operators. Look for consistent 4.8+ ratings, recent reviews, and mentions of safety, punctuality, and the overall experience.
Boat Rental Costs in Fort Lauderdale Summary

TITLE: FAQ About Renting a Boat in Fort Lauderdale
Thinking about renting a boat in Fort Lauderdale but not sure where to start? You're not alone. We get a lot of great questions from first-timers and repeat visitors alike. Below, we've answered the most common ones — from what type of boat I should rent to whether Fort Lauderdale is even worth exploring by water (spoiler: it absolutely is).
Who has pontoon boat rentals in Florida with licensed captains?
includes your choice of a local, licensed captain on all of our boat rental trips. We do not offer bareboat charters. We're fully licensed and insured and follow all Coast Guard rules and regulations, with a 100% safety rating.
Top booze cruise option in Fort Lauderdale?
Lauderdale Adventures is one of the top choices for a
Fort Lauderdale booze cruise
Key points:·
· 8 years in business, 100% safety rating· Spacious and comfy pontoon boats for up to 12 guests· BYOB and customizable day and night boat trips
Where can I book a customizable boat cruise in Fort Lauderdale?
All Lauderdale Adventures boat cruise trips are fully customizable. No cookie-cutter boat trips here. Talk with your captain before you launch — he'll work with you to plan a custom itinerary that's ideal for your day or night on the water. See our
full rental options and pricing
for what's included on every trip, from canopy shade to paddle boards.
What to expect on a Fort Lauderdale sunset cruise?
Lauderdale Adventures offers a
. It's a 2.5-hour boat charter starting around 6:00. You'll take in a beautiful South Florida sunset aboard one of our spacious pontoon boats, then sit back and enjoy a leisurely cruise along our many miles of scenic waterways.
Typical highlights:· Views of waterfront mansions and yachts· Calm water conditions in the evening· Sunset over the Intracoastal Waterway
What to bring:· Drinks and food· Music playlist· Camera or phone for photos
How far in advance should I book a boat rental in Fort Lauderdale?
Reserve in advance for weekends and holidays, as availability can fill quickly. Our boats are designed for groups up to 12, with flexible booking options to fit your schedule.
How Much Does a Boat Rental Cost in Fort Lauderdale?
Pricing depends on the charter length and what's included. With Lauderdale Adventures, pontoon rentals start at $460 for a 2.5-hour sunset cruise and go up to just over $1,000 for a full 8-hour adventure, with everything — captain, premium water toys and essentials - included in the price. See our
full pricing breakdown by charter length
for exact rates.
How Many People Fit on a Pontoon Boat?
Lauderdale Adventures has two pontoon boats: the Adventure I can comfortably accommodate 10 guests, and the Adventure II can comfortably accommodate 12 guests. This makes them ideal for group outings, bachelorette parties, birthday celebrations, and company events. The spacious deck layout means everyone has room to move around, whether they're paddleboarding off the back, lounging on the party pad, or dancing to whatever the captain's spinning on the Bluetooth speaker.
Can You Drink Alcohol on a Boat in Fort Lauderdale?
Yes. Florida law allows passengers to consume alcohol on a boat, as long as the vessel operator is not impaired (the legal limit is 0.08 BAC). On all Lauderdale Adventures charters, your licensed captain stays completely sober while you enjoy the day. We welcome BYOB for guests 21 and older — just skip the glass bottles and bring cans or plastic drinkware instead.
Where to Book a Sandbar Beach Hopping Tour in Fort Lauderdale?
The Fort Lauderdale Sandbar is a popular shallow-water spot where boats anchor, music plays, and guests wade around with a drink in hand. Lauderdale Adventures offers Sandbar and Beach Hopping charters that take you to the best spots based on the day's tides and crowds — we recommend at least a 4-hour charter to make the most of it. According to Jeremy Beller, Yacht Captain and Owner of Lauderdale Adventures, "
ABSOLUTELY! We are one of the top boating destinations in the world, the Yacht Capital. But not everyone can afford the yachting lifestyle, so I started Lauderdale Adventures so everyone could afford a great day on the water
." Our city has more than 165 miles of waterways, the Intracoastal Waterway, and a year-round climate that makes on-water fun available year-round. The diversity of experiences is hard to beat.

By identifying and addressing the root causes of inequities, the Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (OEDI) will deepen the Port’s current efforts toward equity and further catalyze organization-wide, systemic change.
OEDI is conducting a variety of foundational initiatives. We will lead employee and leadership trainings to improve understanding about equity at the Port, participate in strategic planning to infuse equity in all initiatives and objectives, and collaborate with the Commission office to embed equitable policies Port-wide.
This office will foster a transformational and lasting change to the culture of the Port. Those directly and deeply impacted by systemic and institutional discrimination will find opportunities for economic gain, leadership development, and participation in how the Port operates and impacts our communities.
We need everyone, Port leadership and staff, community partners, and Port of Seattle contractors to work together to improve our practices and generate lasting, transformative change.
The Port of Seattle's Equity Statement and Vision
The Port of Seattle commits to taking a lead role in regional and national efforts to achieve equity and social justice. We are identifying and dismantling structural barriers to ensure that historically oppressed communities, particularly communities of color, have access to the resources they need to thrive.
Bias and oppression are embedded in our society, systems, and our organization. By failing to acknowledge inequities, we play a role in perpetuating them. We can and must do better. In order to achieve equitable outcomes for all our communities, we must be accountable for equitable policies that ensure racial, social, and economic justice are achieved in strategies, practices, and projects.
Our Vision is to develop a Port that mirrors — throughout its breadth of operations and services and within its leadership structure — the diversity of our community, instills principles of equity in its culture, and ensures a fair and intentional distribution of opportunities to expand economic development and quality of life for all.

Hosting Events on Port Property
Thank you for considering Port of Seattle non-aviation property for your event.
Introduction
The purpose of Port of Seattle outdoor public spaces is to provide public access, support Port business operations, and facilitate community use. In an effort to balance community access and private demand, the Port offers – whenever possible – certain public spaces for community and private events when they do not overly restrict access by the general public or interfere with port business operations. The Port of Seattle does not provide event planning services or event equipment rental.
Event Licenses
An Event License is needed to reserve any outdoor Port of Seattle property or facility. Event Licenses are issued by the Port in its sole discretion based upon an evaluation of availability of Port facilities, as well as the nature and duration of the proposed activity which is the subject of the license application.Sites that are available for events are listed on the Potential Event Sites page of the application.
Application
An form is available to download. It should be completed in detail. Answers to all questions should give a full description of what activities are planned, when the facilities are needed, and the number of people expected. Additional pages may be added if needed. An incomplete, unsigned and/or undated application will not be processed.Applications for event licenses should be submitted at least thirty (30) days before the requested date of use. Applications submitted with less than 30 days’ notice are not guaranteed to be approved.Event License Applications are accepted starting on the first business day of the calendar year in which the event takes place. Applications for events taking place in January will be accepted on the first business day of December of the previous year.The Port of Seattle retains the right to accept and consider Event Licenses at any time for maritime, recreational boating, or aviation-related events, for Port of Seattle customer events, or for extra-large events requiring significant lead time.
Fees and Charges
Fees may include but are not exclusive to:
Base minimum fee
Electrical hookup fee
Additional use fees such as moorage, facility equipment rental
Labor fee
Upon review of an Event License application, facility management may determine that Port staff is required onsite at an event. Applicants will be advised of this requirement during license review.
Any damage repairs by the Port following the event (see Damage Mitigation on the Event License Policy page)
Damage deposit (for parks only)
A $500.00 per day fine will be charged for any equipment found on the property before or after the license term (for parks only)
Additional fees may be required if applicable. Applicants will be advised of this requirement during license review.
Once we review your application, we will send you an outline of costs. The Port of Seattle and may require special approvals or permits from other agencies in addition to the above fees. All fees (with the exception of the parks damage deposit) are nonrefundable. Proof of insurance, permits, and fees must be provided to the Port of Seattle no later than seven (7) days prior to the commencement of the event.

TITLE: Stephen P. Metruck | Port of Seattle
Executive Director Leadership Team
At the helm of a world-class economic engine in a dynamic region
As executive director of the Port of Seattle, Steve Metruck leads a county-wide special purpose government responsible for providing world-class trade, travel, and logistics services to one of the nation’s most dynamic and fastest growing regions. The Port manages operations for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) – one of the nation’s busiest passenger airports – as well as cruise, commercial fishing, grain terminals, recreational marinas, and other real estate activities.
The Port also operates one of North America’s largest maritime cargo shipping gateways through the Northwest Seaport Alliance, a joint effort with the Port of Tacoma. As executive director, Metruck leads 1,900 employees who deliver safe, efficient, and high-quality services to the region while improving local economic opportunities and safeguarding our environment. The Port of Seattle is one of the Pacific Northwest’s leading economic engines, generating over 216,000 jobs and $894 million in state and local taxes.
Distinguished leadership career in the public sector
Metruck came to the Port of Seattle following a 34-year career with the U.S. Coast Guard, retiring as a Rear Admiral. He has experience across a diverse range of operations and executive-level assignments on both coasts, the Great Lakes, and the Gulf of Mexico. As the Chief Financial Officer for the Coast Guard, Metruck was responsible for all Coast Guard financial management and execution of the service’s $10 billion annual appropriation. As Commander of the Fifth District in Portsmouth, Virginia, he had overall responsibility for the full range of U.S. Coast Guard missions carried out from central New Jersey to North Carolina.
Executive-level management experience committed to diversity and safety
Throughout his career, Metruck has maintained a strong record of advancing a diverse and safe workplace. He is currently leading the Port through a groundbreaking effort to increase diversity in contracting and is supporting expansion of internal employee resource groups and efforts to increase diversity at the Port. Metruck emphasized employee safety and diversity during his Coast Guard career as well. He served three years on the Coast Guard’s Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Taskforce and as a member of the Coast Guard Academy’s Board of Trustees, he oversaw significant increases in the diversity of the student body.

Advanced Flight Training Programs
Sharpen your skills and prepare for new opportunities.
Aircraft Transition
This course is designed to transition pilots into new airframes in order to increase experience and marketability. Ground school is included – covers basic aircraft composition, systems, limitations and performance. Flight training teaches flight characteristics and emergency procedures.
Aircraft Refresher
This course is designed for pilots who currently or have previously flown various types of aircraft. Ground school reviews aircraft systems, limitations and performance. Flight training reviews flight characteristics and emergency procedures.
Inadvertent IMC Course
Recovery from Inadvertent Flight into Instrument Meteorological Conditions consists of classroom and simulator training. It teaches pilots the conditions where flight in IMC might be encountered. You will review several accidents that occurred when pilots have encountered IMC conditions without having the proper training to transition to flight reference instruments. Simulator training gives pilots the skills to maintain control of the aircraft and return to VFR conditions.
helicopter training class rates
Mountain Flying
This course trains pilots to safely navigate and operate in the mountainous terrain. Ground training covers the unique weather and wind dynamics that occur in mountainous terrain and gives pilots skills and techniques to make flying safer. Flight training offers pilots and opportunity to dynamically use the techniques learned in ground training in a practical situation.
Aerial Firefighting Training
This course will develop and implement a helicopter-based aerial fighting program. Students will learn the basic aspects of aerial firefighting that includes tank fill operations (ground and snorkel), bucket fill operations, aerial firefighting strategies and tactics, and safety.

TITLE: Chicago Boat Rental FAQ | Lakefront Boating
Everything you need to know about chartering with Lakefront Boating.
Location & Getting There
Where are your boat rentals located in Chicago?
All of our boats are located on Dock "i" at Diversey Harbor in Lincoln Park, 2601 North Cannon Drive, Chicago, IL 60614. You will receive detailed boarding instructions and directions prior to your scheduled charter.
Is parking available at Diversey Harbor?
There is free street parking available along Cannon Drive. Paid parking is also available at the Diversey Driving Range. We recommend taking a rideshare when possible, especially on weekends and holidays. Please note that parking availability may be limited on special event days in the area.
How early should I arrive to the dock for my boat rental in Chicago?
We recommend arriving at the dock at least 15 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time. This allows time for signing liability waivers, completing a safety briefing, and getting everyone settled onboard. Arriving early helps ensure you can maximize your time on the water during your charter.
What happens if we are late?
Your charter time begins at your scheduled reservation time. Late arrivals may result in a shortened rental period, as all charters must return at their scheduled end time to avoid impacting subsequent reservations. We recommend arriving 15 to 20 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time to allow for boarding and safety instructions.
Boat Rental Basics
Is fuel included in the cost of the boat rental in Chicago?
Yes. Fuel is included in the total rental price for normal cruising within the Chicago harbor and Playpen area. Guests are not responsible for fueling the boat before or after their charter.
Does the boat have a bathroom onboard?
Yes. Each of our vessels is equipped with at least one private onboard restroom for your convenience during your boat rental in Chicago.
Is there a cooler or refrigerator onboard?
Yes. Each of our boats is equipped with a refrigerator for your convenience. Coolers are also available onboard.
Do you provide floating devices with your boat rental in Chicago?
A floating lily pad is available as an optional add-on for $60. This can be added to your reservation at the time of booking or anytime after your booking is confirmed, subject to availability.
Food, Drinks & Personal Items
Can we bring alcohol on a boat rental in Chicago?
Yes. Guests who are 21 years of age or older are welcome to bring alcohol onboard for personal consumption during your boat rental. We recommend avoiding glass bottles for safety reasons and to help prevent potential damage to the vessel.
Is ice provided with your boat rentals in Chicago?
Ice is not provided. We recommend bringing your own ice and beverages for your charter. Coolers are available onboard for your convenience.
What should we bring for our boat rental in Chicago?
We recommend bringing: food and beverages, ice, towels, sunscreen, a portable phone charger, and a valid ID.
What should we wear on the boat?
We recommend wearing comfortable clothing and soft-soled shoes. Black-soled shoes or high heels are not recommended as they may mark or damage the vessel.
What items are not recommended to bring on a boat rental in Chicago?
For safety, cleanliness, and to help prevent potential damage to our vessels, we strongly recommend that guests do not bring the following items onboard: red wine or other staining beverages and foods, fireworks, confetti or glitter, glass bottles, or hookahs. Please note that Chicago Harbors regulations do not allow firearms or weapons of any kind, along with illegal substances, on harbor property. Bringing any of the above items onboard may increase the risk of damage, additional cleaning, or safety concerns during your charter experience.
Can I bring my pet on a boat rental in Chicago?
Pets are not recommended onboard due to safety, space limitations, and the marine environment. If you plan to bring a pet, please contact us in advance to discuss your specific request. Approval may be granted on a case-by-case basis. Approved pets must wear a properly fitted life jacket at all times while onboard. Service animals are permitted in accordance with applicable laws. Please notify us in advance if you plan to bring a service animal so we can best prepare for your charter.
Can we decorate the boat for a birthday or special event?
Yes. You are welcome to bring small decorations for birthdays or special occasions. We recommend avoiding items that may stain, leave residue, or become difficult to remove such as confetti or glitter.
Activities & Destinations
Do you go to the Playpen in Chicago?
Yes. During your boat rental, you are welcome to cruise to popular destinations on Lake Michigan such as the Chicago Playpen. The Playpen is one of the most popular boating areas in Chicago for anchoring, relaxing, and enjoying time on the water with friends and family.
Can we go down the Chicago River during our boat rental?
Yes. Your charter can explore both Lake Michigan and the Chicago River, offering a unique view of the city's iconic architecture and waterfront. Please note that on Fridays, Saturdays, and holidays, a minimum 4-hour reservation is required to allow sufficient time to travel through the Chicago Harbor Lock System.
How long does it take to go through the locks to access the Chicago River?
Passing through the Chicago Harbor Lock System typically takes anywhere from 30 minutes to one hour, depending on boat traffic and lock operations. For this reason, a minimum 4-hour reservation is required on Fridays, Saturdays, and holidays to allow sufficient time to travel between Lake Michigan and the Chicago River.
Can we swim on the charter?
Yes. You are welcome to swim in Lake Michigan when the boat is anchored in a safe area. For safety reasons, please follow all instructions provided during your charter and use proper flotation devices as needed.
Can we bring our own floats and rafts on a boat rental in Chicago?
Yes. You are welcome to bring your own floats and rafts to use during your boat rental. Please ensure that all personal floatation items can be easily stored while the vessel is underway.
Can we tow or waterski off the boat?
Towing activities such as waterskiing, wakeboarding, or tubing are not permitted during your boat rental.
Can we fish off the boat?
No. Fishing is not permitted during your boat rental under any circumstances.
Can we play our own music on the boat?
Yes. All of our boats are equipped with Bluetooth-enabled sound systems so you can connect your device and play your own music during your boat rental in Chicago.
Do you offer fireworks cruises in Chicago?
Yes. You are welcome to enjoy the Chicago fireworks display during your boat rental, depending on your reservation time and location on the water. Fireworks are scheduled from Memorial Day through Labor Day on Wednesdays at 9:00 PM and Saturdays at 10:00 PM by Navy Pier. We recommend booking an evening time slot on scheduled fireworks dates for the best viewing experience.
Captain & Bareboat Charter
What is a bareboat charter?
A bareboat charter is a type of boat rental where the charterer temporarily assumes control of the vessel and responsibility for the vessel for the duration of the charter. As part of this arrangement, you may operate the vessel yourself if qualified or choose to hire a captain separately for your trip. If you choose to hire a captain, you will contract with and pay them directly.
Do I need a boating license to rent a boat in Chicago?
No. A boating license is not required to rent a boat in Chicago. Most guests choose to hire a qualified captain to operate the vessel for their charter so they can relax and enjoy their time on the water. Hot Air Ballooning FAQs
What should I wear for my balloon flight?
Dress for adventure! We recommend wearing comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and closed-toe shoes. It’s also a good idea to dress in layers, as temperatures can vary during the flight.
How long does the entire experience last?
The entire balloon flight experience typically lasts about 3 to 4 hours, this includes pre-flight preparation, the flight itself (usually 1 hour), and post-flight celebrations.
Can I bring my camera or phone on the flight?
Yes absolutely, you’re welcome to bring your camera or phone to capture the breathtaking views during your flight! Just make sure they’re securely stored when not in use to avoid any accidents.
What happens if the weather is bad on my scheduled date?
If the weather is unflyable, we will work with you to reschedule for another convenient time. If we cancel due to the weather or you cancel outside 96 hours prior to your flight we will also issue a full refund in the event that we can not find a suitable date to reschedule your flight. Your safety and satisfaction are our top priority.
What is your cancellation policy?
You can cancel or reschedule with at least 96 hours’ notice for a full refund. Cancellations made less than 96 hours in advance of our meeting time may result in full payment.

TITLE: Parasailing on Kāʻanapali Beach, Maui | 1,200 ft Flights
Kāʻanapali Beach · Maui, Hawaiʻi
Fly up to 1,200 feet above West Maui on the yellow smiley parasail you can see from your hotel lanai. Solo, tandem or triple, dry takeoff and landing, about an hour on the boat.

Why Kāʻanapali
The best water on the island for it
Kāʻanapali sits in the lee of the West Maui Mountains, which is why the water here is glass most mornings while the rest of the island is working. That protection is what makes a 1,200-foot flight comfortable rather than sporty.
From altitude you get the full run of the coast: the resort strip and Black Rock below you, Lahaina down the shoreline, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi across the channel, and the West Maui Mountains behind. In winter the same channel fills with humpback whales, which is why our season runs May 16 to December 14 and the boats come out after that.
Mornings are the calmest. Later departures are still flyable, they just have more texture.
You launch and land on the deck. Nobody swims out to anything.
Want a dip at the end? Tell the crew and they'll dunk your toes.
Crew speaks English, Spanish and Japanese.
Flights
Fly alone or fly together
Solo
One flyer
The quietest version. Minimum 130 lb to fly alone, so most kids go tandem with an adult.
Most booked
Tandem
Two side by side, 125–560 lb combined. The one most couples and parent-child pairs pick.
Groups
Triple
Three under one parasail. Popular with families who don't want anyone sitting it out.
Private
Whole boat
Our two newest boats carry 12, so a family group or a celebration can take the whole trip.
Who runs it
Award-winning operator, Hawaiʻi raised
Dave Vogt grew up around watersports on the islands of Oʻahu and Kauaʻi, and has since flown more than 25,000 people across Florida, Catalina Island, Lake Tahoe, Belize, Mexico, Newport Beach and Santa Barbara — and now Maui.
He holds the Water Sports Industry Association's Award of Excellence for his contributions to the parasail industry — an award that weighs safety record, training and service rather than volume.
Every flight is run by USCG-certified captains on equipment inspected and maintained on schedule. If the wind isn't right, we reschedule or refund — we don't fly marginal conditions.

Right on the sand, a three-minute walk north of Whalers Village. Our shuttle boat takes 6 at a time from the beach out to the parasail boat — expect to get your feet wet, and watch for turtles on the way.

Park at Whalers Village

=== PAGE: https://www.kaanapalibeachparasail.com/guides/what-to-expect-first-flight
TITLE: What to Expect on Your First Parasail Flight
Guide · First timers
Check-in to back on the sand in about an hour. Here's the whole thing, in order, so nothing is a surprise.
Before you leave
Book and check the details
Reserve your departure online and you'll get a confirmation with the meeting point. Departures meet on the sand a short walk north of Whalers Village — look for the yellow PARASAIL umbrellas.
30 minutes before
Check in on the beach
Sign your waiver before you arrive — the link comes in your confirmation email, and a parent or guardian signs for anyone under 18. On the day, find the crew under the umbrellas and give your name. That’s check-in.
Departure
Shuttle out to the boat
From here you'll board our shuttle boat, which takes 6 at a time out to the parasail boat. The shuttle can be a fun ride in itself — be prepared to get your feet wet, and keep an eye out for turtles on the way.
On the water
Life jacket and safety brief
Once you're aboard the parasail boat, the captain and crew run the safety briefing and hand out life jackets. Nothing to memorise — they walk you through the hand signals for 'take me higher' and 'bring me down', and that's the whole curriculum.
Your turn
Harness up on the deck
The crew fits your harness while you're still in your seat on the boat. When they call you up to the flight deck, they clip you in. You sit back into it — nothing to hold on to unless you want to, and nothing to steer.
Air time
Up to 1,200 feet
The winch pays the line out and you rise. Flight times vary with the weather — usually 8 to 14 minutes in the air — and the boat runs a loop of the coast while you're up there. Want to go higher, lower, or get your toes dipped at the end? Signal the crew.
Back aboard
Dry landing, then the beach
The winch brings you back down onto the same deck you left. Once everyone's flown, the boat heads in and the shuttle runs you back to the sand. Whole trip runs about an hour depending on how many flyers are aboard.
What it feels like
Quieter than you're picturing
The lift is gradual, not a jolt — the winch pays the line out and you rise. Because you're moving with the air, there's almost no wind in your face. The engine noise falls away behind you.
What people remark on afterwards is the silence and the view: the resort strip and Black Rock below, Lahaina down the coast, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi across the channel, and the West Maui Mountains behind you.

Where does the snorkel tour leave from?
Kāʻanapali Beach — the same stretch of sand as our parasail check-in. You board off the beach rather than from a harbour.
How long is the trip?

Do I need to be a strong swimmer?

=== PAGE: https://www.kaanapalibeachparasail.com/guides/parasailing-weight-limits
TITLE: Parasailing Weight Limits and Age Limits | Maui
Guide · Before you book
The numbers, first: for a tandem flight, to fly solo, and with no upper limit. Everything below is what those numbers mean in practice.
minimum, solo
tandem, combined
None
upper age limit
There is a minimum as well as a maximum
Most people arrive expecting only an upper limit, and the lower one is the number that catches them out. A solo flyer needs to be at least 130 lb. Below that there is not enough load on the parasail to fly it properly — it is a physics limit rather than a policy, and it is why children almost always fly tandem.
At the other end, a tandem flight runs up to 560 lb for the two flyers together. In between, anything from 125 lb combined works.
Tandem and triple are combined weights
The 125–560 lb range is the total of both people, not each. Triple flights carry three at once. Between 1–3 flyers go up on each parasail, and the crew sorts the pairings on the boat once they can see the group — you do not need to work it out before you book.
If your group is over the limit
Nobody gets turned away for arithmetic. Each boat carries up to 12 guests and flights run continuously through the session, so a party that does not fit one pairing is split across two. The only thing that helps is telling the crew your real weights rather than your optimistic ones — the numbers are what keeps the parasail flying, not a formality.
Age 5 and up, no upper limit
The minimum age is 5. There is no maximum: the harness takes your weight at the hips, you are seated the whole flight, and both takeoff and landing happen on the deck rather than in the water. Check with your doctor first if you have back, neck or heart conditions, or recent surgery.
A parent or guardian signs the waiver for anyone under 18. If you are flying with a child, covers the rest of it.
is parasailing safe for kids
The captain has the last word
Weather and sea conditions change what works on a given morning. A pairing that is fine in flat water may not be in a stiff afternoon breeze, and the final call belongs to the captain on the day. It is the same reason the flight window moves: covers the 1,200 ft line and the 8–14 minutes in the air.
how the flight works
What is the weight limit for parasailing?
For tandem flights the combined weight of both flyers runs 125–560 lb. Solo flyers need to be at least 130 lb — there is a minimum rather than only a maximum, because a light flyer does not load the parasail enough to fly it properly. Weather and sea conditions change what works on the day, and the final call is always the captain's.
Is there a weight limit for parasailing?
Yes, at both ends. Tandem is 125–560 lb combined, and a solo flyer must be at least 130 lb. Triple flights are also available, and the crew works out the combinations on the boat once they can see the group.
What is the maximum weight for parasailing?
560 lb combined for a tandem flight. If your party is over that, the crew will split you across flights rather than turn you away — every trip carries up to 12 guests and flights run through the session.
What is the minimum weight to parasail solo?
130 lb. Below that you fly tandem, which most people prefer anyway — it is the same flight with someone next to you.
What is the age limit for parasailing?
Ages 5 and up. There is no upper age limit; the harness takes your weight at the hips and the landing is soft. Check with your doctor first if you have back, neck or heart conditions, or recent surgery.
How old do you have to be to parasail?
Five. Most children under the solo minimum of 130 lb fly tandem with a parent, and a waiver is signed by a parent or guardian.
Do you get weighed before parasailing?
The crew asks your weight rather than putting you on a scale, and pairs the flights from what you tell them. It is worth being accurate — the numbers are what keeps the parasail flying properly, not a formality.

=== PAGE: https://www.kaanapalibeachparasail.com/guides/is-parasailing-safe-for-kids
TITLE: Is Parasailing Safe for Kids? | Kāʻanapali Beach Parasail
Guide · Families
Short answer: yes, and it's one of the calmer things you'll do on the water in Maui. Here's what actually happens, what the limits are, and how to decide whether your child is ready.
to fly solo
Dry
takeoff and landing
Why it's gentler than it looks
From the beach, a parasail looks like a thrill ride. In the air it's the opposite. The parasail rises slowly on a winch, there's no wind rush because you're moving with the air, and once the line is out you're barely aware of the boat. Most kids describe it as floating, and most parents are surprised how quiet it is.
There is nothing for your child to operate. No steering, no pedals, no instructions to remember. The crew handles the harness, the captain handles the line, and the flyer sits.
You never leave the boat wet
Both takeoff and landing happen on the deck. Your child steps into the harness standing up, lifts off from the back of the boat, and comes back down onto the same platform. Nobody swims, nobody gets dragged, and nobody has to climb back aboard. If they want a dip in the ocean at the end, that's a request the crew grants — not part of the flight.
Fly with them, not behind them
Solo flights need a 130 lb minimum, so most children go tandem with a parent or triple with two family members. That solves the nerves problem better than any explanation from us: a five-year-old holding a parent's hand at 1,200 feet is a different experience than going up alone.
Tandem runs 125–560 lb combined, which covers nearly every adult-child pairing. The crew works out the combinations on the boat once they can see the group.
What the safety actually consists of
USCG-certified captains, harnesses and lines inspected and maintained on a schedule, and a hard rule about conditions: if the wind or sea state is outside our limits, we don't fly. You get rescheduled at no charge or refunded in full. Nobody on our crew is deciding whether to push it.
Dave Vogt holds the Water Sports Industry Association's Award of Excellence for his contributions to the parasail industry, and has flown more than 25,000 people across Hawaiʻi, California, Florida, Mexico and Belize.
When to wait a year
A child who genuinely doesn't want to go shouldn't be talked into it — being harnessed in is not the moment to change your mind. Boat time is the other consideration: the trip runs about an hour, and a child who struggles on boats will feel that more than the flight itself. Anyone can stay aboard and watch; they still get the ride.

No. Takeoff and landing are both on the boat deck, and every flyer wears a life jacket regardless.

=== PAGE: https://www.montereybayboatworks.com/mbbwhistory
TITLE: History | boatworks
2025 marked out 40th year in service, we want to take a look back at how Monterey Bay Boatworks came to be. Jumping back to 1924, Angelo Siino opened the Siino Boat Works, then in 1937 acquired the Monterey Boat Works, currently located and used by the Hopkins Marine Station as a lecture hall. Frank Siino was born the second son of Angelo Siino. He and his older brother Ray, were raised working in the original Monterey Boat Works in the family tradition of building and repairing handcrafted wooden boats. To further keep his hand in the trade, he built the wood boat, Felucca Liboria, that hangs in the Monterey Aquarium. It was with a bit of pride that Frank received Mr. Packard at his home one day, as Mr. Packard wanted to look at the Felucca and ask Frank if they could put it on exhibit where it can be seen today. With the onset of a life-changing illness that Ray was dealing with, the more popular use of fiberglass and steel boats, and a diminishing fishing industry in Monterey, it was decided to close the Monterey Boat Works yard in 1970. Frank went to work as a manager in the local Tynan Lumber yard in Monterey, but never left his lifelong trade of working on boats, as he did so on the side, repairing and tending to the wooden boats of the Monterey fleet. With the support of his friend Mike Maiorana, Frank left Tynan Lumber to return full-time to his lifelong passion of working on boats, but this time at Monterey Bay Boatworks. Mike Maiorana had told the story on a number of occasions that when he was asked to join as a partner in the new Monterey Bay Boatworks Boatyard, he would only do so if Frank Siino ran the yard.Mike Maiorana came to America in 1938 when he was just 3 years old. Like the thousands of other Italians who immigrated to the US, he came with the promise of “The American Dream”. In the late 1970, over coffee with his fishing friends, the Monterey Bay Boatworks became his dream. The local commercial fisherman needed a full-service boatyard where they could maintain and fuel their vessels. The only full-service boatyard they had access to at the time was in Moss Landing, a 2-hour boat ride away. Mike, being the only confident English speaker of the group, was ready to help and applied for the necessary permits. With Monterey’s city council’s approval, permits to start construction were granted in the summer of 1981. In 1985, Monterey Bay Boatworks was established, and in 1986, with the help of the original 5 business partners, remaining active shareholders Chuck Piccuta and Bart Bruno, the Boatworks was operational. Chuck, a friend of Mike’s, saw the gleam in Mike’s eyes while sharing his Boatworks dream with him in the garage with a paper-mache diagram, and knew this was an adventure he could not pass on. This was no easy task, as there were a lot of ducks to acquire before putting them in a row. Chuck, with his experience in finance, found two limited partners to join: Dave Lewis and Clancy Spangle. But someone was missing to complete the team. Bart Bruno, although born in Carmel, is from an Italian immigrant family with a passion for the boating community. His family ran B. C. Bruno & Sons, boat rentals, fishing charters, harbor facilities, fishing supplies, general merchandise, and groceries out of Pittsburg, California, after leaving Monterey near the end of the Sardine era. At a young age, his passion for the boating world began within his family’s company. Over the years, he branched out into the construction and engineering world, and with that, he founded Monterey Peninsula Engineering (MPE), as you can see all around the Monterey Area. Mike met Bart while first starting the realization of his dream. Bart, having a boat in the city marina, put his name on the waitlist with Mike for the future marina. When Mike needed support to petition the city for his dream, he reached out to Bart for a recommendation, which would then result in a partnership agreement. What started as a mere dream has grown into a decades-long, successful adventure. Monterey Bay Boatworks broke ground in 1985, erecting two buildings for restaurants, a dive shop, kayaking, and Boatworks operations. In the beginning, it was a family affair, as Chuck remembers, wives, siblings, and children all participated in building Monterey Bay Boatworks. With memories of being on his hands and knees down on the dock nailing in rub rails, it was a labor of love that pieced the marina and Boatworks together. It was no small feat bring this dream into the real world but over time finding those who brought a little extra to table like Dave Garrett the General Manager for 9 years, who then hired Diane Colwell, General Manager and COO for 21 years, overall serving MBBW for 30 years and Marieta Aranda CFO for 29 years and the current COO, thus ensuring the longevity and success of Monterey Bay Boatworks.While the Frank Siino Boatyard catered to the local commercial fishing community, there was another need for dockage. In 1986, the Breakwater Cove Marina was completed with 60 berths (including frog and end-ties) with a handful of moorings. Following its success and highly sought out need for boat berths in the Monterey area, the first Marina expansion began in 2004 and ended in 2005, adding 35’ berths and updating electrical. The original fuel tanks were installed in the late 80s, then Jim Allen designed our boom system, using boat masts, and has since been upgraded based on his plan still with a boat’s mast, with the last fuel dock expansion completed in 2005. Later, adding the Marina tenant restrooms in 2009. As the recreational boating community increased, more berths were needed, and the second marina expansion was completed in 2012, replacing the old fuel dock with the 200’ concrete dock, known today as the Service Dock and the additional 150’ cement guest dock. The Breakwater Cove Marina is now at max capacity with 100 berths, varying from 25’, 35’, 50’ and 70’. We are the deepest, open water marina in Monterey, where at our shallowest depth being 6’ inside the marina and 12’ at the fuel dock during zero tide. We have facilities set for vessels up to 200’, with reservations booking two years in advance. Over the years, the Frank Siino Boatyard has slowly transitioned from commercial fishing boats to recreational sailboats and powerboats. Monterey Bay Boatworks and Breakwater Cove Marina have been noted and used as examples of environmentally conscious, safety-oriented businesses with environmental agencies. Maintaining our integrity and commitment to not only the boating community but also our environment, we’ve been able to grow, adapt, and transform with the ever-changing times, thanks to the hard work of past and present staff. With Mike’s dream firmly set in stone with dedicated staff on hand, the Partners became Shareholders in 2021, when the Breakwater Cove Partners Inc. was created, securing the operations management of Monterey Bay Boatworks for continued success. Most recently, we leased our Marine Supply Store and Boatyard departments to Monterey Boat Haven in April of 2025. We trust that they will continue to uphold the same standards set forth by our decades of service to our customers and the environment. After 40 years, there are many Monterey Bay Boatworks stories and memories we all share. Through those stories, Mike's dream will live on, and with the support of our dedicated staff, tenants, and Shareholders, the success of that dream will continue to grow. Thank you to all past, present, and future supporters. We look forward to another 40 years, with new and exciting things in the works! Stay up to date by following us on social media and sign up for our monthly e-newsletter, the Felucca.

Are Jet Skis Scary to Ride for the First Time? Plus, What You Need to Know About Boater's Licenses
Jet skiing is an exhilarating way to explore the stunning waters of the Gulf Coast, but if you're new to it, you might be wondering: “Is riding a jet ski scary?” and “Do I need a boater's license?” At Costa Coast Powersports Jet Ski Rental, we want to make sure you have all the information you need to feel confident and ready before your ride. Here's a closer look at first-time jet ski experiences and the rules regarding boater’s licenses in Florida.
Is Riding a Jet Ski Scary for First-Timers?
For those who have never been on a jet ski, the thought of riding at high speeds over open water may seem intimidating. The good news is that modern jet skis are designed to be user-friendly and are generally safe for beginners. Most first-timers find jet skiing thrilling and enjoyable rather than frightening.
At Costa Coast Powersports, we ensure that every new rider receives a comprehensive safety briefing and hands-on training before heading out on the water. We’ll teach you how to operate the jet ski, steer, accelerate, and brake properly. Plus, you’ll get the opportunity to practice in calm waters before exploring further, which helps build your confidence.
First-Time Rider Tips:
: Begin at a moderate pace to get used to the jet ski’s handling.
: Keep your knees bent and maintain a firm stance to stay steady.
: Tension can make steering more difficult, so try to stay calm and loose.
: Follow the guidance provided by the rental staff for a safer experience.
Boater’s License Requirements in Florida
Florida has specific regulations when it comes to operating jet skis and other personal watercraft (PWC). If you were born on or after January 1, 1988, you are required to have completed a Florida Boating Safety Education Course to operate a jet ski legally. This rule was put into effect in the late 1980s to ensure that watercraft operators are knowledgeable about boating safety and regulations.
If you were born before this date, you are not required by law to have a boater’s license, but taking a safety course is still a good idea. It helps you understand important boating rules, safe practices, and emergency procedures. This can make you a more confident and responsible rider, which is beneficial for your safety and that of others on the water.
How to Obtain a Boater’s License
To comply with the law, you can take an approved Florida Boating Safety Education Course online or in-person. These courses cover essential topics, including navigation rules, emergency safety measures, and responsible watercraft operation. Once you complete the course, you’ll receive a certification card that serves as proof of your boater's safety education.
Our Commitment to Safety and Fun
At Costa Coast Powersports, we’re dedicated to making sure you have an enjoyable and safe experience. We provide high-quality equipment and thorough safety briefings to ensure all our riders, regardless of experience level, feel comfortable and well-prepared. Whether you’re new to jet skiing or a seasoned pro, our team is here to make your adventure unforgettable.

Kenai Drift Anglers offers guided fishing trips on the Kenai River and Kasilof River, home to some of the best salmon fishing in Alaska. Best Times to Fish the Kenai & Kasilof Rivers 2026 Alaska Fishing Season Guide
May 16th Season Opener – Kasilof River King Salmon: The Lower Kasilof River opens for King Salmon fishing, offering an exciting opportunity to hook these powerful fish in a drift-only setting. Fishing in May in Alaska offers a peaceful and tranquil experience, providing a private setting on the river with fewer crowds and pristine natural beauty. It’s the perfect time to enjoy the serenity of the Kenai and Kasilof Rivers, surrounded by stunning landscapes while targeting early-season King Salmon on the Kasilof River.
June – A Hidden Gem for Early Season Fishing: We fish both the Upper Kasilof River near Tustumena Lake and the Lower Kasilof River for the Kasilof Sockeye Salmon Run, which begins in early June. This coincides with the Russian River Sockeye Salmon Run, which kicks off on the Kenai River in Soldotna around the same time. June is a great month of Alaskan fishing, with lighter crowds, great fishing, and a true Alaskan experience before peak crowds arrive.
July – Peak Season & Busiest Month: July is the busiest month of the season, bringing incredible fishing action to both rivers. The Kasilof River remains strong for Sockeye Salmon, while the Kenai River Sockeye Run builds momentum, offering some of the largest Salmon runs of the season.
August – Peak Kenai River Sockeye & Silver Salmon Arrive: Sockeye Salmon fishing is at its best on the Kenai River, with outstanding opportunities for anglers looking to catch limits of these prized fish. Silver Salmon (Coho) also begin to show up, providing exciting fishing that extends into fall.

=== PAGE: https://www.seacrossfishingmiami.com/faqs/
TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) - Sea Cross
Frequently Asked Questions
How many people can I have onboard?
The maximum number of people on any charter is 6. Strict insurance regulations only allow 6 passengers.
What is provided?
We provide all rod, reels, bait, tackle, ice, and fishing licenses
What should I bring for the fishing trip?
We suggest you bring hat or visor, sunglasses, sunscreen and a light jacket. Also bring any food and drink you will consume during your fishing trip. We will provide coolers and ice for your perishables.
Do you customize trips?
Yes, we do offer customization on the departure times and return times.
Can we request to target a specific species of fish?
Yes. Are you looking for that trophy fish or what to target a specific species? Just mention it to us we can customize any trip. All trips are special to us.
Do you offer shared or split charters?
No, we do not offer shared or split charters – just private charters.
We would rather have a more intimate experience on a private boat, is that possible?
Absolutely, chartering a private boat means it will be your group only on the vessel with the crew. You are not sharing the boat with anyone you do not know. And there’s never a chance that you watch someone else catch that trophy fish.
Should I tip the captain and crew?
Tips are discretionary. But like any service business, it is customary to tip the crew 15 -20% if you received good service.
Can I get my fish mounted?
Yes, just ask your mate and we will take care of the entire process. He can also explain everything to you in detail. What a great way to memorialize your trophy catch.
Do I get to keep the fish I catch?
Yes, the fish your party catches are yours. We will cheerfully fillet or steak your catch for you. Don’t forget to bring a cooler if you plan on taking your fish. Lastly, we do NOT ship fish – you will need to make any shipping arrangements yourself.

With the Sea Cross and the Sea Cross II, we boast a pair of new air-conditioned custom rigged Hatteras sportfishing yachts.
The Sea Cross is a fully loaded 55’ Hatteras convertible and Sea Cross II is a fully loaded 45’ Hatteras convertible, each with the latest electronics, direct TV, radar, live well, outriggers, top-of-the-line fishing rods and tackle.
The 55’ Sea Cross is our most luxurious vessel. It was completely rebuilt and refurbished from the keel up in 2022 with all the amenities. It is one of the cleanest and biggest sportfishing yachts available for hire in the Miami area. You will experience a professionally maintained and beautiful fishing machine with ample room for you and all your guests to enjoy a top-notch fishing experience.
With a 20 foot beam, there’s plenty of legroom. And if you want to get out of the sun, we have a spacious salon with plush interior and custom hardwood counters and a full bar. There also the huge flybridge with plenty of room for everyone onboard.
The 45’ Sea Cross II is our workhorse making trips daily to our offshore waters. It’s length and beam make it comfortable for guests and maneuverable when chasing the many species of fish in the area. It’s a perfect choice if visiting south Florida on a family vacation and want to experience Miami from the water.
All our boats meet and exceed all US Coast Guard safety regulations. They are crewed by professional licensed captains with more than 25 years of experience. Both vessels are also equipped with top-of-the-line and tournament grade tackle – all custom-made rods from Biscayne Rods.
Why Hatteras?
Hatteras has a storied history of producing high-quality sport fishing boats. It’s no wonder they’ve been long considered some of the best built and toughest fishing boats on the water.
In the 1960’s Hatteras became one of the first boat builders in the industry to construct their boats from fiberglass. Since then, Hatteras has launched nearly 10,000 fiberglass vessels and earned a reputation as an innovator in the marine industry. Along the way, they have pioneered many groundbreaking technologies that have set the standard by which all others are measured.
This is why we have always trusted Hatteras with the safety and comfort of our guests.

TITLE: Experience Ultimate Freedom on the Water by Captaining Your Own Tritoon Adventure
Imagine a day where the only schedule you follow is the rhythm of the waves beneath your boat. No rush, no stress, just the open water and endless possibilities. This is the freedom you get when you captain your own tritoon boat or choose to relax with a licensed captain while exploring nearby islands. Whether you crave adventure or tranquility, this boating experience offers both with ease and excitement.
The Joy of Captaining Your Own Boat
Taking the helm of a tritoon boat gives you control over your day on the water. Tritoons offer 33% more buoyancy and pontoons. These boats are designed for stability and comfort, making them easy to navigate even for beginners. You need prior boating experience to captain your own vessel; a brief orientation covers everything you need to know.
Why captain your own boat?
Freedom to explore
: Choose your own route and discover hidden coves or favorite spots at your own pace.
Privacy and comfort
: Enjoy the company of friends and family without distractions.
Hands-on adventure
: Feel the thrill of steering and managing your own boat.
The tritoon’s spacious deck and smooth ride make it perfect for socializing, sunbathing, or fishing. You can pack a picnic, bring your favorite music, and create a personalized water adventure.
Relaxing with a Licensed Captain
If you prefer to unwind and soak in the scenery, hiring a licensed captain is the perfect option. A professional captain knows the local waters intimately and can guide you to the best islands, beaches, and snorkeling spots.
Benefits of choosing a captain:
Stress-free experience
: No need to worry about navigation or safety regulations.
Local insights
: Captains often share stories and tips about the area’s history and wildlife.
Focus on relaxation
: Spend your time swimming, sunbathing, or enjoying a meal on board.
This option is ideal for those who want to enjoy the water without any responsibilities. You simply show up and let the captain take care of the rest.
Exploring Local Islands Made Easy
The area around your boating adventure is full of beautiful islands waiting to be explored. Each island offers unique experiences, from quiet beaches to lively spots with local eateries.
Top island activities to consider:
Beachcombing and swimming
: Find a secluded beach to relax or snorkel in clear waters.
Wildlife watching
: Spot birds, dolphins, or manatees in their natural habitat.
Picnicking on shore
: Pack a lunch and enjoy a meal with a view.
Photography
: Capture stunning landscapes and memorable moments.
With your own boat or a captain at the helm, you can tailor your day to include as many or as few stops as you like. The flexibility means you can chase the sun or find shade whenever you want.
What Makes the Tritoon Experience Unique
Tritoon boats stand out because of their design and versatility. Unlike traditional boats, tritoons have three pontoons that provide extra stability and space. This makes them ideal for families, groups, or anyone who values comfort on the water.
Key features of tritoon boats:
Stable and smooth ride

Spacious deck

Easy to operate

Safety features

Domestic abuse is the use, attempted use, or threatened use of force or violence against an intimate partner. It is also a pattern of behavior that results in the emotional abuse, economic control, or interference with personal liberty that is directed towards an intimate partner. An intimate partner is a current or former spouse, a person with whom the abuser shares a child or common domicile, or a person who is in a romantic relationship with the abuser.
Examples of domestic abuse include, but are not limited to, taking your cell phone or keys, not allowing you to leave a location, controlling what you wear or who you speak to, limiting your access to money, name calling, pushing, hitting, or sexual contact without your consent.

Everyone’s situation is different — domestic abuse can happen to anyone and it’s not their fault. And it can be difficult to know how to help a friend, coworker or loved one who is in an abusive relationship. Here are five simple things you can do to safely help someone you care about in their time of need.
“How do you prefer we connect?” Having a safe way to communicate is important. Let your friend or loved one tell you what is safest for them and honor that. Do not pressure the person to leave. Instead, support them without judgment. Offer to help them plan for their safety or seek outside support when they are ready.
“Let’s play a game online.” Finding creative reasons to call, text, video chat or use social media check-ins may provide a lifeline for those who feel unsafe at home. For example, some games have chat functions that may allow for communication in nontraditional spaces. Starting up a game that has chat may allow you to check in with your friend without making the abuser suspicious. Learn about privacy and safety tips for technology from the National Network to End Domestic Violence at .

Professional Services: Banking, Audit, and Credit Card Processing Services Feasibility Studies Employee Development Training Consultant Services Instructors
These goods and services are purchased for our Marine Corps Exchanges, clubs, lodging facilities, recreation activities and warehouse facilities. We also contract with nationally recognized companies for fast food operations, money transfer services, and film processing, to name a few.
Our non-resale procurement professionals may also order against other NAFI and Federal Government contracts, such as those issued by the General Services Administration and Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Purchasing Office (AFNAFPO).
It is our policy that procurement using nonappropriated funds be accomplished primarily through competition in a fair, equitable, and impartial manner, and to the best advantage of the MCCS. MCCS contracting is entitled to the same tax exemptions and adheres to the same tax regulations as other Federal agencies. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does not apply to non-appropriated fund procurements, except when specifically required by DoD Directive, Instruction, or Component regulations.

About Development Cost Charges
Development Coast Charges (DCCs) are fees collected by local governments to help fund the cost of growth-related infrastructure expenditures. DCCs are regulated by the . The rates charged reﬂect the impact growth has on infrastructure, parks, and eligible protective services; the greater the impact, the larger the charge. This helps ensure development contributes its fair share towards the necessary growth-related infrastructure improvements that development benefits from.
DCCs help offset the cost of providing new infrastructure related to development. For example, they help build sewers, watermains, drainage, and roads.

One Water Strategy
In September 2023, the Town of Gibsons and the Sunshine Coast Regional District entered into the . As part of that agreement, both parties committed to completing an Engineering Support Project to build greater resiliency in the interconnection between the Town and SCRD water distribution systems.

TITLE: Corporate Climate Action Plan - Town of Gibsons
Corporate Climate Action Plan
The Town of Gibsons was one of the first communities to adopt its Community Energy and Emissions Plan (CEEP) in 2010 to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and create a complete, compact and energy-efficient community, as part of its commitment to the B.C. Climate Action Charter. As a signatory to the Charter, the Town has also committed to reducing emissions and becoming carbon neutral in its own operations. This Corporate Energy and Emissions Plan will provide Council and staff with background information to reduce emissions and develop strategic priorities for the next five years (2024-2029).
Leading by example with its own assets, helping stimulate further GHG emission reductions in the community
Reducing local government energy costs, i.e. providing better value for money to taxpayers
Providing a more comfortable working environment for staff and a healthier indoor environment for visitors
Community economic development by leveraging external funding into projects in the community
Improved climate change resilience”
Based on staff consultation and best practices, actions were identified to be implemented over the next five years. Actions fall under the following five categories.
Existing Buildings and Infrastructure: Improve energy performance and lower GHG emissions in existing Town buildings and infrastructure
New Buildings and Infrastructure: Improve energy performance and lower GHG emissions in new Town buildings and infrastructure, including renovated spaces
Renewable Energy: Increase the use of renewable energy
Transportation: Switch to clean/renewable fuels and reduce GHG emissions in the Town’s fleet and the contractors’ fleet
Enabling Actions and Corporate Leadership: Institutionalize the plan and demonstrate leadership

TITLE: Tandem Skydiving FAQs | Go Skydive Nashville
Have a question not answered here? Give us a call or .
send us an email
Go Skydive Nashville Facilities
Where is Go Skydive Nashville located?
We operate out of the John C. Tune (JWN) general aviation airport, about a 10-minute drive from central Nashville. The address is .
220 Tune Airport Drive, Suite 120, Nashville, TN 37209
Where do I go when I arrive?
Follow the signs for Go Skydive Nashville and you’ll be guided by our Manifest (front desk) staff upon check-in. You’ll complete paperwork, ground training, and meet your instructor at our office. Once cleared for your skydive, we’ll escort you through airport security and gate operations.
Is there parking?
Parking is free but limited at JWN. If you’re bringing a friend or skydiving with a group, please carpool and limit vehicles to one per group.
Where are we flying and where do we land?
It’s a short flight up, over the airport, to reach altitude (14,000 feet). The landing spot is just off the airport property. will drive you back to the airport after your skydive.
Our team
Can solo skydivers jump at Go Skydive Nashville?
No, sorry. We are a only facility.
tandem
Is Go Skydive Nashville a member of the United States Parachute Association?
Yes, we are a proud to be a United States Parachute Association Group Member (USPA) dropzone.
FIRST-TIME EXPERIENCE
I noticed that there is a small booking fee. What’s it for?
The booking fee is charged by the airport, similar to the airport and TSA fees you see when booking a commercial airline ticket. We’ve worked closely with the airport to keep these fees as low as possible, and we include them upfront so there are no hidden charges or surprises when you check out. We believe in being transparent, so you’ll always know exactly what you’re paying before you arrive.
Comfort and practicality are important when choosing your skydive attire. If it’s a hot day when you step outside, you’ll be fine with lightweight pants and a T-shirt in the air but a thin extra layer won’t hurt. In the fall, spring, and on chilly days, we recommend warmer attire, particularly layers, leggings, or form-fitting athletic clothing. Avoid boots, flip-flops, loose accessories, and any clothing that is bulky or features excess material, like a hood. Please choose jeans or clothing you don’t mind getting dirty.
Should I eat/drink before skydiving?
Nourishing yourself is an important part of ! Eat a normal breakfast or lunch on the day of your jump. Don’t eat quantities much larger than your usual amount and avoid extremely greasy food or items loaded with dairy. Drink plenty of water the night before and in the days before your experience. You cannot consume alcohol on the day of your jump and we strongly urge you to avoid it the night before (hangovers at 14,000 feet suck, quite honestly). A small amount of coffee or caffeine is fine before you skydive but too much can make you feel extra jittery combined with nervous energy and anticipation.
preparing for your skydive
Who or what should I bring?
Bring your driver’s license, passport, or government-issued ID. You can bring spectators, friends, or family (they’ll stay on the ground and watch). Don’t bring pets. Feel free to bring a light snack and your water bottle for a quick fuel-up as we prep your flight and parachute (or for right after your jump). Personal items like purses, phones, keys, etc., all stay in a secure location before you board the aircraft. You can’t take a camera or wear a device for video/photos during your jump – but we’ll have you covered with an documenting your experience.
experienced skydiving photographer
When should I arrive?
Please arrive 30 minutes before your reservation time. Depending on the weather and other logistics, your time at Go Skydive Nashville could last up to four or five hours on the day of your jump. At check-in, you’ll complete paperwork before undergoing some ground training. You’ll meet with your instructor – the professional you’re attached to during the jump – who will go over your gear and walk you through what to expect before hopping on our aircraft.
Is there a weight limit?
Yes. For the tandem skydiving equipment we use, . This is not intended to be a barrier or discriminatory but relates to manufacturing guidelines from the makers of our skydiving equipment. In addition, .
Are there any other fees?
Fuel prices around the globe rise and fall often. When they rise significantly, we may institute a temporary fuel fee to offset the difference. While only a small amount, this helps ensure we keep skydiving prices as low as possible for all to enjoy.
SKYDIVING 101
Is there a minimum age for tandem skydiving?
Skydivers must be , and a government-issued ID is required at check-in.
How long am I in the air?
After the plane ride to altitude, less than 10 minutes! And most of that is a gentle, scenic parachute ride. You’ll be shocked at how much adrenaline, exhilaration, and awe is packed into a 35-second freefall. Because you’re moving fast (120 miles per hour fast) the jump from the plane before the parachute deploys is relatively quick. The plane ride up is about 15 minutes.
Do parachutes open every time?
If you’re worried about , keep a few things in mind about parachutes. For starters, parachutes are packed at Go Skydive Nashville with multiple redundancies and our professionals are trained in emergency protocols. In the unlikely event the main parachute malfunctions or there’s a problem, the instructor will deploy the backup or reserve parachute. Both the reserve and main canopy are handled by specially trained riggers. Reserve canopies, as they are used far less often, are inspected and repacked every 180 days by a rigger approved and rated by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. The reserve canopy is there in case the main parachute is inoperable. The most recent reporting by the United States Parachute Association found that 12% of the members it surveyed (professional jumpers, dropzone instructors, etc.) had used their reserve canopy in a 12-month period.
staying safe
Is skydiving safe?
Skydiving is an extreme sport and just like other physical activities, there’s some inherent risk. At our dropzone, we prioritize training, methodical safety checks, and employing the best equipment and staff available. Nationwide, interest in skydiving among professionals and first-time jumpers has increased steadily since the early 2000s. In that timeframe, the rate of skydiving deaths (fatalities per 100,000 jumps) has steadily declined, . In 2023, for example, a total of 10 skydiving deaths were reported in the U.S. – a record low since official data-keeping started in 1961.
according to U.S. Parachute Association data
What’s the airplane like?
Go Skydive Nashville flies a Cessna 182 Skylane, which is a single-engine light aircraft perfect for the short flight to altitude for your jump.
PHOTOS WHILE SKYDIVING
Can I take photos while skydiving?
Sorry, no. We follow the U.S. Parachute Association’s mandate that restricts the use of photography equipment by non-instructors or experienced jumpers. The only skydivers permitted to use a camera in the skies are those with at least 200 jumps under their harness. But we know documenting your skydive is important! That’s why we provide professional photography. More details are below and on our tandem page. Take all the photos you want on the ground!
skydiving media package
Can I buy photos and video of my jump?
We’ve got you! Your instructor will use a hand-cam to capture every thrilling second of your skydiving experience. Our media package includes photos of you skydiving – smile for the camera! – as well as video footage, which will be emailed to you soon after your jump. Check out our page for pricing information.
media package
Are group skydiving photos possible?

Wildlife & Habitat
Scarborough Marsh provides critical habitat for a broad array of wildlife, particularly birds. Waterfowl, egrets, herons, Glossy Ibis and many species of shorebirds depend on this rich ecosystem for food, a place to rest during migration, and nesting habitat. The marsh is also an excellent spot to find a number of grassland songbirds not commonly found in other parts of Maine, as well as various birds of prey that hunt in the marsh throughout the year. Muskrat, mink, otter, and deer also frequent the wetland.
Download our guide to
“What you can see in a salt marsh: Wildlife”
and
“What you can see in a salt marsh: Plants”.
For a virtual tour of a salt marsh and detailed guides to the plants and wildlife you’ll find there, visit Robert Zottoli’s excellent
Field Trip to a New England Salt Marsh
In 2021, Scarborough Marsh Audubon Center Intern Laura Bither created and authored this project on climate change and sea level rise at the marsh. By focusing on the stories of youth and fisherfolk–those typically left unheard in the environmental movement–she centered on the challenges Maine coastal communities face and their visions for a climate-resilient future.
History
Scarborough Marsh has a long history of human use. Indigenous people hunted, trapped, clammed, and fished on the wetland. When European settlers arrived in the 1600s, they harvested the salt hay as fodder for cattle and sheep and used the marsh as summer pasture. The 19th century saw increased ditching, filling of pannes, and the introduction of tidal gates, which prevent the tide from flooding portions of the marsh. Channels were dug to allow boats built inland to float through the marsh out to sea.
When haying declined in the 1900s, people began to view marshes as sacrifice areas for airports or cheap space on which to fill and build. Scarborough Marsh was even proposed as a site for the town dump. Recognizing that a significant coastal wildlife habitat was threatened, in 1957 the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife began the twenty-year process of acquiring the marsh. In 1972, Maine Audubon initiated a partnership with the state to convert into a nature center an old clam shack at the edge of the marsh.
Today, Scarborough Marsh is a workplace for clam diggers, a classroom for schoolchildren, a laboratory for biologists, prime territory for fishermen and hunters, and a fascinating, ever-changing world for naturalists, especially birders. Every spring and summer, more than 10,000 people begin their journey into the marsh at Scarborough Marsh Audubon Center.

In Memoriam
In June 2024, Love Catalina Island Tourism Authority’s past President and CEO passed away, leaving a 27-year legacy on the organization, Catalina Island, and California tourism industry. A remarkable leader, Wayne co-ran the family seafood restaurant for 10 years before he took over as (now Love Catalina Island) where he served for nearly . Wayne and his wife Susie, along with business partner Marlene McAdam, , which went on to become one of the most successful B&B’s in the U.S., earning multiple awards, including the prestigious 4-Star Forbes Award. Wayne served as a member of the WACVB (now DMA West) for 20 years, and he served as from 2001-2002. Wayne also taught classes at the Western Institute for Organization Management, a professional development program run by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. When the U.S. Chamber discontinued the program, Wayne co-founded a new program through , which launched in 2003 as Academy. Wayne taught at WACE Academy for many years, and the program is still thriving today. In 2008, Wayne served as chair of the board of WACE and was later awarded WACE’s Russell E. Pettit Excellence in Leadership Award.
Of note is his long-time membership in the , where he served two terms as president; his membership on the and ; and his regular performances in community theater, especially musicals. By far Wayne’s greatest contribution of service to his island community was at , where he served as organist and cantor for 30 years. When Wayne & Susie retired in 2014, the Catalina Island Chamber of Commerce and Visitors Bureau awarded them the inaugural . The legacy of community service is honored by Love Catalina with the Wayne & Susie Griffin award which is made when an individual or family on Catalina demonstrates exceptional commitment to service. Wayne will be remembered for his leadership and unwavering optimism, as a business and community leader, a civil servant, and a family man who put his wife, children and grandchildren above all else. Most importantly, Wayne will be remembered for his laugh.
