Customers are responsible for the original reservation made. Changes made due to late arrival will not affect the overall price of the rental. Customers are entitled to a full refund given the following situations: Due to unavoidable weather-related conditions. If issues arise beyond our control such as unforeseen mechanical or electrical problems.
Q. Are food and beverages available for my trip? A. Customers are welcome to bring food and drinks, coolers are provided by request. All items brought onboard must leave you at the end of your rental.

=== PAGE: https://goparasailing.com/how-to-prevent-sea-sickness/
TITLE: 9 Proven Ways to Prevent Seasickness (Feel Better Fast)
Are you planning a boat ride or a water activity, but are afraid of getting sick? You’ve come to the right place.
Sea sickness is very common. It happens when your brain gets mixed signals from motion at sea, but the good news is that this problem is very preventable by taking the proper steps before and during your ride.
If you are planning parasailing with
or a boat-based adventure, especially on a smaller boat, this guide is written exactly for you.
Before learning about the tips to prevent sea-sickness, let’s understand why it hits some people so fast.
Some people are quite sensitive to motion. Their inner ear senses motion, and their eyes see something else. Their brain does not like that argument and responds with nausea, dizziness, and cold sweats.
This disagreement gets worse during sickness on a small boat because the motion is quicker and more uneven. Short waves, sudden turns, and engine vibration all add fuel to the fire.
Sea sickness can ruin your entire vacation if not treated. Here are some proven ways that will help you prevent sea sickness when doing any water activities or rides:
Where you sit on the boat matters more than most people realize.
The middle of the boat feels the least motion as it is closer to the center, where the boat is more balanced. If you can, try picking a seat near the middle and sit facing forward.
A few quick tips that help here:
Avoid sitting at the very back, where engine movement is strongest
Skip the front when waves are choppy
Stay seated instead of walking around the boat too much
This single choice can cut symptoms in half for many people.
Your eyes are powerful allies when it comes to balance. When you look at a fixed point like the horizon, your brain gets a clear message about motion.
Staring at your phone or camera can make things worse fast. We have seen people turn green within minutes while scrolling through photos on deck.
Instead:
Look out at the water line
Keep your head steady
Avoid reading or texting
It feels simple, but it works because it fixes the brain confusion at the root.
Many people don’t eat before a boat ride. But that is just as bad as eating too much. The sweet spot is light and simple food about one hour before boarding.
Greasy breakfast burritos and sugary pastries are a bad idea. So is skipping food entirely.
Better options include:
Toast or crackers
Fruits like bananas or apples
Oatmeal or yogurt
Keep yourself hydrated. Water is good, but alcohol is not. Even one drink can lower your tolerance to motion and turn a fun trip into a long hour of regret.
If you already know boats make you sick, medication can be a smart move. Over-the-counter options to prevent seasickness like
are widely used in the US.
The key is timing. These work best when taken before symptoms start. Once nausea hits, they help less.
Important things to remember:
A good time to take medicine is 30 to 60 minutes before the ride.
Expect possible drowsiness
Don’t mix it with alcohol
Remember to follow the label and check with a doctor if you have health conditions.
Not everyone wants pills, and that is fine. Some natural options have real backing and years of sailor use.
Ginger is one of the most effective remedies that works for most who suffer from sea sickness. It helps in calming the stomach and reducing nausea.
Other options include:
Ginger tea or capsules
Peppermint candy
Acupressure wrist bands
Results vary by person, but these are low-risk and easy to try.
What you wear can make sickness on a small boat worse or better. Tight clothing, heavy jackets, and overheating all increase nausea. These tend to restrict your movement internally and externally.
The best thing to do is dress in layers. Fresh air helps a lot, especially if you start feeling off.
Helpful clothing tips:
Go for breathable clothing options and fabrics
Don’t wear tight waistbands
Wear sunglasses to reduce eye strain
Standing in fresh air beats sitting in a stuffy cabin every time. This is one of the best things about parasailing with
, as their boats are open and give enough air to breathe during the boat ride
Sun, wind, and salt air dry you out even if you do not feel sweaty. The best way to tackle this is by keeping yourself hydrated at all times. By that, we don’t mean for you to drink gallons of water at once.
Small sips of water during the ride help keep your body steady. Gulping large amounts can backfire, so go slow.
Avoid:
Soda
Energy drinks
Strong coffee
Plain water or light electrolyte drinks are best.
Boat crews
like those at San Diego Parasail Adventures see seasickness every day. They know the signs before you do. If you feel even slightly off, tell them.
They can:
Adjust speed when possible
Suggest a better seat
Help you focus on breathing
Trying to tough it out quietly often makes things worse. There is no badge of honor for feeling awful on vacation.
This sounds almost too simple, but controlled breathing can calm nausea. When waves hit, people tend to tense up and breathe shallowly.
Slow breathing sends a calming signal to your nervous system. It reduces panic and helps your stomach settle.
You can try this instead:
Inhale through your nose for four seconds
Exhale through your mouth for six seconds
Repeat for a few minutes
It is discreet, free, and surprisingly effective.
This is a common worry, and it is a fair one. Parasailing itself is smooth once you are in the air. Most discomfort happens during the boat ride before and after.
That is why knowing how to prevent sea sickness before boarding matters so much. The flight part feels calm and peaceful for most people. The boat ride is the part to prepare for.
If you follow the steps above, especially seating and food choices, most first-timers do just fine.
Many people just get scared before and cancel amazing experiences out of fear. But with planning, even people who get sick on a small boat can enjoy water activities.
The key is being honest with yourself and preparing ahead of time. Think about:
What triggers your nausea
The preventive measures you take
Whether you’re comfortable communicating with the crew about this
If the answer is yes, the odds are strongly in your favor.
Follow the Measures and Have An Amazing Sea Experience
At the end of the day, the ocean should feel exciting, not intimidating. There’s a lot to do in the ocean and you wouldn’t want to ruin it by not taking preventive measures. But with the right prep, you can step onto the boat confident, relaxed, and focused on the experience instead of your stomach.

We have a best price policy: if you find a better price in another Squamish kiteboarding school for the same product or service, we will beat it. Our boats are the newest and largest in the Howe Sound and we also provide you with high quality kite equipment and cold water gear. We believe that all students should experience the best gear available for their skill level. We have a highly qualified instructor team. In fact, we are proud to employ 3 certified level 2 instructors out of less than 200 in the world! We want to make your kiteboarding learning experience easier: On the practical side, launching from our boats spares you the long bumpy spit road and allows you enjoy launching from the water instead of the crowded Squamish Spit. We also consider catering our lessons to each student as highly important since we want to make kiteboarding a sport as inclusive as possible. For instance, we are glad to have initiated the Kiteboarding and Adventure Youth Camp and to have founded Adaptive Kiteboarding Canada with the help of our instructors.
After you have purchased your lesson, you can complete your booking online at
www.squamishwatersportsbookings.com
. Once you submit your booking, Aerial Kiteboarding will get back to you via email within 48 hours to confirm your Squamish Kiteboarding lesson.
If you are interested in purchasing a lesson with Aerial Kiteboarding in Squamish, BC, you can do so with a credit card or paypal account directly through aerialkiteboarding.com or any associated website. If you are not sure what lesson program is best for you, give us a call at our toll free number 1-855-5MY-KITE or email us at aerialkiteboarding@gmail.com and we would be happy to guide you through your decision.
Yes and No. Kiteboarding is a very technical sport and with the proper instruction, you could be riding within your first few lessons in Squamish, BC Canada. Naturally, there will be some frustrating patches, such is when you are faced with a difficult new task. Kiteboarding is a progressional sport, and as a Kiteboarder, you will always get better and learn new things every session.
Learning on your own can be dangerous and impossible at the Squamish Spit, Squamish, BC. Learning the proper kite skills and the many safety features of the kites will allow you to kiteboard safely. In addition, teaching yourself can be frustrating and often leads to bad habits. Self-taught riders often damage their kites while learning and, as a result, spend more money in the long run then they would on lessons. Lastly, there are many different kite companies, however few produce quality performance kites. Having the opportunity to spend time with an experiences rider and Aerial Kiteboarding instructor in Squamish, BC, will provide you with better knowledge about kiteboarding equipment as well.
Our Squamish office is open from 10am to 6pm from the May 1st to September 30th. We are also available by appointment from 8am to 10pm year around. Our water lesson run from 9am to 9pm (weather dependent) from March to November. Throughout the year, Aerial Kiteboarding School & Shop does run lessons and camps abroad so we ensure that we are available for any questions or inquiries via email.
All summer lessons are held in Squamish, BC Canada. Aerial Kiteboarding runs lessons from our downtown location, located at 37813 2 Ave, Squamish, BC. Once suited up and ready to go, we walk 1 block to our boat launch, and head out onto the water. We will launch your kite from our boats in the Howe Sound, or from a sand bar if the tide is low. Lessons can also take place from our secondary location at the Squamish Spit from May 15th to September 15th by request.
For all lessons purchased directly through us and starting from our downtown location, there is no additional fees and all gear rentals are included. If your lesson needs to be cancelled at any point due to wind, we will invite you back to complete your lesson at another time.
Lessons must be cancelled or rescheduled at least 48 hours prior to your lesson or your lesson may be voided. Since kiteboarding is a wind dependent sport, we are limited to the hours in the day where Mother Nature provides us with sufficient wind. FAQ’s
Do I need a fishing License?
Anyone 16 years of age or older will need to purchase a fishing license.
licenses can be easily purchased online through the , your smartphone, and also at local bait and tackle stores.
Ohio ODNR licensing website
What Should we bring on the Charter?
You will want to bring appropriate clothing, *snacks, beverages, a fishing license (if required) and Dramamine (if you get seasick)

Will we share a charter with others?
No, the charter is reserved for one reservation at a time.
Is alcohol allowed?
Yes, alcohol is allowed on the boat. However, glass containers are not allowed.
How many people can come onboard?
Our charter can hold up to 6 people.
Is smoking allowed?
Yes, the use of tobacco is permitted. Remember that this is a drug-free vessel so illegal drugs will not be permitted.
What if bad weather hits the day I scheduled the charter?
We will communicate with you if cancellations are necessary.
What if I need to use the restroom?
Our charter comes equipped with a fully functioning and private toilet.
Is there an age limit for guests?
We believe fishing is a great sport for all ages! There is no age limit but it is a good idea to use your judgment in deciding who should come and if they can handle 7 hours on a water vessel.

TITLE: Smallmouth Bass Fishing Charters on Lake Erie near Port Clinton, Ohio | Champion Charters
Smallmouth Bass Charters on Lake Erie
Ready for a freshwater smallmouth bass fishing adventure on Lake Erie near Port Clinton, Ohio?
Smallmouth Bass Fishing Charters in Port Clinton, Ohio
Get ready for an exciting freshwater small mouth bass fishing adventure with Champion Charters on Lake Erie, one of the most highly-regarded smallmouth bass fisheries in the nation. Departing from Anchors Away Marina in Lakeside Marblehead, our charters are ideally positioned for anglers visiting Port Clinton, Ohio and surrounding communities.
Lake Erie smallmouth bass are known for their spirited fights and strong leaps, making them a favorite sportfish for anglers of all skill levels. The Western Basin’s rocky reefs, islands, and submerged structure provide excellent habitat — and when you book a charter with us, you’ll have access to these prime smallmouth hotspots with an experienced local Fishing Guide / Captain at the helm.
When to Fish for Smallmouth Bass
Smallmouth bass fishing on Lake Erie is productive from May through October, with peak action often occurring in summer and early fall when fish roam rocky points, reef edges, and drop-offs searching for gobies and other prey. Typical catches range from about 14–20 inches, with a chance at larger trophy-class fish thanks to Lake Erie’s healthy bass population.
Charter Experience & What to Expect
Expert local guides familiar with seasonal smallmouth behavior
All tackle, rods, reels, and bait provided (live bait options available)
Family-friendly trips ideal for both newcomers and seasoned anglers
Coaching on techniques like jigging, tube baits, and casting structure
Whether you’re chasing hard-fighting smallies or just enjoying a day on the water, our charters provide an unforgettable Lake Erie fishing experience. Book your smallmouth bass charter today — perfect for visitors from Port Clinton, Marblehead, Sandusky, and northern Ohio looking to hook into one of the most exciting freshwater gamefish in the Midwest.
You will want to bring appropriate clothing, snacks, beverages (unless you do an executive charter which includes food and beverage), a valid Ohio fishing license and Dramamine (if you get seasick).
Your Captain will provide all the necessary smallmouth bass fishing equipment.
Can I keep my catch of the day?
Due to the small mouth numbers and table fair quality, we strongly recommend NOT keeping your catch unless its a trophy fish that you wish to get mounted.

TITLE: Perch Fishing Charters in Port Clinton & Lakeside Marblehead, OH | Champion Charters
Lake Erie Perch Fishing Charters
Book your next perch fishing charter near Port Clinton, Ohio with Champion Charters!
Perch Fishing Charters in Port Clinton, Ohio
Join us for an exciting Lake Erie adventure targeting one of the lake’s most delicious species — yellow perch. Departing from in Lakeside Marblehead, our perch charters give anglers of all skill levels an unforgettable fishing experience on one of the nation’s most productive freshwater fisheries.
Perch Season and Locations
Lake Erie’s yellow perch fishery is a favorite for anglers during late summer through fall — typically from July 1 through October 31 — when schools of perch move into shallower waters near the Western Basin. This timing aligns perfectly with our Anchors Away Marina departure point in Lakeside Marblehead, Ohio 43440, making it ideal for day trips from Port Clinton, OH, Marblehead, OH, and surrounding communities.
During this prime perch season, Lake Erie charters often locate concentrated schools of perch that can result in limit catches. Anglers frequently use spreader rigs baited with emerald shiners or minnows, which can produce multiple catches on the same line — especially when fish are actively feeding.
What Makes Perch Fishing Special
Yellow perch are prized for their delicate, mild flavor, making them one of the most sought-after freshwater catches. Perch typically range from about 8 to 12 inches, with anglers catching their daily limits (which can be up to 30 perch per person depending on Ohio regulations).
Whether you’re a family looking for a fun day on the water or an experienced angler chasing high-action perch bites, our charters provide:
Expert local guides familiar with Lake Erie perch hotspots
All rods, reels, bait, and tackle included
Family-friendly charter experience
Flexible scheduling and custom trip options
Departures change seasonally, starting from Anchors Away Marina in Lakeside Marblehead, giving you the best perch fishing opportunities throughout the season.

Don’t miss out on one of the Midwest’s premier perch fishing adventures. Whether you’re visiting from Port Clinton, Ohio, or nearby Lakeside Marblehead and Oak Harbor, Champion Charters delivers high-quality perch fishing excursions that make for memorable days on Lake Erie.

TITLE: Guided Fishing Charters & Experienced Fishing Charter Captains Lakeside, OH | Champion Charters
Our Fishing Charter Boat Captains
Jim Cramer
Captain Jim started fishing on Lake Erie as a young man; primarily for walleye and perch. His love of fishing led to obtaining his USCG 50 ton Masters Captains License in 2015 and he is also a licensed Lake Erie Fishing Guide. After finding the perfect boat, he began Champion Charters and added a second boat in 2022. He believes in doing everything right every time and that attention to detail makes all the difference. He is passionate about not only catching fish; but having fun doing it.
Luke Cramer
Champion Charters business was named after Captain Luke and his brother Captain Jake; both were outstanding high school and NCAA collegiate wrestlers obtaining state champion and NCAA champion titles. Captain Luke began fishing on Lake Erie as a young boy with his father Captain Jim Cramer. He began first mating at the age of 12 and continued until obtaining his Captains license at the age of 18. He has been a full time Captain for 9 years, winning the Demeter’s Captains tournament on Lake Erie in 2021. He is one of the best fishing guides on Lake Erie. Now a Registered Nurse, he divides his time between the lake and the hospital.
Dakota Siefke
Captain Dakota grew up fishing Lake Erie with his grandfather. His sport fishing journey began 3 years ago as a full time First Mate working for Champion Charters. In 2022 he obtained his own 25 ton Masters Captains License and is a licensed Lake Erie Fishing Guide. He is very knowledgeable of the Western Basin and many different fishing tactics specific to Lake Erie.
Don McCullough
Captain Don, who has a 25 ton USCG Masters Captains license and is a licensed Lake Erie Fishing Guide, grew up in Northwest Ohio and has been boating and fishing his entire life. Don spent 4 years in the United States Navy, spending most of that time in the Pacific and Indian Oceans, and is also an avid licensed diver. Most of his fishing experience has been devoted to yellow perch and walleye here on Lake Erie. (Back in the day when yellow perch were plentiful right off shore and walleye were caught primarily with Erie Dearie lures.) Although times have changed and bait and tactics have modernized; Don is always looking forward to what another day of fishing and being on the water brings.
Trent Lee
Captain Trent has fished Lake Erie since he was a young lad and has professionally tournament fished many lakes and waterways across the U.S. since 2000. He successfully competed in tournaments with the Lake Erie Walleye Tour (LEWT), FLW Tour, Masters Walleye Tour, and Michigan Walleye Tour. This experience has helped him develop a great deal of knowledge about the greatest walleye, perch and small mouth fisheries in the U.S. This is Captain Trent’s third year of being a Charter boat Captain on Lake Erie.

TITLE: Custom Fishing Charter Trips & Lodging Marblehead, OH | Champion Charters
Charter Trips & Lodging
Everyone who books a fishing charter wants to have a good experience and catch fish. At Champion Charters, we understand that a “good” experience is different for different types of people. Below, you can explore the different charter services we offer. Whether you are an avid fisherman, business executive, or a family looking for a day of fun, you will find a charter that is just right for you!
Standard
Affordable and Fun
Those looking for a fun day out on the water can do so with our standard trip. This is a great charter for families and those who just want to enjoy a day of fishing.
Executive
All Inclusive, Great for Parties and Business
Our Executive trip is great for companies who want to take out a client, have a small company retreat or just reward employees with a day out of the office. Many families also choose this trip as it is all inclusive, meaning we take care of everything needed for the day. In addition to all fishing supplies; food and beverages for the day are provided as well as fish cleaning at the end of the day.
Custom
We have coordinated many custom charter trips that have included time spent on Put- in- Bay and Kellys Island. Another option is combo fishing trips where we fish for two species of fish on the same day (walleye, perch, or bass). We have also fished in Canadian waters, and this requires special planning and fishing licenses. Discuss with Captain Jim to create your best day on the Lake. Time and prices will vary
Lodging
Lodging is limited so it may be available upon request. For more details or to reserve lodging for your charter experience, contact us. Captain Jim will do everything he can to assist you with a comfortable stay.

TITLE: FAQ – Slide n Glide
FAQ
We recommend bringing a valid ID, a credit card for the rental deposit, sunscreen, a swimsuit, a towel, and sunglasses. Water shoes or sandals are also a good idea.
Yes, a security deposit is required for all jet ski rentals. The deposit amount will be held on your credit card and released upon the safe return of the equipment.
Are life jackets provided?
Yes, life jackets are provided and must be worn at all times while on the jet ski. Safety is our top priority.
Can I bring a passenger on the jet ski?
Yes, most of our jet skis can accommodate one passenger in addition to the driver. Please check the specific jet ski model for passenger capacity.
What is the rental process?
Book Your Jet Ski: Reserve your jet ski online or by phone.
Check-In: Arrive at our location 30 minutes before your scheduled rental time for check-in and the safety briefing.
Enjoy Your Ride: Head out on the water for your rental period.
Return: Bring the jet ski back on time and check out with our staff.
What if the weather is bad on the day of my rental?
Safety is our priority. If the weather conditions are deemed unsafe for jet skiing, we will work with you to reschedule your rental or provide a full refund.
Can I cancel or reschedule my reservation?
Customers will receive store credit for the amount paid with a 24 hour notice of cancellation. This will be used to rebook your experience for a future date, subject to availability. Customers will also receive a full store credit in case of operator cancellation due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances. No-shows will be charged the full price.
Do you offer guided tours?
Yes, we offer guided tours led by our experienced guides. These tours are a great way to explore the area, learn about local landmarks, and enjoy a structured adventure.
Need more help?
Have a question or need more information? Click on button below and fill the form on Contact page, and a member of our team will get back to you shortly.

=== PAGE: https://slidenglide407.com/safety-checklist/
TITLE: Safety Checklist – Slide n Glide
What to Do If a Jet Ski Is Capsized
​Go to the side rear of Jet Ski, use one hand to press down on edge using all of your weight, use other hand to pull metal bars in your direction until Jet Ski is flipped back over.
Swim to the rear of Jet Ski, use the pull down ladder to climb back on.
Never get on Jet Ski from the side, use only the rear.
2 people (combined weight must not exceed 380 lbs). Riders must be physically capable of lifting their own body weight in the event of falling off the Jet Ski.

Politique de cookies de la Marina du Vieux‑Beloeil
15 mai 2025 citoyens et résidents légaux du Canada
1. Introduction
Le site web de la Marina du Vieux‑Beloeil (ci‑après « le site ») utilise des cookies et technologies similaires pour améliorer votre expérience de navigation. Des cookies peuvent également être déposés par des prestataires tiers. Nous vous expliquons ci‑dessous le rôle de ces cookies et la manière de les contrôler.
2. Que sont les cookies ?
Un cookie est un petit fichier texte déposé sur votre appareil (ordinateur, mobile, tablette) par votre navigateur lorsque vous consultez un site. Il stocke des informations renvoyées ensuite aux serveurs du site ou de tiers.
3. Que sont les scripts ?
Un script est un fragment de code utilisé pour faire fonctionner notre site de façon interactive. Il peut être exécuté sur notre serveur ou directement dans votre navigateur.
4. Qu’est‑ce qu’une balise invisible ?
Une balise invisible (ou « web beacon ») est un petit élément (texte ou image invisible) inséré dans une page web pour suivre le trafic et collecter certaines données de navigation.
5. Prestataires tiers
Nous faisons appel à des fournisseurs externes pour certains services (cartes, polices, statistique, etc.). Ces tiers peuvent déposer et lire leurs propres cookies. Nous n’avons pas le contrôle sur leurs pratiques ; nous vous invitons à consulter leurs propres politiques de confidentialité.
6. Catégories de cookies utilisés
6.1 Cookies strictement nécessaires / fonctionnels
Essentiels pour le bon fonctionnement de certaines fonctionnalités (préférences de langue, formulaire de réservation, rester connecté·e, etc.). Sans ces cookies, certaines sections du site peuvent être inaccessibles ou dysfonctionner.
6.2 Cookies de performance / statistiques
Permettent de collecter des informations anonymes sur la façon dont les visiteurs utilisent le site (pages visitées, durée, origine du trafic) afin d’optimiser l’expérience utilisateur.
6.3 Cookies de marketing / suivi
Utilisés pour créer des profils de navigation et proposer des publicités ou promotions ciblées, sur notre site ou sur d’autres sites.
6.4 Cookies de réseaux sociaux
Intègrent des contenus issus de plateformes (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) pour permettre le partage ou l’affichage de nos flux sociaux. Ces cookies peuvent stocker et traiter certaines données à des fins publicitaires et analytiques.

If you've been reading through our website you've probably figured that we're very transparent about what we offer. There's times of year that we can offer some epic fishing and experiences. Summer months are the trickiest of our year, the reason being is that river levels aren't always optimal. The summer heat in BC melts the snow pack and that drains into the rivers. Early December - late February
Winter Fly Fishing in BC
Winter fly fishing in Squamish runs through December, January, and February. We spend these months offering guided trips on the Squamish and Cheakamus rivers targeting wild bull trout native to the Pacific Northwest. Whether it's a day off from skiing or you just need some fresh air, we'll get you warmed up even on the coldest of days.
December to February, with a break to make sure we don't miss Santa.
Bull trout feeding on the remnants of the fall salmon runs.
Why You'll Love Winter Fishing
BC's south coast where we guide generally sees mild temperatures during the winter months which means we don't hang up the rods once fall salmon season ends. We jump right into our winter fly fishing program, chasing those big bull trout that are gorging on the flesh and eggs left behind by chum and coho salmon. River conditions are usually low and clear, so we fish light gear, swinging small steamers, egg patters and have a few other secret trips up our sleeve. Don't worry, we'll tell you exactly what to wear so you enjoy a comfortable day, even if it's a bit frosty.
A Winter Day Rundown
We generally start a bit later in the morning on the winter guided days. Let the day warm up a bit and enjoy a coffee. You'll meet your guide and then we head out with us to explore the upper Squamish River or the Cheakamus River, two rivers that we've spent over 20 years guiding on. We offer a variety of trip options, though full-day and half-day walk and wade trips are best for the winter and offer some time to warm up between spots.
Winter Bull Trout
Its a Rodeo
As you've gathered, our winter fly fishing trips focus on chasing bull trout. Bull trout are native to the Pacific Northwest and the fishery we enjoy here in Squamish is pretty unique. Bull trout get their name because of the flat tops of their heads that resemble that of a bull. Bull trout feed heavily in the winter months, gorging themselves on salmon eggs and flesh. In the spring months they feed on salmon fry. Average size of bull trout is 12-15 inches but 20+ inches aren't rare, we just need a hungry one.

According to the Chesapeake Bay Program, the striped bass is Maryland’s state fish, and one of the most popular commercial and recreational catches in the Chesapeake Bay.
The Bay is the largest striped bass nursery area on the Atlantic coast. Seventy to 90 percent of the Atlantic striped bass population uses the Bay to spawn.
The oldest recorded striped bass was 31 years old. The largest recorded striped bass was 125 pounds, caught on the North Carolina coast in 1891.
The recreational record for Chesapeake Bay striped bass is .
Read more about Striped Bass from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR).
It is believed that each tributary to the Chesapeake Bay has its own white perch population, since this fish likely does not venture far from the stream where it was born.
The Maryland Chesapeake Bay record white perch, caught in 1979 in Dundee Creek, weighed 2 pounds, 10 ounces.
Read more about the White Perch from Maryland DNR.
Yellow perch are generally freshwater fish and can be found in all Maryland reservoirs.
In Maryland, yellow perch have adapted to the estuarine waters of the Susquehanna Flats in the Chesapeake Bay and have historically been reported in all of its major tributaries and streams.
Yellow perch can reach a maximum size of 18 inches.
ead more about the Yellow Perch from Maryland DNR.
Blue crabs can be found in a variety of salinities ranging from the high saline waters at the mouth of the bay to the tidal fresh waters of the upper bay and tributaries. The blue crab isa bottom-dwelling species that utilizes a diversity of benthic habitats such as mud flats, oyster bars, channel edges, and tidal marshes. Submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) areas also serve as important nursery habitats that provide refuge for both juvenile blue crabs and molting crabs that are vulnerable to predation.
Blue crabs mate from May to October in the brackish or slightly salty waters of Chesapeake Bay.
Read more about the Blue Crab from Maryland DNR
Blue catfish are the largest of the catfish family in North America and can weigh in excess of 100 pounds.
The Maryland State record blue catfish is 84 pounds.

Time it right
Best time of year & tides for clear water
The Florida Keys are beautiful year-round, but a few simple things make the water clearer and the day calmer.
Wind matters most
Lighter winds mean glassier, clearer water. Calm mornings are often the prettiest time to be on Florida Bay.
Mind the tides
Around a higher or slack tide, the shallow flats look their clearest. Big swings stir up sediment, so the hour or two around slack water is best for visibility.
Light is everything
Mid-morning to early afternoon sun lights up the turquoise shallows; late afternoon delivers that golden glow for sunset sails.
Seasons
Winter & spring bring drier, breezier days; summer is warm and calm but can build afternoon clouds, so earlier departures are a safe bet.

=== PAGE: https://visitcentralflorida.org/featured/wonder-house-historic-tours/
TITLE: Wonder House Historic Tours - Central Florida - Visit Central Florida
Wonder House Historic Tours
The rebuilding and remodeling of the Wonder House was covered by episode 9 of the Netflix show Amazing Interiors. Owners of the private residence offer historic tours Friday – Sunday.
Before Cypress Gardens and Walt Disney World Resort, tourists flocked to this one-of-a-kind mansion in the heart of Central Florida.
With its concrete walls inlaid with glass tile mosaics, it’s no surprise the unique homestead, known as the Wonder House, quickly became a popular tourist destination from the 1930s – 1960s.
Building the Wonder House
Conrad Schuck was born in 1877 in Pittsburgh, PA, where he became a successful building contractor and stone quarry dealer. Upon doctors telling him he had only one year to live, Schuck packed up his family, and started to build his dream home in sunny Central Florida.
Wonder House Photograph Of Schuck
Construction of the Wonder House began in 1926. When Schuck started the excavation for the house, he found that he was digging into bedrock. An inventive architect, and stone dealer by trade, he decided to use the rocks to his advantage. Schuck built his four-story home out of concrete over stone, reinforced with steel railroad rails. On the ground floor, the walls are 18-inches thick!
The house was primarily built by Schuck and his five sons. His children hand-placed each tile, creating beautiful mosaics that each took weeks to complete. Because Schuck felt his dream home was never truly finished, his family never actually lived in the house they worked so hard to build.
Despite his bleak medical prognosis, Schuck went on to live for 40 more years, rather than the one predicted by doctors.
Unique Architecture
As Schuck didn’t anticipate living very long, he didn’t waste time with blueprints. In fact the blueprints of the Wonder House weren’t drafted until 1937, 11 years after construction of the house began.
The Wonder House was built in the shape of a cross, with each room opening up to two porches. If you lit the fireplace on the second floor, which is in the middle of the house, the hot air would rise, creating a cross-draft -– A/C of the 1920’s!
The porches were also designed to cool the house, as they were built with hollow concrete columns. Cold rain water from the roof ran through the inside of the walls, and could be turned on with a spigot to water the plants growing on the outside of the house.
Macabre Decor
Along with the unique architecture, another feature that fascinated tourists in the ‘30s was Schuck’s interesting collection of oddities. Schuck proudly displayed jarred snakes, taxidermy and even a coffin in the parlor! Keeping true to Schuck’s vision, the current owners have decorated the house with several unusual features, like the taxidermy deer and bug collection.
Restoration Process
After many years of being vacant, the once vibrant home, fell into disrepair. Fortunately in 2015, a young couple fell in love with the undeniable charm of the Wonder House, and made it their mission to restore the estate to its former glory. In fact, you can watch the restoration process on the Netflix Original show, Amazing Interiors.
Drew Davis and Krislin Kreis have worked tirelessly to restore and preserve the home, and in March 2019, their efforts paid off. The city of Bartow approved a zoning variance allowing the couple to open their home to paying guests on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.
With guided tours once again filling the 18-room home, this is an exciting time for visitors and locals alike to experience an important piece of Central Florida history.
Tour the Wonder House
When you visit the Wonder House, you’re treated like a guest, rather than some patron to a museum. You are welcome to sit on the furniture, and enjoy long conversations with the owners, while learning about this fascinating house.
Tours are available Friday at 7:00 p.m. and Saturday & Sunday at 10:00 a.m., Noon and 2:00 p.m. All tours must be scheduled in advance, via the Wonder House website, and tours typically last an hour and a half.
Parking for the tour is located in the rear of the property, accessible via El Paso Trail.
Cost: $20-$25/Adults, $10-$12.50/Children 12 and Under. The on-site gift shop is CASH ONLY.

=== PAGE: https://visitcentralflorida.org/featured/circle-b-bar-reserve/
TITLE: Hiking Trails in Central Florida - Lakeland, Florida - Visit Central Florida
A prime destination for hiking, bird watching and cycling. Visit the Polk Nature Discovery Center and learn about Polk County’s ecosystems through hands-on activities or climb around on the indoor play area that’s perfect for kids. A trip wouldn’t be complete without an alligator sighting, which can be safely done from the preserve’s pier or shoreline.
Central Florida Hiking Trails
From blazing red and orange sunrises over Lake Hancock to soaring bald eagles and rustic trails, Lakeland’s Circle B Bar Reserve is known as one of the best places to see wildlife in the state. Sure, you can walk the up to six miles of trails if you’d like – but you can also explore this slice of Florida nature by bike. Just make sure to pay attention for the main attraction, alligators.
See an Alligator, or 10
If the state’s most popular reptile is on your must-see list, this is perhaps the best place to observe them in the wild. Comprised of nearly 1,300 acres, the park has numerous trails, with the most popular trail being Alligator Alley Trail.
Alligator Alley runs along alligator-inhabited Lake Hancock, and the star attractions may be observed at a distance from shore or from a number of piers. Ranging in size from mere inches to nearly as long as your average hatchback car, the alligators are at home in the oak hammock, freshwater marsh, hardwood swamp and the lake shore on the reserve.
The Trails
With all the alligators around, it’s the perfect place to bring a camera – but don’t miss out on everything else around you. Circle B Bar Reserve, with a series of well-maintained marked trails of different lengths, provides countless opportunities for photographers and painters looking to capture the beauty of nature. The tremendous bird population includes a variety of wading birds, waterfowl, ospreys and bald eagles.
Nine hard-packed trails are great for hiking as well as gravel or mountain bikes. Trail maps and information are available from the knowledgeable volunteers that greet you at the front desk of the Discovery Center. These volunteers are excited to help and love to answer any questions.
Tram Tours
A unique way to enjoy the beautiful reserve is to sign up for a tram tour. Circle B Bar Reserve staff and volunteers offer free guided tram tours a few times each month. You can experience the local ecosystems on wheels rather than foot.
Polk Nature Discovery Center
One of the greatest features of this reserve is the Polk Nature Discovery Center. This educational building is the perfect place to start your adventure before trekking into the woods. Here, you are filled with information on Central Florida’s ecosystem with interactive exhibits that are sure to stimulate young minds (and adult minds, too!)

TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions - Discover Tahoe Chartered Cruises
Frequently Asked Questions
You can book online or in person (walk ins welcome on a 1st come-1st served basis). Our address is 2435 Venice Dr, South Lake Tahoe, CA 96150. All bookings come with a captain which you choose from a pre-approved list upon arrival. You can also appoint a USCG captain but must call staff well in advance to set up training. PLEASE READ YOUR EMAIL from us! It contains pertinent information about where we meet, what to bring, and your waivers. Many people who get lost do not read their email!
The Tahoe Keys Marina has plenty of parking on the parking lot. On busy days, sometimes parking is limited, so parking on Venice Dr will do.
Yes, please call (530) 659-3452 or email Contact@discovertahoerentals.com. We can drop off rentals on public docks or private docks that you have made arrangements with.
Bookings can be made on the spot if there is a boat available. However, most of the time we sell out online well before.
The responsible party (renter) must be at least 18 years old. The driver (operator) of the watercraft must be at least 25 years old and possess a current USCG Officer credential of any type. The operator must be trained with the watercraft well before the booking starts. Captains are retained on a list for hire by the renter.
If you are renting the watercraft without a captain (Must be discussed with staff well before the booking). You will need a Boaters Education card from either of the following states.
In Nevada, if you were born after 1983, you can obtain a Boaters Education Card. Visit the Nevada Boating Safety page on NDOW.org
In California, if you are 65 years old or younger, then you can obtain a California Boater Card. More information can be found here: Visit the California Boater Card website
If your boat is captained, then don’t worry about it.
Life jackets must be worn by anyone who is 12 or younger. This is USCG law and strictly enforced.
Alcohol is allowed on the boat. The operator must remain sober by all means. If no one wants to be the DD, ask about the Captains service!
Smoking vapes and e-cigarettes’, pens, etc. are allowed. Smoking anything that causes ash to be produced and/or causes an increase risk of fire is prohibited onboard.
Click on the “Book Adventure” page on the top of this webpage. You will find the booking process there. Pick a boat first, then fill in your information. Online available times are set well before the booking date. If you want to go out at a different time then what is open online, please call or text us at (530) 659-3452. Once you purchase your booking, you will get an email from us with meet up information and waivers. PLEASE READ THE EMAIL! It will save you time and confusion once you arrive at our busy marina.
We are now using an automated waiver system. If you complete the waivers online, you will just need to get on the boat when you arrive. If you don’t use the automated system, please arrive 15 minutes prior to your booking to sing waivers on our IPad. The person paying for the booking will need to be at least 18 years old. Each person riding with us will need to sign a liability waiver and the main renter will complete a pre-inspection report with the captain before they set out.
100% refund 5 days before the booking starts no questions asked. Dangerous weather or boat malfunctions receive 100% refund or the option to reschedule. These are often last minute judgments due to their nature. We thank you in advance for your patients.
Renters more than a 1/2 hour late without making contact with staff will be considered a renter cancelation. Failure to provide adequate verification, sign rental agreements, etc. will also be considered a renter cancelation. The best way to reduce the chance of this happening is communicating with staff as soon as a problem is noticed. We do not refund any portion of the booking for late arrivals or missing guests. Please plan in advance.
Lake Tahoe can be a little fussy sometimes. Dangerous weather for purposes of cancelations are named storms, excessive wind causing larges waves or the watercraft to yaw or roll dangerously and active lightning storms. Other weather cancelations are at the discretion of staff. Usually, rain or cold/overcast weather does not qualify for a refund but you can get a reschedule if staff permits. Your safety is our #1 priority.
In most cases, the boats come back unharmed. However, weather the damage was caused by your captain or someone in your party, Discover Tahoe will investigate each case carefully.

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

1. General Tour Information
What is the Kaneohe Sandbar?
The Kaneohe Sandbar is a natural, white-sand reef located in the middle of Kaneohe Bay on Oʻahu’s windward coast. A stunning spot to walk, swim, and explore. It’s one of the most unique experiences in Hawaii and is only accessible by boat.
Where is Kaneohe Bay located?
Kaneohe Bay sits on the east side of Oʻahu, about a 30- to 40-minute drive from Waikiki or Honolulu. KBOS operates directly out of Heʻeia Kea Boat Harbor, the closest and most convenient marina to access the sandbar.
How long is the sandbar tour?
Our tours typically last about 3 hours, giving you plenty of time to enjoy the boat ride, relax at the sandbar, and try out activities like snorkeling, paddleboarding, and banana boat rides.
What activities are included in the sandbar experience?
Depending on your package, activities may include snorkeling with tropical fish, paddleboarding, kayaking, banana boat rides, bumper tubes, or simply relaxing on the sandbar. We provide the equipment and guides, so you can focus on having fun.
Is the sandbar tour family-friendly?
Yes! Families with children of all ages are welcome. The calm waters of Kaneohe Bay make it safe and enjoyable for kids, while adults can enjoy both relaxation and adventure.
2. Weather & Seasonal Conditions
Is the Kaneohe Sandbar tour available year-round?
Yes, our tours run throughout the year. Hawaii’s warm, tropical climate means you can enjoy the sandbar in any season.
What happens if it rains on the day of my tour?
Light tropical showers are common in Hawaii and usually pass quickly. Tours still run in rain, but in the rare case of unsafe weather, we’ll notify you and help reschedule or refund your booking.
Does the tide affect the sandbar experience?
Yes, the tide changes how much of the sandbar is exposed. During low tide, you can walk on dry sand, while at high tide, the water may be waist- to chest-deep. No matter the tide, the sandbar is always beautiful and swimmable.
When is the best time of day to visit the sandbar?
Both morning and afternoon tours offer incredible views. Mornings often have calmer seas and clearer water, while afternoons provide golden light perfect for photos.

You can easily book online through our official website or by phone. Advance reservations are highly recommended, as tours often sell out.

Can I change or cancel my booking?
Currently, changes and cancellations are permitted within our 48-hour policy window. Please review our full cancellation policy when booking, or contact our team for assistance.
Do I need to print my ticket, or is digital confirmation accepted?
Digital confirmations are accepted. Simply show your booking email on your phone at check-in.
Are group bookings or private charters available?
Absolutely. We offer private charters for families, corporate groups, weddings, and special events. Please contact us for custom packages.

Pricing depends on the package and activities included. Standard and All-Inclusive tours start at an affordable rate per person, while private charters are custom-priced.

Yes, we offer kamaʻāina rates for Hawaii residents and discounts for children.
What payment methods do you accept?
We accept major credit cards, debit cards, and online payments.
Are tips or gratuities included in the price?
Tips are not included but are greatly appreciated by our crew if you enjoyed your experience.
Do you offer refunds?
Refunds are available if you cancel within our policy window.

We operate out of Heʻeia Kea Boat Harbor in Kaneohe. Directions and parking details will be provided in your confirmation email.

Yes, parking is available at Heʻeia Kea Harbor.

Bring your booking confirmation (digital or printed), a photo ID, sunscreen, a swimsuit, towel, and any personal items you may need.

Our saltwater fly fishing is done off a boat, typically near the shorelines, in very shallow water. We fish both top-water and sinking flies, using both floating and sinking lines. Fly fishing is a method where you’ll be casting hand-tied flies and weighted line that match with a specific weight fly rod. TITLE: Your Seattle Fishing Guides | Puget WA | Spot Tail Guides
Your Seattle Fishing Guides
My name is Keith Robbins, and I’ve been fishing on the Puget Sound my whole life. I’ve been guiding for 35 years now with my own business, and worked for another captain for three years before that. Some kids love football or basketball, but it was always all about fishing for me. When I was a kid, my mom used to drop me off at the dock in the morning and pick me up at the end of the day (back when you could do that kind of thing). From when I was a little kid, to a young rookie, to becoming a captain and business owner, fishing has always been my favorite thing to do.
Some people have to drag themselves to work every morning. But me, I get to spend every day on the water introducing anglers to my favorite place on the planet. I love being on the Sound and watching someone catch their first fish or the biggest salmon of their lives. I hope to give everyone on my boat a really memorable day on the water, surrounded by the sights and beauty of the Puget Sound (and I hope the fish cooperate too). All I know, is the only reason I have ever worked any job was to support my fishing habit. I try to share the best things about fishing with every guest who boards my boat: From the sunrise over Mount Rainier and the Seattle skyline, to feeling that first bite at the end of your line, to when your arms are aching after a successful day at sea, fishing on the Puget Sound is an unforgettable experience. I’d love to share that with you and your family.

=== PAGE: https://www.backwoodsairboatadventures.com/blog/are-alligators-mammals-the-truth-about-these-ancient-reptiles/
TITLE: Alligators: Mammals or Reptiles? Clear Up the Confusion
The American alligator is one of the most iconic animals in the United States, especially in places like Florida and Louisiana where they roam freely in swamps and marshes. Their prehistoric appearance has fascinated both scientists and wildlife enthusiasts for decades. However, one common question continues to pop up among curious minds: ? Let’s dive deep into this question and uncover the truth about these ancient creatures.
What Exactly Is an Alligator?
Before answering is an alligator a mammal, it’s important to understand what an alligator actually is. An alligator is a large, carnivorous reptile with a broad snout, powerful tail, and armored body covered in scales. They belong to the order Crocodylia, which also includes crocodiles, caimans, and gharials. Specifically, they fall under the family Alligatoridae.
Are alligators mammals or reptiles?
The answer is straightforward—alligators are reptiles, not mammals. Their biological and physical characteristics firmly place them in the class Reptilia. While they may share some superficial similarities with mammals—such as having a backbone—their fundamental traits set them apart.
Here’s a breakdown of what makes an alligator a reptile:
Alligators are ectothermic, meaning they rely on external sources to regulate their body temperature. Mammals, on the other hand, are warm-blooded and regulate their temperature internally.
Alligators have tough, keratinized scales (known as scutes) that cover their bodies, providing protection and reducing water loss. Mammals have skin covered in hair or fur.
Another major distinction is reproduction. Many people wonder, does a alligator have a backbone and does a alligator lay eggs? The answer to both is yes. Alligators are vertebrates (animals with a backbone), and they reproduce by laying eggs—unlike mammals that give birth to live young.
How Do Alligators Reproduce?
One of the clearest signs that an alligator is a mammal is false lies in their reproductive method. During the breeding season, female alligators build large nests of vegetation, mud, and sticks. Once ready, they lay between 20 to 50 eggs per nest. These alligator eggs are carefully guarded by the mother until they hatch.
Unlike mammals, which nourish embryos internally, alligators rely on external incubation. The temperature of the nest even determines the sex of the hatchlings—warmer nests produce males, while cooler nests produce females.
Similarities and Differences Between Alligators and Crocodiles
Many people also ask, is a crocodile a mammal? Like alligators, crocodiles are reptiles too. Although closely related, alligators and crocodiles belong to different families and have distinct features:
Alligators have a broad, U-shaped snout and darker skin, while crocodiles have a more pointed, V-shaped snout and lighter, olive-colored skin.
Crocodiles are more tolerant of saltwater environments, while alligators prefer freshwater swamps and rivers.
In alligators, the upper jaw is wider than the lower, so their teeth are less visible when the mouth is closed. Crocodiles show both upper and lower teeth when their mouths are shut.
So, to settle the question—is a crocodile a mammal? No, just like alligators, crocodiles are reptiles.
Does an Alligator Have a Backbone?
Yes, absolutely. A common misconception is thinking reptiles are “primitive” and lack complex skeletal structures. In fact, does a alligator have a backbone? Yes, it does. Alligators, like all reptiles, are vertebrates. Their backbone (spinal column) runs from the skull to the tip of their tail, giving their body structure and aiding in movement. This vertebrate characteristic is one thing they share with both birds and mammals.
Why Do People Confuse Alligators with Mammals?
The confusion likely stems from the fact that alligators display highly developed parental care, which is uncommon in most reptiles. Female alligators fiercely guard their nests and even help their hatchlings reach water—a behavior more often associated with mammals or birds. Their intelligence, complex social behaviors, and ability to vocalize (like bellowing or chirping hatchlings) also blur the lines for the average observer.
However, despite these behaviors, the biological evidence is clear: is alligator a mammal? No. They are reptiles through and through.
To sum it all up: are alligators mammals? Is a alligator a mammal? No, alligators are reptiles. They are cold-blooded, egg-laying animals with scaly skin, and they belong to the class Reptilia and the order Crocodylia. Although they have a backbone like mammals and demonstrate impressive parental care, their core biological traits firmly separate them from mammals.
So the next time you spot one of these majestic creatures basking in the Florida sun or swimming gracefully in a swamp during a , you’ll know the answer to both are alligators mammals or reptiles and is an alligator a mammal—they’re reptiles, relics of an ancient lineage that predates even the dinosaurs.

TITLE: Bowen Island Sea Kayaking | Discover Adventure Today
Book Now
Bowen Island Sea Kayaking offers spectacular kayak tours, kayaking lessons and kayak rentals on beautiful Bowen Island. Whether you are an experienced kayaker or this is your first time we will ensure you have an unforgettable time. It is easy toand one of the top places to go from Vancouver.
Explore the Vancouver Coast with our Scenic Kayaking Tours
At Bowen Island Sea Kayaking, we offer a wide range of kayaking tours. Looking for an introductory half day kayaking tour with children or a full day kayak tour exploring the Pasley Islands, we have you covered. Plan a multi-day kayaking adventure with our small team of qualified guides, for the trip of a lifetime.
With over 25 years of knowledge, we know the best places to see wildlife and enjoy the beautiful mountain and ocean views. From complete beginners to avid kayaking adventurers, we have kayak tours for everyone.
Explore Half Day Kayak Tours
Enjoy Freedom with our Flexible Kayak Rentals
Looking to explore the coastline by kayak with your friends? At Bowen Island Sea Kayaking, we offer one person or two-person kayaks for rent. Our kayak rentals start with a minimum 2 hour duration for those looking for a morning or afternoon on the water. Experienced kayakers have the ability to rent our kayaks for multiple days to explore the BC Marine Trail campsites situated throughout Howe Sound. We also offer Stand Up Paddle boards for rent.
Whether you are looking for a quick paddle in the safety of our protected bays or a more challenging ocean experience, every rental comes with all the safety gear you need, basic instruction, advice on paddling routes and the best spots for wildlife viewing.
Learn More About Rentals
Build Your Skills with Kayaking Lessons
Looking to get into kayaking for the first time? Have your own kayak and want to build confidence on the water? Bowen Island Sea Kayaking offers a number of different ways to improve your kayaking skills. We host half-day introductory courses teaching paddling techniques and how to safely launch and land. We also offer capsize recovery classes, a skill that should be practiced every year if you spend time kayaking. Level 1 skills courses can also be arranged if you are looking for more comprehensive training.
Our small class sizes make sure you are well looked after by your instructor.

=== PAGE: https://h5helicopters.com/faqs/
TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions - H5 Helicopters
Frequently Asked Questions
Booking & Pricing
How do I book a helicopter tour?
The easiest way to book is to call us at (480) 272-1100 (text works too)— we respond quickly and love talking through options with you. You can also email us at info@h5helicopters.com and we’ll get back to you promptly. Package rates are listed on the website; custom adventures will be quoted personally.
How much does a helicopter ride cost?
Pricing is based on total flight time, any layover time, the nature of the flight, and time of day. Our packages start at $1,850 for the 35-Minute Phoenix ride and go well over $10,000 for longer custom trips, with all rates billed per flight — not per person — for up to 5 passengers. Package rates are listed on the website; custom flights are quoted individually. Our pricing reflects the world-class, cinematic experience we deliver — guests consistently call it the best investment they’ve ever made in a memory. There are no taxes on our flights. A 3.65% processing fee applies when paying by credit card — no fee for cash or wire transfer.
Are rates per person or per flight?
All of our package rates are billed per flight, not per person. Whether it’s just the two of you or a full group of five, you pay one flat rate — making it an incredible value the more people you bring.
Can I customize my flight?
Absolutely. We accommodate virtually any request — unique flight routes, champagne toasts, catered mountain-top meals, proposals, anniversaries, corporate experiences, and more. Call us and we’ll brainstorm something unforgettable together.
The Experience
What should I expect on my flight?
Think of it as a luxury SUV in the sky. You’ll fly in our climate-controlled Airbus AS350-B2 wearing Bose noise-cancelling headsets, so you can hear your pilot’s narration and carry on full conversations with your group. H5 plans every flight the same way we do when filming for IMAX, National Geographic, Netflix, and AppleTV — so you get a cinematic, front-row perspective on Arizona that most people never see.
Is a helicopter tour worth the money?
Overwhelmingly, yes. Our guests consistently call it the best or most memorable experience of their lives. The helicopter is essentially a time machine — it lets you see places in minutes that would take hours to reach by land, and from angles that are simply impossible any other way. Rates are per flight, not per person, so split among a group it’s surprisingly accessible. We’d challenge you to find a better value for an experience of this caliber.
Will we be the only ones on the helicopter?
Yes — every H5 flight is completely private. You’ll never share your helicopter with strangers. One passenger can ride up front with the pilot, and up to four in the back. For couples, we often remove the front seat to open the whole cabin for maximum comfort and visibility.
Are the flights narrated?
Yes. Our pilots have deep knowledge of Arizona’s landmarks, geology, history, and hidden gems. They’ll point out everything worth seeing and are happy to answer questions along the way.
When is the best time to fly?
Arizona’s weather is exceptional for flying nearly year-round. Morning and afternoon flights are both great. Sunset flights are our most popular — Arizona sunsets are genuinely spectacular from the air. If you’re flexible, we’re happy to help you pick the best time for your goals.
What are some tips to maximize my experience?
Arrive on time. Wear comfortable clothes (our cabin is climate-controlled, but wear closed-toe shoes if you’re doing an off-airport landing). Immerse yourself in the experience — taking pictures/videos is encouraged and we recommend soaking in the moments to the fullest. Bring sunglasses for bright days. And ask questions — our pilots love sharing what they know.
Do you film the tour?
We can! H5 was founded as an aerial film production company, so professional-quality video is in our DNA. Let us know when you book and we’ll mount cameras to capture the highlights. It makes for an incredible keepsake.
Safety & Comfort
Are helicopter rides safe?
Yes — safety is our absolute top priority. H5 Helicopters has been flying incident-free since opening in 2008. Our Airbus AS350-B2 is widely considered one of the safest helicopter models in the world, and it’s maintained by certified Airbus Airframe & Powerplant mechanics. We adhere to the strictest FAA safety standards on every flight.
What makes H5 Helicopters different from other operators?
H5 was established in 2008 as an aerial film production company — we’ve flown for IMAX, National Geographic, Netflix, and AppleTV. That means we approach every guest flight with a filmmaker’s eye: optimal routes, cinematic perspectives, and an attention to detail that generic operators simply don’t have. Flights will include a combination of flying at different altitudes to give you the best perspective. We’re family-run and veteran-owned. Our typical clientele includes celebrities, executives, and high-net-worth individuals who expect an elevated experience. You’re not cattle being herded through — you’re the star of the show.
How experienced are your pilots?
H5 pilots are among the most experienced in the industry. With more than 55 years of combined aviation experience and a spotless safety record between our two pilots, you’re in excellent hands. Our team has flown missions for major film productions and has extensive knowledge of Arizona’s terrain and airspace.
What if I'm nervous about flying?
Nerves are completely normal! We hear this often, and almost every nervous first-timer ends up loving it. Our pilots are calm, professional, and great at putting guests at ease. The aircraft is smooth and quiet. And here’s something that helps: if for any reason something feels off after takeoff, we can return to the hangar immediately — no questions asked. There’s no pressure. Just let your pilot know and we’ll take care of you.
Do you recommend anti-motion sickness medication?
Only if you’re particularly prone to motion sickness. Our flights are exceptionally smooth — guests often compare it to riding in a luxury SUV. The overwhelming majority of passengers have no issues whatsoever. If you want to be cautious, we provide complimentary over-the-counter motion sickness medication that can be taken beforehand is a reasonable precaution.
What is your weather policy?
Safety and guest experience come first, always. Arizona’s weather is outstanding for flying the vast majority of the time. We monitor conditions closely before every flight and will proactively reach out if we anticipate any concerns. Guests are never charged for delays or cancellations caused by weather.
Who Can Fly
Are there age restrictions?
There are no age restrictions for our tours. Per FAA regulations, children age 2 and older must have their own seat and seatbelt. Children under 2 may sit on a parent’s lap. There is no maximum age limit, and we’re happy to assist guests getting on and off the helicopter.
Is there a weight restriction?
Yes — our AS350-B2 has an 850-lb total passenger weight limit (sometimes reduced in summer heat) and a 300-lb per-passenger limit. Please keep this in mind when booking so we can ensure a safe and comfortable flight for everyone.
Can I fly if I'm pregnant?
We don’t have a blanket restriction on flying during pregnancy. However, we recommend that guests in their third trimester consult their doctor before flying. Our flights operate at lower altitudes, which reduces any altitude-related concerns.
Can guests with disabilities or mobility limitations fly?
Absolutely. We assist guests in and out of the aircraft and have accommodated guests who use wheelchairs. We may be able to store a folding wheelchair in the cargo area depending on it’s size and your flight plan. Give us a call and we’ll work out the details together.
Logistics
Where are you located?

=== PAGE: https://h5helicopters.com/the-h5-hangar-group-experience-scottsdales-most-unique-corporate-event-and-incentive-trip/
TITLE: The H5 Hangar Group Experience: Scottsdale's Most Unique Corporate Event and Incentive Trip - H5 Helicopters
Picture this. Your top sales rep just closed the biggest quarter of her career, and the reward you’ve got planned is a steakhouse dinner and a round of golf they’ve already played a dozen times. Meanwhile, forty of their colleagues are standing in a private hangar at Scottsdale Airpark, watching a group of four lift off over the McDowell Mountains while the rest of the team mingles next to a vintage car display with music playing and drinks in hand. Twenty minutes later, that group lands, and the next group climbs aboard. This is what a corporate event looks like when it’s built around something people actually remember.
For meeting planners, DMCs, and HR teams searching for a corporate group experience in Scottsdale that isn’t another rented ballroom, the H5 Hangar Group Experience was built specifically to solve that problem. It’s not a helicopter tour with a corporate label slapped on it. It’s a purpose-built event format designed to get large groups airborne, entertained, and talking about it long after they’ve flown home.
What Is the ?
H5 Hangar Group Experience
The H5 Hangar Group Experience combines short rotational helicopter flights with a private hangar venue, all in one package, at one location: our hangar at Scottsdale Airpark, adjacent to Scottsdale Airport. Instead of a single group boarding one aircraft for a long tour, we run our AS350-B2 A-Star, SaberCat1, on a continuous rotation. Small groups of up to four to five passengers fly a short scenic loop over the Valley, land, and the next group boards while the previous one rejoins the party in the hangar.
That rotation format is what makes this package work for groups that other tour operators simply can’t accommodate. A single-aircraft charter can only move one small group at a time. The Hangar Group Experience turns that limitation into a feature: everyone gets their turn in the air, nobody is stuck waiting outside in the Arizona sun, and the energy never stops between flights because the hangar itself is part of the experience.
Built for Groups Up to About 60, Not a Generic Off-Site
Most “unique venue” searches in Scottsdale turn up rooftop bars, resort ballrooms, or golf clubhouses that dozens of other companies have already used for their off-site. A private hangar with a helicopter rotation running through it is not something your team has seen before, and that novelty is exactly what makes an incentive trip or team-building day land differently.
Between flights, guests have the run of the hangar space, shaded from the Arizona sun, which matters a great deal if your event falls during the hotter stretch of the calendar. Groups bring in their own catering, music, and activities, so the space flexes around whatever format your planner has in mind, whether that’s a structured team-building agenda or an open cocktail-hour vibe. It’s a working aviation hangar with a fleet of helicopter memorabilia and history, not a converted event space pretending to be something it isn’t.
Turning a Reward Trip Into an Incentive Travel Win
We’ve seen firsthand how much more a reward trip means when the activity itself is the story people tell afterward. Earlier this year, we chartered a private flight to Sedona for a company’s top sales performers as part of their annual award trip, the kind of President’s Club or sales-incentive reward that’s supposed to feel unforgettable. That’s the standard we build every corporate booking around, whether it’s one VIP flight for five top performers or a full Hangar Group Experience for an entire regional team.
If you’re a planner working with a DMC on an incentive travel program for teams visiting the Phoenix Valley for a conference, sales kickoff, or company retreat, this is the kind of activity that gets remembered in the post-trip survey. It photographs well, it gives every attendee an individual moment (their turn in the air), and it doesn’t require anyone to be an outdoor-adventure type to enjoy it fully.
Is the H5 Hangar Group Experience Good for Large Corporate Groups?
Yes. The Hangar Group Experience is specifically designed for groups that a single helicopter charter can’t handle at once, typically groups approaching 60 guests. The rotation format keeps flights moving continuously throughout the event, usually getting somewhere in the neighborhood of a dozen or more guests airborne per hour, while the rest of the group stays engaged in the private hangar between flights. It’s built for corporate off-sites, conference add-on excursions, incentive trips, and DMC-booked group programs across the Scottsdale and greater Phoenix area.
Pairing the Hangar Experience with a Signature Flight
Many of our corporate clients layer in something extra for their VIPs or top performers on top of the group rotation. A Mountain Top Landing, with its private summit layover above Roosevelt Lake, makes a fitting reward flight for an executive team or your top three sales performers before or after the main group event. It’s the kind of add-on that lets a planner build tiers into an incentive program, a group experience for everyone and a signature flight for the people being specifically honored.
Why Scottsdale Airpark Works for Groups Flying In
Scottsdale Airpark sits minutes from the resort corridor along Scottsdale Road and from Old Town Scottsdale, which means groups staying at Valley resorts or attending a downtown Scottsdale conference can be at our hangar with a short shuttle ride, no detour to Phoenix Sky Harbor required. From the air, guests get a genuine sense of the Sonoran Desert landscape that surrounds the Valley, the McDowell Mountains, Pinnacle Peak, and the desert terrain stretching toward the Superstition Mountains and Four Peaks, all in a single short flight. For DMCs building a multi-day itinerary, that proximity is often the difference between an activity that actually fits the schedule and one that eats an entire afternoon in transit.
Planning Your Group’s Visit
Every corporate and group booking at H5 is a private arrangement. We don’t sell seats on shared tours, which means your group’s flights, timing, and hangar setup are built around your event, not fit into someone else’s schedule. Whether you’re a DMC building out a client proposal, an HR team planning an incentive trip, or a company simply looking for the most memorable few hours your team has had together in years, we’d like to help you plan it.
Call us at (480) 272-1100 or email info@h5helicopters.com to talk through your group size, dates, and vision for the H5 Hangar Group Experience. You can also find more detail on our group and venue offerings on our website. Your team’s flight of a lifetime is ready when you are.
