Can we do a sunset 35-minute flight?
Yes! A sunset upgrade is available for $300 and is absolutely worth it. Arizona’s sunsets are some of the most spectacular in the world, and seeing them from the air is an experience you’ll talk about for years.
Is this a good experience for kids?
Kids love it. There are no age restrictions (children under 2 may sit on a parent’s lap; 2 and older need their own seat per FAA rules). The flight is smooth, exciting, and something the whole family will remember. Our pilots are great with young guests.
Your private flight, professional pilot narration, Bose noise-cancelling headsets with Bluetooth connectivity, a climate-controlled cabin, and the H5 experience. Music and drinks are included. Any add-ons (champagne, custom requests, video production) can be arranged when you book.
Is the price really per flight, not per person?
Yes — $1,850 covers your entire group for one flight, up to 5 passengers (or 850 lbs total). The more people you bring, the better the value. Split five ways, it’s less than $400 per person for an experience most people call the highlight of their trip to Arizona.
What is the best helicopter tour in the Phoenix / Scottsdale area?
H5 Helicopters is widely regarded as the top helicopter experience in the Phoenix-Scottsdale area. We’re the only operator flying the same routes and techniques used for IMAX and National Geographic productions — which means you get a cinematic, once-in-a-lifetime perspective on Arizona. Our 35-minute ride is an ideal starting point, and our guest reviews speak for themselves.

=== PAGE: https://h5helicopters.com/sedona-helicopter-tours-from-scottsdale-red-rock-country-the-way-almost-nobody-sees-it/
TITLE: Sedona Helicopter Tours from Scottsdale: Red Rock Country the Way Almost Nobody Sees It - H5 Helicopters
Just minutes after lifting off from our private hangar at the Scottsdale Airpark, the desert stops being brown. The saguaros thin out, the Bradshaw Mountains rise on your left, and then the whole world turns the color of a struck match. Sandstone spires. Deep green ribbons of Oak Creek. Buttes standing in open air like something built rather than eroded. You have seen photos of Sedona. Almost nobody has seen it from 1,000 feet with nothing between them and the rock but a pane of glass and a quiet, air conditioned cabin.
That is the honest pitch for a Sedona helicopter tour out of Scottsdale. It is not a shortcut. It is a different Sedona entirely.
Why Sedona Looks Completely Different From the Air
Sedona is a landscape built in vertical layers, and the ground gives you exactly one of them. From State Route 179 you see the front faces of Bell Rock and Courthouse Butte. From a trailhead you see the wall in front of you. What you cannot see, at any price, from a road or a jeep seat, is the geometry. The way Cathedral Rock’s fins fan out like a hand. The way Oak Creek Canyon knifes north into the Mogollon Rim and turns from red rock to ponderosa pine in the space of a few miles. The way Boynton Canyon closes into a box with sheer walls on three sides.
From the air, those relationships snap into place. Guests who have hiked Sedona for years say the same thing on the flight home, that they never understood how the place fit together until they saw it whole. That is the perspective shift people are actually paying for. The helicopter is just the delivery system.
What You Actually Fly Over Between Scottsdale and the Red Rocks
The route north is not filler. Our Sedona Experience runs a 25 minute flight through the Red Rock canyons, and the approach to get there is a tour in its own right. You climb out over the McDowell Mountains and the north Valley, cross Black Canyon City and the wide open country of Bloody Basin, run the eastern flank of the Bradshaw Mountains, and drop into the green sweep of the Camp Verde Valley with the Verde River winding underneath. Then the rock changes color and you are into red rock country, working the canyons at an altitude that makes the formations feel close enough to touch.
The whole experience, Scottsdale to Sedona and back with time on the ground in between, is a two hour block of your day. Driving the same 115 miles up Interstate 17 burns roughly four hours round trip, most of it spent looking at asphalt.
The Sedona Airport Layover: Where a Flight Becomes a Day
Here is the part people do not expect. The Sedona Experience an optional layover at the Sedona Airport, which sits on top of Airport Mesa, a flat table of rock in the middle of town with one of the most photographed views in Arizona right off the end of it. Many guests like to enjoy lunch at the famous Mesa Grill which is located at the airport. Guests can enjoy watching planes takeoff and land at the Sedona Airport runway from the comfort of the restaurant. Guests who want a longer window on the ground can extend the layover when they book.
So it reads like a scenic flight and it functions like a day trip. You get Sedona itself, without the drive, and you are back at the hangar in Scottsdale in time for a dinner reservation in Old Town.
Sedona Helicopter Tours in Summer: Quietly the Best Time to Go
Late summer in Arizona sends most visitors indoors, and this is exactly where flying beats every other outdoor option in the Phoenix Valley. Our AS350-B2 A Star has a fully air conditioned cabin. While a jeep tour, a hike, or a balloon basket puts you out in the heat, you are sitting in cooled air watching the state go by. Sedona sits about 4,500 feet up and runs meaningfully cooler than the Valley floor, so your time on the ground on Airport Mesa is comfortable in a way midday Scottsdale is not.
Monsoon season adds something too. Late summer storms scrub the air and green up the high desert, and the light after a cell moves through is what photographers drive across the country for. Weather occasionally moves a flight, and we never charge for a weather cancellation.
Common Questions About Sedona Helicopter Tours
Plan on about two hours total. That includes the flight north through the red rock canyons, a layover of at least an hour at Sedona Airport, and the return flight to Scottsdale.
The H5 Sedona Experience offers an optional add on layover at Sedona Airport on Airport Mesa, so you get time on the ground in town rather than only a flyover.
Every flight we operate is private. You are never seated with strangers. The aircraft carries up to 5 passengers, subject to an 850 pound total passenger weight limit, and the entire helicopter belongs to your group.
Our private hangar in the Scottsdale Airpark at 16114 N 81st Street, Scottsdale, adjacent to Scottsdale Airport. Guests arrive 20 minutes early for check in, a hangar tour, and a safety brief.
Who This Flight Is For, and What Comes After It
Couples celebrating an anniversary book this one constantly, and so do families who want one unforgettable day instead of a week of scattered activities. Groups in town for a conference use it as an executive add on, and the destination management companies we work with across Scottsdale and Phoenix build it into itineraries for clients who have already done the golf and the resort spa.
If Sedona is the appetizer, the Grand Canyon Experience is the full meal. It includes everything in the Sedona Experience and then continues north through the Zuni Point Corridor over the Grand Canyon, with a layover at Grand Canyon Airport plus the Little Colorado River Canyon, the Painted Desert, Meteor Crater, and the ponderosa pines of the Mogollon Rim on the way home. It is our most requested flight, and it captures more of Arizona in four hours than most people see in a lifetime.
H5 Helicopters is veteran owned and family run, flying out of Scottsdale since 2008 with two pilots holding more than 55 years of combined experience and a perfect safety record. The same aircraft has flown aerial work for Apple TV, Netflix, National Geographic, IMAX, and Discovery. When you book, you get that airframe and those pilots to yourself.
To check availability for the Sedona Experience, or to talk through a custom itinerary for a couple, a family, or a corporate group, call us at or email . Tell us the date and how many are flying, and we will build the day around it.

TITLE: About Center Hill Lake | Center Hill Marina
Center Hill Lake
Welcome to Center Hill Lake!
Welcome to Center Hill Lake! Located just an hour outside of Nashville, Center Hill Lake offers the perfect getaway from the hustle and bustle of the city. CHL was created by the construction of the Center Hill Dam across the Caney Fork River. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers led the construction to its completion in 1948. Since then, Center Hill Lake has been a hot spot for boating, fishing, camping, wildlife watching, hiking, and so much more! Whatever your interest may be, there is something for everyone at Center Hill.
Center Hill Lake is home to several state parks and waterfalls that are sure to impress! A few that we recommend visiting include Burgess falls, Fancher falls, and Rock Island State Park. There is so much to explore whether you are vacationing for the week or getting away for the day! With 18,000 acres of lake, you’re sure to find the perfect spot to get in some quality fishing! Fish such as bass, crappie, bluegill, and catfish can be caught from the shoreline or from a boat! It’s important to remember that all fisherman age 13 or older are required to have a valid Tennessee State fishing license.
Escape and Relax
Vacationing at Center Hill Lake is about escaping from the everyday stresses of life. It’s about taking the time to unplug and unwind all while making long-lasting memories with the people you love, and we would love to be a part of that experience. As far as lodging we offer both cabin and houseboat rentals, but if you’re looking to just get away for the day we also offer pontoon rentals! El Lago Mexican Restaurant is open year-round serving up authentic and delicious food, and is the perfect way to end your day at Center Hill Lake.
Interactive Map
Click on the magnifying glasses to see more!
A Brief History Of Center Hill Lake
1942
Construction Begins
Construction of Center Hill Dam begins, initiated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to provide flood control and hydroelectric power.
1948
Completion
Completion of Center Hill Dam, creating Center Hill Lake.
1950s-1960s
Development
Development of recreational facilities around the lake, including parks and boat ramps.
1980s
Preservation Efforts
Implementation of environmental protections to preserve the natural habitat and water quality.
2007
Rehabilitation Begins
Start of a major rehabilitation project on the dam to address seepage and stability issues.
2015
Rehabilitation Complete
Completion of the dam rehabilitation, ensuring the safety and structural integrity for future generations.
June 10, 2024
New Gate
On Monday, June 10th, the Corps reinstalled the orifice gate at Center Hill Dam. This crucial effort is designed to improve the celebrated cold-water trout fishery’s habitat downstream on the Caney Fork River, attracting anglers from throughout the area.
12 Fun Facts About Center Hill Lake
Size: Center Hill Lake covers approximately 18,220 acres
Shoreline: The lake boasts about 415 miles of largely undeveloped shoreline.
Depth: It has a maximum depth of around 190 feet near the dam.
Dam: Center Hill Dam is an earthen dam, measuring 260 feet high and 1,382 feet long.
Water Source: The Caney Fork River is the main water source for the lake.
Fish Species: The lake is home to various fish species, including bass, crappie, and trout.
Parks: The lake is surrounded by several state parks and recreational areas, such as Edgar Evins State Park and Burgess Falls State Park.
Wildlife: The area around the lake is rich in wildlife, including deer, turkeys, and various bird species.
Water Quality: The lake is known for its clear, clean water, ideal for swimming and diving.
Historical Aspect: The area around Center Hill Lake is rich in history, with several sites dating back to early Native American and pioneer days.

Community Events: The lake area hosts various community events, including fishing tournaments and festivals.
#11
Management: The lake and dam are managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, ensuring their sustainable use and preservation.

TITLE: Boating Safety at Center Hill Lake | Center Hill Marina
Boating Safety
Lake Weather Safety Tips
Check the Weather Forecast
Always check the weather forecast before heading out. Look for signs of storms, strong winds, or other adverse conditions.
Use a reliable weather app or a marine radio to keep updated on changing weather conditions.
Understand Wind Patterns
High winds can create rough waters, making boating challenging and dangerous. Generally, winds over 15 knots (17 mph) can make conditions unsafe.
Know how to navigate depending on wind direction. It’s often safer to travel into the wind when returning to shore.
Recognize Weather Signs
An indicator of an approaching storm.
Often precede a storm.
Can signal incoming weather changes.
Safety Equipment
Ensure everyone on board wears a life jacket.
Include first-aid kit, flares, and a whistle.
Carry a fully charged mobile phone and a VHF radio.
Have an Emergency Plan
Inform someone on shore about your trip plan, including your expected return time.
Know the nearest safe harbors or sheltered areas where you can take cover if the weather turns bad.
Be Cautious of Fog
Fog reduces visibility significantly. Use sound signals and proceed slowly.
Use GPS and radar if available, and follow navigation buoys carefully.
Avoid Lightning
Boating during a thunderstorm is extremely dangerous due to lightning strikes.
If you see lightning or hear thunder, immediately head to the nearest safe shore.
Water Temperature Awareness
Even if the air temperature is warm, falling into cold water can lead to hypothermia.
Wear appropriate clothing and have dry clothes on board.
Sun Protection
Protect yourself from UV rays with sunscreen, hats, and sunglasses.
Bring plenty of water to stay hydrated.
Night Boating Precautions
Ensure your boat is equipped with proper navigation lights.
Reduce speed and be extra vigilant about other boats and obstacles.

The Smithville Fiddlers’ Jamboree and Crafts Festival is an annual Appalachian music, dance, and crafts celebration in Smithville, Tennessee. Since its establishment in 1972, the festival has become a significant cultural event, attracting musicians, artisans, and visitors worldwide.
The festival hosts contests in various categories, including old-time fiddle, bluegrass banjo, and Appalachian flatfoot dance, showcasing talented participants vying for top honors.
Attendees can explore handmade crafts—from woodwork and pottery to jewelry—showcased by artisans across the region.
A diverse selection of food booths offers local delicacies like homemade biscuits, barbecue, and sweet tea, while live performances provide continuous entertainment throughout the event.
1 Public Sq, Smithville, TN 37166
First Fridays in Smithville, Tennessee, are monthly events held in historic downtown Smithville on the first Friday of each month. These gatherings feature local artisans displaying handmade crafts and artworks for sale, live performances by local musicians, a variety of cuisines from food trucks and local eateries, and family-friendly activities such as face painting and street games that ensure enjoyment for all ages.
Events typically begin around 5:00 p.m. and continue into the evening in downtown Smithville, particularly on West Walnut Street and surrounding areas. Parking may be limited during popular events, so arriving early or carpooling is recommended.
This annual event transforms Walnut Street in Historic Downtown Smithville into a lively, pedestrian-friendly art fair each fall. The Art Walk highlights a diverse array of local artisans and craftspeople who exhibit their creations, including paintings, sculptures, woodwork, and other handcrafted items.
Live performances by local musicians add to the festive atmosphere, while food trucks and local eateries offer various dining options, ranging from Southern comfort food to international cuisines. Admission is free and open to the public.

First, what is it?
What is patch reef fishing, exactly?
A patch reef is a small, isolated head of living coral and hard bottom — usually the size of a car or a small house — surrounded by sand and turtle grass. There are hundreds of them scattered across the shallows between Key West and the main reef tract, sitting in . The fish hold tight to each patch. You drift or anchor up-current, drop a small bait on light spinning tackle, and watch the line.
The whole experience is the opposite of offshore sport fishing. There's no trolling at 8 knots. No fighting belt. No outriggers. No bouncing through chop for an hour to reach a spot. Most patches we fish are inside the reef line in protected water — one- to two-foot seas, often glass-flat. You can see the bottom. Sometimes you can see the fish before they take the bait.
It's . The bites come constantly when conditions are right, the captain handles all the seasonal-limit and size-limit math for you, and the pace is slow enough that someone in your group can be napping on the bow while you're fighting a yellowtail off the stern. That's the trip.
Why trip, and not offshore sport fishing?
Key West has world-class offshore sport fishing — marlin, sailfish, tuna, kingfish, mahi. We're not that. Here's why someone books our patch reef trip instead.
Not everyone in your group fishes
On a dedicated sport-fishing boat, four hours of trolling is brutal for anyone who isn't holding a rod. The Jeanneau has shade, a head, room to lounge, and a swim platform. Non-anglers swim and sun while anglers fish.
Constant action, not a long wait
Offshore is a marathon — long runs, fewer hookups, occasional fireworks. Patch-reef fishing is a steady drip of small-fish action: snapper, hogfish, grunts, all afternoon. Kids stay engaged. Beginners hook fish.
Half the cost, half the day
Full-day Key West sport-fishing trips run $1,500–$3,000+ for a boat. Our four-hour patch reef charter is $1,395 all-in, leaves the afternoon free, and still ends with a cooler of fish for dinner.
The lineup
What you'll catch on the Key West patch reefs
The bread-and-butter species. These are the eating fish locals actually target — small to medium, light-tackle-friendly, and excellent on the plate.
Yellowtail snapper
The Florida Keys signature snapper. Light fight, picky eater, one of the best-eating fish in the ocean. Caught on chum slicks over the patches.
Mangrove snapper
Smart, structure-hugging, surprisingly hard-fighting for their size. The most consistent bite on the patches year-round.
Mutton snapper
The trophy of the patch reef. Spookier, bigger, harder to fool. When one eats, the rod doubles.
Hogfish
The single best-eating fish in the Keys, full stop. Caught on shrimp on the bottom. Not legal year-round — the captain knows the season.
Grunts & porkfish
Constant action. Smaller, scrappier, great for kids. The fish that keep everyone hooking up between the better bites.
Cero mackerel & small grouper
The bonus fish. Cero blow up on a chum line; small groupers come off the bottom. Most groupers on the shallow patches are catch-and-release.
The Six Fins move: fish in the morning, sandbar or snorkel in the afternoon.
Most of our patch-reef bookings are actually combo days. You fish for two to three hours while the bite is on, then pull anchor, run ten minutes, and anchor at a hidden local sandbar or a swimmable reef. Half the day fishing, half the day floating. Everyone in the group ends up happy.
Tell the captain at the dock what your group wants. Want all-fishing, no swim? Done. Want one hour of fishing and three hours sandbar? Also done. We're a private boat — the day is yours to shape.

TITLE: Fun Family Things to do in Portland, Oregon | ISLAND STYLE CHARTERS | Boat Tour FAQ
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
YOU DON’T KNOW WHAT YOU DON’T KNOW! ASK US ANYTHING!
Can I bring my own food or drinks?
No. For legal reasons, outside food and drinks are prohibited on our .
Can I purchase food and drinks during the boat tour?
Yes! We have a variety of beer, wine & tropical ciders as well as other fun beverages and snacks for the kids.
What about bad weather?
We sail rain or shine! Palapa top is waterproof & covers most of the boat. On rainy days, bring a raincoat (No umbrellas please)! If for any reason the captain determines that a tour could be unsafe due to weather, etc. (i.e. lightning) we will make every effort to inform you at least one hour prior to your scheduled departure. If we cancel unexpectedly, you will receive a full refund.
Are tips included in the price?
No, but gratuities are always greatly appreciated! You’ll find a Square QR code and a cash jar near the bar if you want to show your appreciation for our crew!
How early should I arrive before my tour?
Please note the “Check-in” time on your confirmation email (30 minutes prior to the tour) and allow extra time for traffic and parking. Your confirmation email contains additional instructions about check-in/ arrival and departure.
To help speed up the check-in process, please take time to sign the online waiver in advance for yourself and any minor children.
Portland Visitors, please note: Expect traffic delays in and around downtown Portland, especially at rush hour!
Where does the boat tour start and end?
Our start at South Waterfront Park on the Willamette River in the heart of downtown Portland, Oregon.
Portland Boat tours
Please do not attempt to board the vessel early. Our staff will meet you at the park benches above the dock. Once everyone has been checked-in, our crew will escort the entire tour group to the boat.
Note: If you are using a ride-share app (Uber/Lift) make sure the driver checks the address once in route. Some Apps have a glitch that causes the address to change to “SW” vs. “S” River Drive.
Is there parking near the dock?
There are a couple public parking garages within a short walking distance from the embarkation dock as well as paid on-street parking. Download parking apps, like Parking Kitty, in advance for added convenience.
Is there a restroom on board?
We have a restroom on board, but encourage guests to also use the nearby public restroom before boarding (especially for kids!) and follow the “no solids” rule while on board.
What should I bring?
Bring a valid driver’s license if you plan to consume alcohol. We accept debit or credit cards for food and drink purchases. For tips (only) we also accept cash or square payments. Keep in mind, it can feel colder (or be sunnier) out on the water than on land. Sunglasses or a brimmed hat may come in handy. On chillier days and nights, consider bringing a beanie & a puffy (for all you non-Pacific Northwest natives, that’s a cozy hat & warm jacket!) or you may even want a personal blanket on colder, windy days.
Do I need to wear or bring a life jacket?
Our vessel is equipped with USCG-certified Type I PFDs (life vests) for all passengers, available for use in case of emergency. Adults are not required to wear lifejackets during the cruise, but you are welcome to bring your own USCG-approved lifejacket if it makes you more comfortable.
Oregon state law requires children under 12 to wear a lifejacket at all times while on board. We provide USCG-certified lifejackets for children, or you may bring your own. Parents are responsible for ensuring compliance with this regulation.
What if I’m running late?
Out of respect for timely passengers, we start all boat tours on time. If you are late you will miss the tour, forfeit your ticket and its cost.
Are all tickets the same price?
Tour prices vary depending on day, time, tour type and season. We offer a discount to senior citizens (62+), veterans and active military (ID required), and children’s tickets are reduced on select tours.
Are children allowed?

for great prices on children’s tickets! Our boat tours are one of the best fun family things to do in Portland, Oregon! These tours are set up to be more affordable and extra fun for the kiddos!
Do I have to buy a ticket for a baby if I hold them on my body or lap?
Yes. The Coast Guard counts every human or “soul” as part of the passenger count regardless of age and our capacity is limited. Therefore, you will need to purchase a ticket, provide the full name of your child or infant at check-in and sign a separate liability waiver on their behalf. On select tours children and infant prices are reduced. For legal reasons, lap infants are not permitted on our 21+ tours.

Dale’s love for watersports, boating, and sailing began at a young age. By eight, he was already taking friends, neighbors, and even new acquaintances out in the family powerboat on the lakes of Fort Worth, Texas. His early experiences naturally led him to become a sailing instructor and join the Coast Guard, charting a course for a lifetime of maritime adventures. In 1984, he followed his enthusiasm for windsurfing to the Columbia Gorge, where he settled down, raised two daughters, and grew his career in the maritime world.

But in early 2024, Captain Dale turned his attention toward a new direction—creating meaningful moments on the water closer to home with. Frequently asked questions
Is tandem paragliding safe?
Yes. We are USHPA certified and fully insured — the only paragliding school near Seattle that can say both. Our pilots have thousands of flights between them. Every flight follows strict FAA and USHPA safety protocols, and equipment is inspected before every flight.
Do I need any experience?
None at all. Tandem paragliding is designed for complete beginners. Your pilot handles the takeoff, flight, and landing. All you need to do is run a few steps on launch and enjoy the ride.
How long is the flight?
Flights last between 10 and 15 minutes depending on weather and thermal conditions. The total experience from arrival to landing is typically 2 hours.
Where exactly do you fly?
We launch from Poo Poo Point on Tiger Mountain in Issaquah, Washington — about 30 minutes east of downtown Seattle. We meet at the Poo Poo Point trailhead parking lot.
What if the weather is bad?
Safety comes first. If conditions aren't suitable for flying, we'll reschedule your flight at no extra charge. We monitor weather closely and will contact you in advance if we need to adjust.
Is there an age or weight limit?
We can fly anyone 15 years or older and 260lbs or lighter. This is based off equipment safety and FAA requirements. If you have specific concerns, call or email us and we'll let you know if we can accommodate you.
Can I take photos or video?
Absolutely. We recommend a secure phone strap or GoPro mount so you can capture the flight hands-free. Ask your pilot about video options at launch.
Do you offer group bookings?
Yes. Tandem paragliding is great for birthdays, bachelor/bachelorette parties, corporate outings, and other group celebrations. Contact us to coordinate scheduling.

=== PAGE: https://elkhornslough.com/cancellation-policy
TITLE: Elkhorn Slough Safari — Cancellation Policy
For parties of five or less, Elkhorn Slough Safari offers a convenient, 24-hour cancellation policy for reservations on our regular public tours. With at least 24 hours notice, customers have the option to receive a full refund, reschedule for another tour, or have their purchase transferred to a gift certificate.
For parties of 6 or more passengers, please call 3 or more days before the day your tour is scheduled to depart to receive a full refund, reschedule to another tour, or have your purchase transferred to a gift certificate.
For private charters, we require notice at least one week before the day your tour is scheduled to depart to cancel or reschedule. Full payment for charters must be received at least one week prior to launch to guarantee reservation.
To cancel a reservation and receive a full refund you must call our office and speak with a reservationist. No shows, and reservations for seats on public tours that are cancelled inside of your policy are not refundable, but can be rescheduled for a fee of $10 per reserved seat, or transferred to a gift certificate (minus the $10 per seat fee).
All guests 18+ are required to fill out an industry standard waiver form before departure. Refusal to do so will be considered a last minute cancellation, and no refund will be issued.
If you are booking on behalf of other adults, we kindly ask that you make them aware of our policies by forwarding this info to them, or directing them to our website.
For private charters we ask that you give at least 1 week’s notice for cancellations.
SCHEDULED TOURS WILL NOT DEPART WITH FEWER THAN SIX PASSENGERS
There are rare instances when we do not receive our required minimum of six reservations for a given tour. In these instances, the tour will be cancelled at least two hours in advance of the scheduled departure time, and we will reschedule you free of charge or refund you. If you are concerned about the status of your tour as the date approaches, feel free to call our office at (831) 633-5555 to speak with a representative.
CANCELLATIONS DUE TO WEATHER
Tours will depart at the discretion of the Captain, who will use all tools available to discern if conditions are suitable. As a policy, we err on the side of caution and will not subject our guests to unsafe or unreasonably uncomfortable conditions. We will not go out in heavy rain or wind, but light drizzle and mist is not grounds for us to cancel, and can actually offer exceptional wildlife viewing. Under such conditions we will provide tarps, blankets, and/or umbrellas to make our guests as comfortable as possible.
If we cancel due to weather, we will reschedule you free of charge or refund you. If the Captain decides that conditions are suitable and we depart as scheduled, our regular cancellation policy applies. (see above)
When weather forecasts suggest unsuitable conditions for morning tours scheduled to depart before 11AM, a decision to cancel will be made the afternoon before to accommodate guests who would have to begin their travels too early the next morning to be reached. In this event, every effort will be made to reach each person who has made a reservation for the cancelled tour by 4PM the day before. For this reason it is very important that you provide us with a phone number and e-mail address that you will be attentive to.
Elkhorn Slough Safari is not responsible for inconveniences caused by unanswered phone calls, and unchecked e-mails and voicemails. If you do not receive a phone call or e-mail within two hours of your scheduled departure time, assume that your tour is departing as scheduled.

ALASKA WILDLIFE
What wildlife can be found in Prince William Sound?
Sea otters, harbor seals, Steller sea lions, Dall’s porpoise, 200 different species of birds, including Eagles, black-legged kittiwakes, glaucous-winged gulls, oystercatchers, storm petrels, Jaeger’s, arctic terns, marbled murrelets, pigeon guillemots, arctic loons, Arctic warblers, Pacific loons, red-faced cormorants, bluethroats, surf scooters and on a rare occasion a puffin makes its way into Prince William Sound.
Is this a whale-watching cruise?
We see a variety of wildlife including orcas (killer whales) and humpback whales. Whales are not guaranteed, but we do see them 50-60% of the time.
When is the best time to see whales?
Whales are more often in May, June, and September when they are migrating to and from California and Hawaii. For a full list of the wildlife we see, please visit our
Wildlife page.
Glacier Cruise Questions
The Captain and our crew will provide narration and point out key areas of interest along our routes. Together, they will share the history, explain the geography, provide facts about the glaciers and wildlife encountered during the cruise. Due to the combination of our stable catamarans and the calm, protected waters of Prince William Sound, we guarantee a trip without seasickness or your money back. If you are concerned about motion sickness in the least, we are the choice for you!
is 5.25 hours and covers 120 miles round-trip through the glacier-filled fjords in Prince William Sound. We use our fastest high-speed catamarans that travel at 30-34 knots per hour on this route. Both M/V Klondike Express, M/V Bravest, and M/V Chugach Express are used on this cruise so if you are traveling with friends on multiple reservations, let us know at the time of booking so we can make sure you are on the same boat and sitting together.
The 26 Glacier Cruise
travels 45 miles round-trip to Blackstone Bay. This tour is operated on our M/V Glacier Quest which cruises at 19 knots allowing us to take in the views on our way to the glaciers. On occasion, the M/V Chugach Express or M/V Bravest may be used on this tour in place of the M/V Glacier Quest.
The Glacier Quest Cruise
We spend time in front of several tidewater glaciers on each cruise. The captain will stop for wildlife sightings along the way at the kittiwake rookery and other scenic areas along each route.
No, we do not stop where our guests would step off the vessel during the tour.
Many guests will be interested in touching the glacier ice. We will provide some glacier ice on display, and our bartender will also prepare some glacier ice that you may put in your drink to enjoy.
We recommend you dress in layers. That way, you can adjust the layers as the weather requires. Bring a waterproof or windproof jacket, rubber-soled shoes, gloves, and a hat. The vessel moves quickly across the water, which will cause a wind chill factor, especially if you are on the outside decks when we are underway. The interior of the vessel is heated and comfortable.
The average temperature of the water is only 42’F.
The Chugach National Forest is the most northern and western rain forest in the United Stated, so rain is certainly possible. We cruise rain or shine. Photographers prefer cloudy days because the blues of the glaciers are more intense in overcast conditions.
We cruise rain or shine unless the Coast Guard advises that we cancel due to weather. The weather frequently changes in Alaska, and we travel quite a distance on our cruises. If the weather is rainy at the pier as you are boarding the vessel, do not worry. The weather will change once you exit Passage Canal and cruise towards the glaciers.
Meal Service Questions:
What does the meal include, and when is it served? We serve a hot meal for each Adult and Child 2-11 shortly after your cruise leaves the harbor. A meal is not included for infants 0-24 months.
The most popular meal choice is our delicious wild Alaska smoked salmon chowder. If you prefer a vegetarian option, we offer a hearty vegetarian chili. Your complimentary meal also includes oyster crackers, a fresh Julienne vegetable salad, a multi-grain roll, a cheese stick, and a fruit snack. If you require a gluten-free meal, you will be pleased to know that our chili is Gluten-free. Please confirm the lunch choice when you make your reservation.
Young cruisers age 2-11 may have chowder, chili, or choose our kids’ meal that features an all-beef hot dog, a bag of sun chips, and a fruit snack. Occasionally we have a few adults choose this option too. Please keep in mind that the portion sizes were designed for kids.
Due to our remote location, we request your meal choice at the time of booking. Any meal changes must be confirmed at least 24 hours before your cruise departure.
We offer a Vegetarian option featuring a hearty vegetarian chili. Guests with special dietary needs or traveling with an infant are welcome to bring meals or snacks. If you have allergies or questions about the ingredients, you may consult our and our .
We provide complimentary hot tea, coffee, and ice water throughout the cruise.
We have a full-service bar with alcoholic beverages, snacks including trail mix, bison hotdogs, nacho chips, movie theater size candy, and small gift shop items available for purchase. Try our very own Glacier Ice Margarita with ice from the glaciers in Prince William Sound. Warm-up with our signature hot drinks, the Klondike Coffee or Polar Smooch hot chocolate. The M/V Glacier Quest travels at a cruising speed of 18 knots, 23 miles per hour.

The M/V Glacier Quest has higher thresholds best navigated by walking short distances or stepping over raised points. The vessel has multiple restrooms on the main deck, with one accessible restroom on the aft starboard side.

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

Our premium half-day charter — built for families and groups who want both the thrills and the relaxation in one trip. Two hours of water sports behind a USCG-licensed captain, two hours cruising the back bays of Seven Mile Island, plus 45 minutes at our aqua park for the kids. Available in two sizes: Small Group ($950, up to 6 guests, full water sports menu) and Large Group ($1,350, up to 22 guests, tubing only). It’s the boat day you actually wanted, without piecing it together.
Not at all. Book the package, show up, tell your captain what your group feels like doing. Want to hit water sports first thing while everyone’s fresh, then relax for the cruise? Easy. Want to cruise to a spot down the bay first and do water sports there? Also easy. Want to start with the aqua park to wear the kids out before they get on the boat? Done. The structure is the structure — 2 hours water sports, 2 hours cruise, 45 minutes aqua park — but the order and pace are up to your group.
Two hours of water sports, two hours of cruising, with 45 minutes at the aqua park happening before or after the boat trip — your call on timing, same day. The cruise portion is part of the experience, not an add-on you can skip. That’s how it’s built. If you want straight water sports with no cruise, book a 4-hour Half Day on the ski boat product instead.
Small Group ($950, up to 6 guests): Full water sports menu — tubing, wakeboarding, water skiing. Best for one family or a tight group of 6 who want the complete package. Large Group ($1,350, up to 22 guests): Tubing only — two couch-style tubes, three riders each. No wakeboarding or skiing on this package (the boat is built for groups, not towing single riders). Both packages include 2 hours of water sports time, 2 hours of cruising, and 45 minutes at the aqua park.

The 2-hour cruise is part of the package, and we don’t shorten it or swap it out for more water sports. If your group wants 4 hours of water sports with no cruise, book the 4-hour Half Day on the ski boat product instead — that’s what it’s built for.
No. Plenty of TCWE bookings have one or two adults who never get on a tube and don’t want to. The aqua park time is built for the kids in your group — they can come early or stay after the boat trip. Six years old. All participants need to be comfortable in the water and able to wear a life jacket. The park is physical — kids are climbing, jumping, and running across inflatables — so we hold the 6+ rule firm to keep everyone safe.

Stories of Lightships and Their Sailors
Discover the fascinating history of America’s lightships and the sailors who served aboard them. Historian John Bolster explores the many lightships that once marked the entrance to Delaware Bay, sharing stories of daily life, dangerous storms, and the men whose courage kept mariners safe. Bolster serves on the board of the Overfalls Foundation and is curator of the Overfalls Lightship Museum, offering a unique perspective on one of Lewes’ most treasured maritime landmarks.

Our Mission
The mission of the Overfalls Foundation is to preserve, teach and honor the lightships and their sailors of the United States and the maritime history of our community through the preservation and display of the Lightship Overfalls (LV-118) and its collection of associated maritime artifacts.

Built in 1938 for the U.S. Lighthouse Service, the LV-118 was decommissioned by the U.S. Coast Guard in 1972 and has been in Lewes, Delaware since 1973. LV-118, renamed Overfalls in honor of the Overfalls Shoals lightship station located nearby and the American lightship sailors that served there, is now preserved, maintained and operated by a dedicated team of volunteers.Come visit our facilities and learn the story of how the ship went from near ruin to becoming a National Historic Landmark worthy of ship tours and public events. You will hear about the roles lightships played in American history and see what life aboard a lightship was like. We’ll introduce you to the Delaware Maritime Hall of Fame, explain what a Monomoy is and show you several life-size aids to navigation.Don’t forget to visit the Ship Store and American Lightship Museum where you can learn more about the history of lightships and purchase ship related clothing, jewelry, original artwork, books, maps, and other items.
The Ship, Ship Store and Museum are open for the season. See our Events listing below for special openings during the season.

[top]
California Boating Laws, as well as Los Angeles County Ordinances covering boating apply and are enforced.
All applicable Fish and Game regulations apply and are enforced.
Appropriate launch permit fees apply.
Possession of a valid launch permits is required for all boats.
Watercraft may be launched from the Lagoon or Main Reservoir designated areas ONLY! Launching any kind of vessel from the campgrounds is prohibited.
All boats must have "CF" numbers on the front bow, valid registration and all safety equipment in order to launch.
All boats are subject to inspection for safety equipment.
All boats are required by law to contain one Coast Guard approved wearable life vest per person PLUS one throwable cushion for boats 16' or over.
All fuel-powered vessels must have a fire extinguisher, including personal watercrafts.
Children 12 years of age and younger must wear a Coast Guard approved personal flotation device (PFD).
Vessel operators must be at least 16 years of age.
Lake speed limits: Maximum speed limit is 35 MPH. Coves and launch ramp areas are 5 MPH. Refer to map.
CONSUMPTION OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES IS PROHIBITED. L.A. Co. Ord. 17.04.440
Possession of any type of firearm is prohibited.
Please prepare vessel in the upper parking lot. Park in designated boat/trailer areas ONLY.
Launch and retrieve vessels from designated areas.
All vessels, other than Personal Watercraft (PWC) are to stay out of special use areas.
Tying to a buoy from a boat is prohibited.
Castaic Lake is a drinking water reservoir. FUELING OF ANY VESSEL ON THE WATER IS PROHIBITED.
All boats must travel in a COUNTER CLOCKWISE direction.
Water Skiing and Wakeboarding are restricted to designated areas.
(See map)
Ski boats must travel in a COUNTER CLOCKWISE direction.
Maximum of two persons at a time may be towed behind vessel (if tube is designed for 2 people). Only one tow line and one tow device per vessel.
All boats towing a skier shall have an OBSERVER not less than 12 years of age.
Red ski flags must be used to indicate a skier, rope,or ski gear is in the water (according to the "ABC's" of CA Boating law).
Personal Water
crafts
Personal Watercraft may only carry the number of passengers for which it is manufactured.
Personal Watercraft may not tow anything, including a skier, inner tube, etc.
Personal Watercraft are restricted to the special PWC area of the lake and must travel in a COUNTER CLOCKWISE ROTATION.
Passing too close to other vessels can be dangerous at any speed. PWC operators must keep a distance of 25 feet from any other vessel while underway.
The owner of any Personal Watercraft is responsible for the actions of anyone who uses his vessel.
Castaic Lake is a drinking water reservoir. FUELING OF ANY VESSEL ON THE WATER IS PROHIBITED. FUELING OF PERSONAL WATERCRAFT IS TO TAKE PLACE OUT OF THE WATER.
Immediately upon launching, all PWCs must proceed directly to the special use area at a speed of 5 MPH.
Fuel must be stored in the designated fuel area only.
VESSEL OPERATORS MUST BE AT LEAST 16 YEARS OF AGE.
Any vessel launching on Lagoon waters, must be powered by hand, sail, or electric trolling motors.
Gasoline powered engines are not to be used on Lagoon waters. Engine must be tilted up when the vessel is on Lagoon waters.
Wind surfers may carry no more than one person.
All float tubes require launch permits, which should be displayed in a manner similar to fishing licenses.
All persons in float tubes must wear a U.S. Coast Guard approved Personal Floatation Devices (PFD’s) at all times.
Use of float tubes is restricted to the Castaic Lake Lagoon.
Whistles or other sound signaling devices, while not required, ARE STRONGLY RECOMMENDED.
A 12” x 12” orange square is required on the back of the float tube.
SWIMMING IS PROHIBITED, EXCEPT IN DESIGNATED AREAS, ONLY WHEN A LIFEGUARD IS ON DUTY. Beaches are open FOR SWIMMING on a seasonal basis only.
Always watch your children when they are in or near the water.
Report a lost child immediately to the lifeguard on duty.
Animals must be on leashes. No animals are allowed in the water or on the beach.
(top)
ONLY RIDE ON OPEN TRAILS.
Remove all trash and protect natural areas.
Maintain control of your pet animals and/or bicycles at all times.
Always yield the trail where appropriate.
Never scare or harass animals.
Use of off-road vehicles (ATV's, Motocross bikes or go-carts) on the trails is PROHIBITED.
All safety equipment recommended for the sport must be worn at all times. This includes wearing a protective helmet.
USE OF COUNTY MAINTAINED TRAILS IS AT THE RISK AND RESPONSIBILITY OF THE INDIVIDUAL.
All California Fish and Game regulations are strictly enforced.
All fishermen MUST have a valid fishing license if 16 years or older (additional rods require stamps).
Fishing in coves "Closed for spawning" is prohibited.
Cleaning of fish on the water or shoreline is strictly prohibited.
Live bait can only be used if caught in the same day and location.
Trolling in the Main Reservoir ski area is NOT permitted.

A California department of Fish and Game permit covering the date of the tournament must be forwarded to the Administration office for our files.
Only organized fishing clubs are allowed overnight (no family or commercial use).

=== PAGE: https://www.castaiclake.com/moonlight-madness
TITLE: Moonlight Madness | Friends of Castaic L
September 26 Registration
Join us for an unforgettable night of fishing under the stars!​
​Friends of Castaic Lake invites you to Moonlight Madness, a unique nighttime fishing event at beautiful Castaic Lake.
Whether you’re fishing from shore or launching your boat, you’ll enjoy an evening on the water with fellow anglers while supporting Friends of Castaic Lake and our mission to enhance and preserve the lake for everyone.
A HUGE THANK YOU TO OUR 2026 EVENT SPONSORS
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Moonlight Madness is a nighttime boating and fishing event at Castaic Lake where participants can enjoy an evening on the water under the stars. Whether you’re fishing, cruising, or simply relaxing with family and friends, it’s a unique summer experience. This special event is a fundraiser hosted by Friends of Castaic Lake (FOCL) to support community programs, events, volunteer efforts, and projects that benefit Castaic Lake and its visitors.
Q: Is pre-registration required?
A: No—pre-registration is not required, but preferred.​
Q: Why is pre-registration preferred?
A: It helps plan for the event, speeds up check-in, and helps participants not miss event giveaways.
Q: Is walk-up registration available?
A: Yes—walk-up registration is available beginning at 6:30 PM.
Q: What payment methods are accepted?
A: Credit/debit card and cash.
Q: Do Annual Lake Passes or County Passes cover this event?
A: No—admission is separate from regular lake access.
Q: What will I receive at check-in?
A: Vehicle ribbon and Event information and safety instructions
Q: Is a light stick required?
A: Yes—every participant is required to have a light stick.
Why: Light sticks help Lake Lifeguards, event staff, volunteers, and other boaters identify participants and improve visibility during nighttime operations.
Available: Light sticks are available for purchase from Friends of Castaic Lake at check-in, and participants must have one before participating.
Q: What must my boat have?
A: All boats must meet California boating regulations and pass a Lake Lifeguard safety inspection before entering the water.
Current boat registration.
One Type III U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device (life jacket) of proper size for every person on board.
A Type IV throwable flotation device (required for boats 16 feet or longer).
Proper navigation lights (front and back) for nighttime operation.
A sound-producing device (horn or whistle).
Required event light stick for each participant (available for purchase from Friends of Castaic Lake at check-in).
A fire extinguisher if required for your vessel.
Q: Will boats be inspected?
A: Yes. Boats may be inspected for required safety equipment, operational safety, and compliance with boating regulations. Any vessel that does not pass the required safety inspection may be denied entry onto the water.
Q: Do we need life jackets on board?
A: Yes. Every person aboard must have a properly fitting U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket available while aboard the vessel.​
Q: Do kids have to wear one?
A: Yes. Children 12 years old and younger must wear a properly fitted and secured life jacket at all times while aboard the vessel.
Q: What are the key lake rules during the event?
The speed limit during Moonlight Madness is 5 MPH.
Please obey all posted lake rules and No Wake zones.
For everyone’s safety, maintain a proper lookout at all times.
Operate your vessel carefully due to limited nighttime visibility.
Maintain a safe distance from other vessels, shorelines, docks, and restricted areas.
Follow all directions from Lake Lifeguards, park staff, event staff, and volunteers.
Towing activities are not permitted during Moonlight Madness.
Boats may anchor in appropriate areas while allowing plenty of room for other participants.
Q: What’s required after sunset?
A: Boats operating after sunset must display proper navigation lights.
Q: Is alcohol permitted?
A: No. Alcohol is not permitted at Castaic Lake. Boat operators must remain sober and comply with all California boating laws.
Q: What if my boat breaks down?
A: Contact event staff or Lake Lifeguards immediately if you need assistance. The Lake Lifeguard emergency contact number will be provided during the safety inspection and included on the information handout provided at check-in.
Q: Do I need a fishing license?
A: Yes—anyone 16 years of age or older who is fishing must possess a valid California fishing license.
Q: What rules apply?
A: All current California Department of Fish and Wildlife regulations must be followed, including:
Size limits
Bag limits
Legal fishing methods
Catch and release requirements
Q: How do I dispose of fishing waste?
A: Participants are responsible for properly disposing of fishing line, hooks, bait, and other waste.
Q: Are kayaks allowed?
A: Yes
kayaks 8 feet or longer are welcome to participate, including inflatable kayaks, as long as they meet the safety requirements.
For a nighttime event, you’ll need: • A red/green bow light • A 360° white stern light • A U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket for each person on board
Q: Are
paddle boards
allowed?
A: No, paddle boards are not permitted on the upper lake.
Q: Is Moonlight Madness family-friendly?
A: Absolutely—Moonlight Madness is a family-friendly event.
Q: Can more than one person be on my boat?
A: Yes. Please make sure your boat does not exceed its legal passenger capacity and that there is a properly fitted life jacket available for everyone on board.
Q: Are dogs allowed?
A: Friendly dogs are welcome aboard your boat. Please keep pets under control at all times and clean up after them.
Q: Will the event still happen if the weather changes?
A: The event will proceed as scheduled unless weather, water conditions, visibility, or other safety concerns require changes.
Friends of Castaic Lake and Lake Lifeguards reserve the right to delay, modify, suspend, or cancel the event if conditions become unsafe.
Q: Where will updates be shared?
A: Any updates will be communicated through Friends of Castaic Lake social media and email to registered participants.
Q: Do I have to fish?
A: No—fishing is optional and many participants simply enjoy a peaceful evening boat ride under the stars.
Q: Who can I contact if I have questions?
A: Friends of Castaic Lake
Facebook: Friends of Castaic Lake

Fishing gear (if you plan to fish)
Life jackets for everyone on board
Light jacket or sweatshirt—even summer nights can cool down
Plenty of water
Snacks or a picnic dinner
Flashlight or headlamp
Bug spray
Fully charged phone
Prohibited Items
Fireworks
Open campfires
Glass containers
Illegal substances
Reckless or unsafe boating behavior

Check-in begins at 6:30 PM
Water entry begins at 7:30 PM or when lifeguards clear the lake
All boats must be off the water by 12:30 AM
Navigation lights are required after sunset
Make sure everyone has a properly fitted life jacket
A valid California fishing license is required for anyone age 16 or older who is fishing
Follow all lake rules and directions from park staff, Lake Lifeguards, and event volunteers

TITLE: Absolute Flight
aviation is our passion
Utah is our playground
Absolute Flight is Utah’s #1 rated backcountry flight service on Google!
Our Story
At Absolute Flight, we believe that exceptional aviation requires more than just hours in a logbook—it demands a legacy of discipline, adaptability, and mastery.
Absolute Flight was founded by Neil Amonson, an Air Force Special Operations veteran with over 23 years of aviation experience. Rooted in a background of high-performance aviation, leadership under pressure, and mission-driven execution, Neil transitioned his tactical expertise into the civilian world to create a premier flight service built on uncompromising standards.
His pursuit of aerial mastery extends far beyond the cockpit. Holding a Bachelor’s degree from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, Neil is also a former professional athlete for GoPro, where he spent years combining elite athletic performance with global brand storytelling. As an instructor in skydiving, paragliding, and wingsuiting, his understanding of the air is total, fluid, and applied.
Absolute Flight was built to bring this rare blend of military precision, academic foundation, and extreme-environment experience to our clients. From remote backcountry access to professional air taxi operations, we execute every mission with the highest level of professionalism and skill.
A DESTINATION
Absolute Flight is Utah's premier backcountry flight service! Located one hour from the stunning red rock cliffs of Mexican Mountain and two hours from the grassy meadows of Smiley Creek. We are the epicenter of the best backcountry flying in the lower 48.
To fly with us is to experience a type of flying most people only dream about. Featuring the natural beauty of the American West, seen from one of the best tools for backcountry exploration, a bush plane.
“Keep close to Nature’s heart… and break clear away, once in a while, and climb a mountain or spend a week in the woods. Wash your spirit clean.” –John Muir
No matter how big or small your flying goals, we have an option for you.
Road trips not exciting enough for you? We now offering regular flights to Wendover, Zion, Bryce Canyon, Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef and Dutch John! Want something more adventurous? We can arrange customized backcountry airplane camping trips! Send us a message with your vision and we will be your flying concierge.
AIR TAXI
Learn the fundamentals of flying a conventional gear aircraft and receive your FAA tailwheel endorsement. TAILWHEEL ENDORSEMENTS

SCENIC TOURS

HIGH PERFORMANCE ENDORSEMENTS

FLIGHT TRAINING
SAFETY PILOT SERVICES

our AIRCRAFT
CESSNA 170B
What is a bush plane? Usually a combination of things. Some of the more important features would be good prop clearance to avoid obstacles on the ground, enough horsepower to make short take-offs and steeps climbs, a STOL kit on the wing to land and take off at slow speeds, and big tires for rough strips. Our 1953 Cessna 170B has all of those things and more.
CESSNA 182B
The early 182 models have a great reputation for being light on the controls and having excellent performance. Our 182 has an upgraded Northpoint XP 470 engine conversion, an MT Propeller, 850 x 10 main tires and an oversized airglass fork, sportsman STOL cuff with VGs and many more mods. There are not many places this nose dragger can't go!

TITLE: Urbanna Town Council
Instructions
Fill out the attached application and submit it to the Town Office located at 300 Virginia Street – or mail it to P.O. Box 179 Urbanna Virginia. If acceptable a permit will be mailed back to the address of the Owner / Agent listed on the application. The short term rental permit is be valid for one year from the date of issuance and must be renewed annually prior to the expiration date. A permit fee of twenty five dollars ($25.00) must accompany the application and subsequent renewal applications.
Restrictions and Requirements you need to remember:
The number of adult (18 years old or older) guests residing in a short-term rental unit shall not exceed the number of permanent bed spaces in the unit. Children under 18 years of age may be accommodated using cots or sleep sofas in common areas and shall not exceed a maximum of four (4) children.
Adequate off street parking for guests must be provided. There shall be a minimum of one parking space per bedroom. If such parking cannot be provided on site, the owner must submit a parking plan indicating how the parking requirement will be met. No on street parking shall be a part of the plan nor is it allowed.
A short term rental shall have no more than two (2) rental contracts during any consecutive seven (7) day period and shall be limited to operating one structure per property.
Interconnected smoke detectors, a fire extinguisher and, where propane is present, carbon monoxide detectors must be installed.
There shall be no outdoor amplified sounds after 10:00 PM or before 10:00 AM
The owner/Agent must post in a conspicuous place within the rental unit a summary of the pertinent town ordinances, a copy of the parking plan if any, trash and waste pick up schedules and emergency telephone numbers, as well as any additional rules the owner/agent has for the tenants.
The owner or agent is responsible for obtaining a form and paying the to the Town of Urbanna. Additionally the owner or agent shall maintain a registry showing the names, addresses and telephone numbers of all short term rental occupants. The owner/agent must allow the zoning administrator and his/her designee to inspect such registry upon reasonable advanced notice, to verify that the short term rental is being operated in accordance with the all the provisions of the Code of Urbanna.

TITLE: Urbanna Museum In The Street Walking Tour
Take a walking tour to discover Urbanna's rich history. You'll learn how Urbanna's deep natural harbor allowed European merchants to dock their ships and trade their goods for tobacco. In the early 1900's steam ships were a common site in the harbor.
We invite you to take a pleasant stroll around our coummunity to learn more about this facinating small town.
The Urbanna Virtual Museum Tour
The virtual museum tour in Urbanna utilizes YouTube videos to enhance your experience. Larry Chowning, town historian, will amaze you with never-before-seen photos that were too grainy to fit in any of his books.
There are currently 18 historical markers around town. Simply scan the QR code with your phone to begin viewing the video for that marker. Please pick up a brochure at the town office, the local library, or the Town of Urbanna Museum.
The virtual walking tour is FREE. It truly is remarkable. See Urbanna’s three-hundred-year history come to life!
Start your tour at the first historical marker located on the Cross Street side of R.S. Bristow’s Store on the corner of Virginia Street and Cross Street.

=== PAGE: https://mvminnow.com/faq/
TITLE: FAQ | M/V Minnow
Where should I park?
Island wide, parking can always be a challenge. We recommend guests arrive 30 minutes before their tours during high season or use our free trolley system which stops right at Bridge Street.
Will I feel seasick?
Almost certainly not! Even people who claim to be very susceptible to seasickness don’t have issues on our boat. We use a very stable pontoon boat and the waters we are in are generally calm. If for some reason you do feel sick we can take you back to land but we are confident that won’t happen.
What is your cancellation policy?
Requests to reschedule your reservation must be made at least 24 hours before your charter is scheduled. Please note, cancellations or changes may only be made by phone. Email, Voicemail, Text, or otherwise is not acceptable to change an existing booking.
Will we see dolphins?
We see dolphins approximately 99% of the time so we hope you do on your tour. We always see some sort of wildlife whether it’s dolphins, manatees, rays, fish, birds etc. If you don’t see dolphins on your tour we will do our best to accommodate you on another tour free of charge!
How many guests can you carry?
Our capacity is 30 passengers and 2 crew, this includes infants and children under 3.
Is there shade on the boat?
All 30 passengers on board the vessel can sit in padded and covered seating.
Are there bathrooms onboard?
Yes, we do have a marine head (bathroom).
Can we bring food & drinks?
Yes, you are welcome to bring food and drinks including beer, wine, and liquor. We always recommend you check out AMOB on the Pier!
Is the boat handicap accessible?
We can accommodate most people. Access to the boat is by low angle ramps and short steps. Please inform us ahead of time if you or a member of your party has mobility issues and we will make sure we can accommodate them.
Is the tour family-friendly?
Absolutely! We take pride in making all our tours fun for passengers of all ages. Kids get to wear Captain’s hat and sit at the helm under the supervision of the Captain. It makes for great pictures and the kids love it!
Do I need to make reservations?
We prefer if you do but walk-ons are always welcome provided we have the room. To book online click here.
Other Questions?
Ask us anything

TITLE: Golf Cart FAQs | Ocean Atlantic Rentals - Outer Banks Beach Rentals
$25 OFF ORDERS $149+
Which cart type for where I am staying?
Please refer to the map on the main page to determine which golf cart is allowed in what areas. Please note that golf carts and LSVs may not be permitted in some communities.
When in doubt, our staff can advise you on which communities allow golf carts. We will do our best to get you in the right cart, but we are not responsible for changes made by NCDOT, homeowners associations, and state and local governments.
You may also refer to the map provided by Dare County regarding
legal roadways for community golf carts and LSVs here.
What are the main things I need to know about renting a LSV golf cart?
LSV’s (low speed vehicle golf carts) are legal on any NC public road with a speed limit under 35 mph. (Some private communities have chosen to exclude them.)
LSV’s carry a registration and license plate and must be operated by a licensed driver (21yrs & older) with valid auto insurance.
LSV golf carts CAN drive at night unlike standard golf carts which are not usable after sunset.
Remember, no motor vehicles may be used on sidewalks, or multi-purpose trails in Dare & Currituck counties.
If you wish to explore around the town you are staying in, an LSV cart is recommended.
View our 4 person LSV golf cart video is here.
View our 6 person LSV golf cart video is here.
What are the main things I need to know about renting a standard golf cart?
Our standard golf carts include headlights, taillights, and turn signals, and safety belts. Many vendors do not offer these safety features.
You must be 18 years old with valid drivers’ license to operate a Standard Golf Cart.
Many OBX communities allow standard golf carts in housing subdivisions (for use to getting to/from the beach, ONLY).
Standard golf carts are NOT legal on NC12, Hwy 158 or other state roads.
A standard golf cart is not a street legal cart, and can be ticketed by law enforcement if used on a public road.
Standard golf carts cannot be used after sunset.
If you wish to go to the beach access only or around your neighborhood, a Standard cart is recommended.
Is delivery service available?
Yes, delivery is available in most areas for a $50 fee. The cart will be delivered on check-in day, before 8pm. It will be picked up (early morning) of your departure date and must be clean and fully charged to avoid an additional $50 fee.
Express delivery is not available for golf carts.
Is the LSV or Standard Golf Cart electric or gas powered?
They are all 100% electric powered and include a power cord to recharge the cart after each use. They use a standard outlet to plug into for recharging.
What is the speed, power of these carts?
The LSV is powered by an electric 48-volt power-train, with a max speed of 25mph. LSV’s will travel up to 30 miles on a single, full charge. Range will vary depending on speed, cargo, etc. We encourage you to recharge the cart whenever not in use. It should be charged every night, overnight. We require the carts to be 100% charged at the end of your rental to avoid a $75 fee. The cart has a charge level indicator on the dashboard.
Standard golf carts have a 48-volt power-train, with a max speed of 19mph. Standard carts will travel up to 30 miles on a single, full charge. Range will vary depending on speed, cargo, etc. We encourage you to recharge the cart whenever not in use. It should be charged every night, overnight. We require the carts to be 100% charged at the end of your rental to avoid a $75 fee. The cart has a charge level indicator on the dashboard.
What are additional features of the carts?
A canopy covers the top of the cart. 4 cup-holders are built in. The onboard charger plugs into a standard outlet to recharge the batteries; the instrument panel has a warning light to warn of low battery charge. Extension power cord is provided with rental. The ignition uses a key to operate, like a car. There is a parking brake.
Can the Standard golf carts or LSV’s be driven on the beach or off-road?
No, ALL CARTS must be operated on paved roadways, only. You can be ticketed for improper use of a golf cart or low speed vehicle. Failure to comply with safe driving practices & OAR policies may result in termination of rental with no refund.
Where can I park my golf cart or LSV?
Can I drive golf cart or LSV on a bike trail or sidewalk?
No cart can be driven on a bike trail or sidewalk.
What is my responsibility for the golf cart or LSV, while in my possession?
The responsibility is the same as a rental car, or any other rental item. The registered driver/lessee is responsible for any damage or neglect to the vehicle, while in your possession. Charges apply for any damage. Photos of the vehicle condition (just like a car rental) will be completed at your time of possession, and upon return.
We require the carts to be 100% charged at the end of your rental to avoid a $75 fee. The cart has a charge level indicator on the dashboard.
OAR does not permit the use of child/baby car seats in our golf carts.
All motor vehicle laws apply to low speed vehicles, including open-container and D.U.I ordinances. Same laws and rules as a car/auto apply to an LSV.

=== PAGE: https://marinaatholdenbeach.com/frequently-asked-questions/
TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions - Holden Beach Marina
Frequently Asked Questions
General Questions
Do you have boat launch facilities at the marina?
There is no ramp at marina, but NC Wildlife boat ramp is located directly across the waterway from the marina, underneath the bridge on the island.
Do you offer fuel at the marina?
We offer convenient, from-the-water fueling with both
90 octane Non-ethanol gas on Pump 3 and 4, and Off-Road Diesel on Pump 1. You can only get Diesel from the Diesel slip that is located directly beside the launch pad. You can get non-ethanol on the gas dock right at the bridge or any slip in front of the marina building. Walk up the ramp to the gas pump and push the intercom button for service. Pump will not start until turned on upstairs. Come upstairs to pay after fueling. NOTE: We do not offer fuel from land at Holden Beach Marina.
How long does it take to get to the open ocean from your marina?
Lockwood Folly Inlet is located at the east end of Holden Beach about a mile from the marina and Shallotte Inlet is located at the west end of Holden Beach approximately 11 miles from the marina.
Is there free parking?
Yes. We offer free parking at Holden Beach Marina for our guests.
Can I fish off your docks?
No. Fishing is not allowed from our docks. You can fish from our parking lot directly under the bridge. Be courteous and watch for boat traffic.
Can we drink alcohol at the marina?
Yes. We have our on-premises permit and serve draft beer, beer/malt beverages by the can, and wine slushies upstairs in the Ship’s Store. You can sit out on the deck or down at the picnic tables to enjoy. Please do not drink and drive.
Is your marina/gift shop open to the general public?
Yes! Please come in to use restrooms, drink a beverage, or buy some merchandise. The store is open to the public, even if you do not have a boat!
Rental Questions
Do I need a Boater's License to Rent a Boat or Jet Ski?
For Jet Skis: You must be 21 years old+ and have a valid car driver’s license to be the signed Renter for your jet ski rental. To drive the jet ski, you must be 18 years old+ and have a valid car driver’s license. You must bring your valid driver’s license to your rental. You DO NOT need a boater’s license.
For Boats: You must be 25 years old+ and have a valid car driver’s license to be the signed Renter for our boat rentals. To drive the boat, you must be 21 years old+ and have a valid car driver’s license. You must bring your valid driver’s license to your rental. You DO NOT need a boater’s license. Some boater’s experience is required. Please do not rent if you have never driven a boat before or do not have someone in your party over 21 that has.
What is the minimum age limit to be a passenger on a jet ski?
Passengers must be at least 5 years old, and their feet must reach the floor. If any passenger on a PWC is under 18 years of age, the driver of the PWC must be 21 years of age or older. Any participant under 18-year-old (minors), must have a legal parent/guardian present (with ID) at the beginning of the rental to verify signing of legal document. If a parent or guardian cannot be present, you must provide a notarized power of attorney giving an adult in your party (with ID) the legal right to sign for the minor.
How many people can ride on a jet ski?
Do I need to be able to swim to rent a jet ski?
All participants must be able to swim and climb aboard the jet ski from the water on to the back of the jet ski safely. You must be able to lift your own weight out of the water.
Can I keep the boat at our rental home during multiple day rentals?
Yes, IF you are staying at a home on a canal. If not, the boat has to be back at the marina 30 minutes before sunset or earlier and can be picked back up 30 minutes before sunrise or later the next morning.
If I rent a boat for multiple days, can I have the boat out at sunset/sunrise?
Boating is not allowed when dark! For safety, our boats are not allowed out from 30 minutes before sunset through 30 minutes after sunrise. No exceptions! HOWEVER, if you wanted to enjoy a on the Intercoastal while in Holden Beach, we do offer a 3-hour sunset cruise aboard a luxury Bennington tritoon, captained by a U.S. Coast Guard licensed captain, IF you’re interested in booking it.
Do you provide life jackets?
Life jackets are provided for everyone except infants. For any infant/child under 30 pounds, you must bring your own life jacket or purchase one upstairs in the Ship’s Store. All children under 13-years-old must wear a life jacket at all times while on the boat/water. Anyone who is not a strong swimmer should wear a life jacket at all times. All jet ski riders must wear life jackets at all times.
Can I bring food/drinks/alcohol on the rental boat?
You are welcome to bring food, just be sure to clean up. A cleaning fee will be charged for any boat left excessively dirty. Beer, wine, and malt beverages are allowed on the boat. Consumption must be responsible and only by those 21-years old and up. The driver(s) of the boat cannot consume any alcohol. Glass bottles and liquor/spirits are not allowed and red liquids are not recommended.
Am I allowed to smoke on the boat or jet ski rental?
No smoking/vaping; no illegal drugs. If ANYONE in your rental party shows up to the beginning of the rental intoxicated or smelling intoxicated–on alcohol or drugs (including marijuana)–your rental will be canceled; and your rental fee will not be refunded.
Where do I park?
You can park in the sand lot under the bridge or along the grass. Follow parking pattern.
Boat Storage Questions
What are my storage options?
We offer outside, partially covered, and fully covered boat storage options. Availability and pricing depend on the size of your boat. Give the office a call for availability and pricing.
What is required to store my boat at the marina?
We require that your boat is insured and provide us with a copy of your insurance declaration page. We also require a $300 refundable security deposit. It is refundable once your contract is complete, the account is paid off, and your boat is removed from storage. Your boat must also have a battery switch, 2 dock lines, and 2 bumpers.
How soon can you have my boat in the water?
Give us a call one hour before you’d like to arrive to use your boat. During this call, let us know if you would like us to fill up your gas tank. Please arrive on time or call to let us know you’ll be running late. The boat will be pulled out of storage, sprayed off and in the water waiting for you to arrive. Every once in a while, we will have to “Launch on Arrival”. This generally only happens on busy summer holidays.
Do you clean/flush my boat?
When we pull a boat out of storage, we rinse the dust off the boat before we put it in the water. When we pull your boat out of the water, we flush your engine(s) with fresh water and rinse the saltwater off the boat. If you would like a deep clean boat wash, please call the office in advance to schedule. This more than likely cannot be done same day.
How late/early can I have my boat launched?
If you call the day prior for a “First Launch”, we will try our best to have your boat launched by 8:30-8:45am. “Last Launch” of the day is 4:30pm during season and 4pm during off-season. Call for a “Last Launch” if you will be arriving to use your boat after the marina closes or the next morning before we open.
What do I do if I arrive back with my boat after hours?
Dock your boat and securely tie it up with 2 dock lines. Leave your bumpers out. Place your keys in the key drop beside the garage door downstairs. If you would like your boat pulled out the next morning, bow in and please put down your antenna or bimini top. This will signal to us that you are ready to be pulled out the next day.
Can you charge up my trolling motor?
Yes. If you give us a call the day before you’d like to use your boat. We will put it on charge overnight, so it’ll be charged up the next morning when you call for a launch. There is a $10 fee per charge.
