TITLE: Fishing Charter Checklist | Flash Sport Fishing Charters
Before hitting the open water on your upcoming charter trip with us in San Francisco, it’ll help to know the things you’ll need to bring with you and the things we’ll be providing!
Check out our San Francisco fishing charter checklist:
What to wear on a fishing charter in San Francisco:
Clothing
When it comes to dressing for your charter trip, we suggest sticking to and .
First, lightweight clothing articles will help keep you feeling cool and comfortable throughout the day, while also saving you from some unwanted sunburn.
Second, light colored clothing will reflect the sun’s rays rather than absorb them as it happens with darker colors.
Comfortable Footwear
As much as you’ll be relaxing, you’re also going to be on your feet, fighting a battle with your soon-to-be big catch.
Be sure to wear your most comfortable shoes or boots, preferably non-skid so that when you’re on your feet, you on your feet.
Sunglasses & hat
Although you may feel that refreshing breeze coming from off the water, you’re going to start feeling the effects of the sun’s rays beating down on you throughout the day.
Come well-prepared with a pair of sunglasses and a hat, keeping you cool and protecting you from the sun.
Raingear (if necessary)
Keep an eye on the weather before you venture out on your fishing charter trip because you may need to bring a handy parka or windbreakers to fend off the elements.
What to Bring on a Fishing Charter in San Francisco:
Seasickness medication
If you are prone to motion sickness, you may experience a level of seasickness while out on the fishing charter.
There are several over-the-counter remedies for seasickness, but it would be best to consult with your doctor or pharmacist on the matter because preparation is key.
Sunscreen
When on a fishing charter trip, you must take the necessary precautions to protect yourself from the sun.
Bring along at least 30+ SPF and remember to reapply throughout the day.
Fishing License
One of the most important items you’ll need to have with you at all times is your fishing license.
You can purchase a California fishing license from the or they are available for purchase on the boat.
Food & Drink
You’re going to get hungry out there on the open water and unfortunately, you won’t be able to eat that fresh catch you just reeled in yet.
Not to worry though—bring along a lunch, snacks and drinks that will keep you hydrated and full for that full-day of fishing!
What Do We Provide on Our Fishing Charters:
At Flash Sport Fishing, we only need you to bring yourself (properly dressed for the weather). A lunch, and your fishing license.
We provide you with everything else!
Fishing Equipment
You can’t score your big catch without the right equipment—luckily, Flash Sport Fishing Charters supplies everything you’ll need.
Here are a few key pieces we’ll provide for your fishing trip:
Custom Rods
Quality reels
Tackle
Bait specialized for each trip
Rods and reels are available for our left-handed anglers and there are two speed reels available for children.
Captain Steve uses Avet reels and hand built custom rods by Mac’s Custom Rods, setting them up before you arrive depending on what type of fish you’re aiming for.
However, your personal equipment is always welcome! Just ask Captain Steve about how best to set up your rod and reel.
Latest Fish Finder Technology

=== PAGE: https://detoursamericanwest.com/faqs/
TITLE: DETOURS American West FAQs - Tours, Vehicles, Policies & More
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
DETOURS FAQS
FAQs - General
Do you run tours every day of the year?
Historically, we do not run tours on Thanksgiving Day or Christmas Day. Other than these two days, DETOURS American West operates tours daily, so long as weather conditions provide for safe touring and our minimum guest count has been met. If inclement weather is threatening a tour, a DETOURS agent will contact you to provide alternate options for your tour.
Can you pick up and/or drop off at the Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport?
No, we may be able to arrange drop off at a hotel nearby that allows guests to take the SkyTram into the airport, though. This is never a guarantee. Please reach out to our office to check availability.
Do you pick up and drop off from all hotels? What about private residences?
For tours, we can pick up at any hotel or private residence within our pick up zone.
For tours, we pick up from select hotels in Phoenix, Scottsdale, Tempe - and some tours we pick up at select locations in Flagstaff. However, we must limit the number of pick ups/drops off we do, so there is a chance you may need to meet at another hotel, depending on the size of your party. DETOURS will contact you upon booking with more information.
How many other people will be in the vehicle?
Our vehicles seat a maximum of 13 guests. Typically, there will be 9-13 guests.
What if my group is larger than 13 passengers?
We can accommodate large groups in multiple DETOURS vehicles or sometimes, we can outsource motorcoaches for an additional expense. Please call for details.
Do I need to bring a passport?
If you are visiting from outside the United States, we recommend having your passport with you at all times. Only for the Tombstone day tour departing from Phoenix are you required to bring your passport. This is due to the tour traveling close to the US/Mexico border and the chance of being stopped by Border Patrol. We always suggest you have your ID on you at all times regardless of which tour you are on.
Are kids allowed on your tours?
We don’t permit children under the age of 3 on our public tours. Children under 3 may be permitted on a private tour, please inquire with our office for more information.
Are any of your tour guides bilingual?
Our tours are conducted in English. Some of our guides speak Spanish but their availability is not guaranteed. Please call for details.
Is smoking allowed on the trip?
All DETOURS vehicles are smoke-free. Smoking in our vehicles is NOT permitted.
Can I bring my personal firearm/are firearms allowed on tour?
No, we prohibit all firearms on tour.
What if I have a walker/wheelchair?
We can accommodate a folding walker or folding wheelchair. For any other type of medical equipment, please contact our office.
What if I am prone to car sickness or have any other illness?
Please let us know at the time of booking that you are prone to car sickness or have any other injuries or illness. We can only make accommodations for this if we are aware of it prior to your tour departure. Please note that there is no assigned seating and seats may be rotated anytime during the tour.
What if I am late for or miss my pick-up?
Please call our office immediately. We will do our best to get you on that day’s tour, however, we cannot guarantee our vehicle will wait for you. We recommend arriving at your pick up point 15 minutes early. If you miss your tour altogether, we cannot provide refunds or credits but will work with your schedule to try another tour date.
What if I leave something on the vehicle?
Please contact our office immediately. You will be required to pick up your belongings from our office at a pre-arranged time. Please do not show up at our office unless we are expecting you. If you have already left town, DETOURS can ship the belongings at your expense.
Can I bring my own snacks and drinks?
Yes, except for alcoholic beverages. We provide unlimited bottled water on all tours. For our public Antelope Canyon tour, a continental breakfast and lunch are included. We also make stops along the way on all tours where you will be able to purchase food/snacks, but you are more than welcome to bring your own.
How much should I tip my guide?
20% is customary and graciously accepted.
FAQs - Vehicles
For public tours, we use customized High Roof Ford touring vans seating a maximum of 13 guests. Each vehicle is equipped with individual leather captain’s chairs and oversized windows, ensuring a comfortable and scenic journey. Plus, a speaker system for a clear and audible guided tour. This is also the vehicle used for private tours with six or more guests.
Is there WiFi in the vehicle?
No, and during parts of the drive there may be limited cell phone service.
Are there bathrooms in the vehicle?
No, but the guide will make multiple rest stops along the way though and can stop at the nearest rest stop at the request of a guest.
Are the vehicles accessible?
Unfortunately, our vehicles were not designed to accommodate wheelchairs. Guests should be able to walk up 3 steps into the vehicle on their own or with the help of a companion.
Does my child need a car seat/booster seat?
Arizona law states that children under five must use a car seat. Children between ages 5 and 7 must use a booster seat unless they are 4 feet 9 inches tall. Once a child is 4 feet 9 inches or taller or 8 years old, they are no longer required to ride in a booster seat. You must provide your own child safety seats if applicable. DETOURS does not provide or rent out child safety seats.
How much luggage can I bring on the vehicle?
On day trips we recommend bringing no more than a day pack. On overnight tours, individual pieces of luggage must be kept to a maximum of 50 pounds. It is recommended to travel with a backpack or soft overnight bag with a small day pack for easy access to a wallet, camera, etc. If luggage exceeds vehicle storage, DETOURS reserves the right to freight excess luggage at passenger’s expense.
If you will be bringing any luggage on tour with you please notify DETOURS at the time of booking the quantity and dimensions of luggage.
FAQs - Reservations & Cancellations
How far in advance should I book my tour?
We recommend making a reservation at least two weeks in advance to ensure you have secured your spot.
For single day tours, your credit card will be charged 24 hours prior to the departure of your tour except the Antelope Canyon Day Tour and Grand Canyon with Helicopter Day Tour which will be charged 48 hours prior.
For single day tours, your credit card will be charged 48 hours prior to the departure of your tour.
For overnight and multi-day tours, a $150 non-refundable deposit that goes toward the total tour amount is due upon lodging confirmation and the tour balance is due 7 days prior to tour departure.
If you book an overnight or multi-day tour that departs within 7 days, your credit will be charge the full tour amount immediately.
What’s not included in the tour cost?
Guide gratuities, snacks, and any meals not mentioned in the tour description are not included in the tour cost. Gratuities are always appreciated!
What form of payments do you accept?
DETOURS accepts payment by any of the following credit or debit cards: Visa, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover. We do not accept cash or checks. For private multi-day tours, please contact us.
Can I pay cash?
At this time, we are unable to accept cash as payment. We require credit or debit cards only.
What if my flight was cancelled?
DETOURS does not offer refunds or credits for cancelled flights. We HIGHLY recommend booking your tour on a date that occurs at least two days after you arrive. Please call our office if you have any questions.
What is the cancellation policy?
Cancellation Policy for Direct Bookings:
Public Day Tours – 24 hours prior to tour date - EXCEPT for the Antelope Canyon Day Tour and Grand Canyon with Helicopter Day Tour which have a 48 hour cancellation policyPrivate Day

Where will I sleep?
We typically secure you a lodge inside Grand Canyon National Park at Maswik Lodge, based on availability. Upgrades may be available for lodges located on the rim for an additional charge. El Tovar, Kachina, Thunderbird and Bright Angel are all located on the rim, with Bright Angel being the most rustic. Proximity of tour date, season and budget can determine availability of rim lodges. Please contact our office if you have any requests or preferences.
Will I be overnighting with a group?
Not necessarily. Our overnight tours are comprised of our single day tours. You will be on your own for the late afternoon/night and morning before you catch the shuttle to Las Vegas on Day 2.
Grand Canyon National Park is typically 25 degrees cooler than Phoenix/Scottsdale. The winter months can be cold with potential snow. Dress in layers and wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes.
What should I pack?
Layers, closed-toe shoes, sunscreen, sunglasses, hat. Even during summer, the nights and mornings can be chilly.

Private Tombstone Tour Itinerary
Travel back in time to one of the most famous Old West towns, with a day on the streets of Tombstone. The home of the famous O.K. Corral lets you experience the lives of outlaws, businessmen, miners, and cattlemen who flocked to the area for a chance to strike it rich on the frontier.
A ride straight from your hotel takes you out of the city for your visit to the historic town. While you’re in Tombstone, pay a visit to the original gathering spots for outlaws and gunmen, like Big Nose Kate’s Saloon and the Bird Cage Theatre, which earned a reputation as the wickedest nightspot between Basin Street and the Barbary Coast. When you step into the museum at the Tombstone Courthouse, learn about the men who were charged with keeping the peace in this rough-and-tumble town. True to the reputation of the Wild West, gunfights and stand-offs were a regular occurrence, and many of their victims are buried at the infamous Boot Hill Cemetery—named for the men who died, and were buried, with their boots still on.
Explore San Xavier del Bac
On your way back to your hotel, visit the White Dove of the Desert; one of the Southwest’s best-preserved missions at San Xavier del Bac. Founded in 1692, the San Xavier Mission is still in operation and allows guests to marvel at the ornate craftsmanship showcasing both Spanish and Native American influences. TITLE: What Does A Safari Cost? - Africa Adventure Consultants
Traveling to Africa is a bucket list trip for many, but also a substantial undertaking, one that’s . It’s also one where you need to appropriately budget for the kind of experience you dream of for your safari. We take you through some of what goes into the cost of a safari, along with suggested daily budgeting amounts, below.
best planned by an expert
Trip Cost Is More Than Your Accommodations
Safaris are not a bargain vacation, nor should they be once it’s clear what goes into making the magic happen. From transportation costs (ground and light aircraft transfers) to staff (the team that takes care of you at camp, your guide and possibly tracker, to the people you never see that keep things running) and the logistics of making everything happen (the fresh fruit on your breakfast plate might be grown onsite, or could have traveled by plane or overland truck from the coast to get to you) – it is a well-organized operation that takes considerable resources to make seamlessly happen. Additionally, the lodges we work with and the places we operate need funds for conservation and research – your trip helps to make those things happen.
Additionally, when you work with experts like the team at Africa Adventure Consultants, you are able to tap into a deep knowledge base to help plan your safari. And it’s not just building out your dream trip – we provide pre-trip support that includes services like flight guidance, trip insurance options, packing tips and more, as well as 24/7 emergency support throughout your travels. Also, we are licensed and insured in the United States giving you strong consumer protection for your travel purchase.
Group Trips versus Private, Customized Departures
Do you prefer to travel with an organized group or do you want a safari adventure that is unique to you? While we do offer of seven or fewer people, we specialize in for our travelers. While a small group trip can be a good choice for solo travelers or those on a budget, it’s our customized safaris that allow you to pick and choose what is important to you – what types of lodges or camps you want to experience, whether to visit private reserves or national parks (or both), whether to add on a city or beach escape to your trip and much more. We will work with you to craft a trip that matches your travel style – perhaps you would prefer tented camps to lodges or want to incorporate adrenaline activities into your safari adventure – a customized safari lets you make the most of every day (and night).
some hand-selected small group set departures
customized, private trips
With either a customized or a small group safari, you will have the chance to meet and interact with other travelers at your camp or lodge (unless you book fully private accommodations). On a customized itinerary, you will meet new people at each stop whereas on a group safari, you would spend your entire holiday with the same set of people.
We do not sell or recommend large group safaris. Our customized and ensure a guide and staff to guest ratio that ensures a wonderful experience for our travelers. Our guides are highly skilled, inspirational people that take travelers’ experiences to the next level. Unlike a customized safari, group safaris have set dates of departure and a fixed itinerary so there is little or no room for flexibility.
select small group departures
On a large group safari, you might find yourself in a middle seat or in a mini-bus. Some customized safaris include a private vehicle, while others do not. Game drives on our safaris are always done in a game drive vehicle (some open, some closed depending on destination and safari type) and we do not offer safaris that use mini-buses on game drives.
The Best Value Isn’t Always the Least Expensive
and offer the best value for money on safari in 2025 due to an exchange rate that is very much in favor of the US Dollar, however a bargain experience in these or any other African country might compromise accommodation size and quality (along with your own comfort!),the field experience of your guide, visiting areas that are less rich in wildlife or spending extra time in cities to keep costs down. Furthermore, you might find yourself in a middle seat on the safari vehicle with blocked views of the wildlife you’ve traveled so far to see or staying somewhere that is unable to accommodate your dietary needs.
Watch Out for Online ‘Deals’
You might see what looks like a fantastic safari deal in your inbox, but buyer beware – these aren’t always what they seem. The price might be based on a group departure of 30 people or include stays at accommodations lacking amenities. Or, you may be spending a significant portion of your trip driving between locations versus flying. Even worse, it could omit mandatory park and conservation fees, which can add up to a few hundred dollars per person, per day; changing the final cost of your safari substantially. You don’t want to be surprised arriving at a camp and finding that you owe four days of park fees to the tune of $900 per person!
Working with an Africa travel expert will ensure that all of the elements of your trip are clearly laid out, and you will be given a full accounting of what is included. It also doesn’t mean you can’t take advantage of seasonal specials or discounts though – be sure to about available specials for your destination.

TITLE: What to Know About Chimpanzee Trekking - Africa Adventure Consultants
Trekking to see Africa’s chimpanzees is exhilarating! The closest living relative of humans, chimpanzees are fascinating to observe in their natural habitat. The primates are found in many places throughout Africa, but we recommend trekking in (where Jane Goodall’s pioneering research on the species took place) and based on the terrain, availability of appropriate accommodations and quality of the experience. Both countries also offer a robust safari experience to add on to your chimp trekking adventures.
What to Expect
is a physical activity and travelers who wish to see the chimps should have a good level of fitness. Some areas are tougher to trek in than others – the Mahale Mountains in western Tanzania reach an elevation of over 8,000 feet (with a base level of around 2,500 feet), while Kibale National Park in Uganda is relatively flat and not strenuous. Treks can range in distance from a mile or two to several miles with steep climbs, depending on where you choose to trek and generally run from 2-5 hours, including time with the chimps.
Trekking chimpanzees
Scouts are out in the forest early to locate the chimpanzee families, making it easier for your trekking group to find them. You will follow generally well-cleared paths for much of your trek, but bushwhacking is sometimes necessary as well. Once you find the chimps, you’ll have the chance to observe them from a distance of 8-10 yards for an hour. You’ll find that the time passes very quickly – we recommend booking two treks if you have the flexibility.
If you’d like more time with the chimps, Uganda’s Kibale National Park offers a habituation experience. This is a smaller group of trekkers going into the forest with researchers and spending up to 4 hours with a group of chimpanzees. about this special option.
Ask your Journey Specialist
It is important to note that permits are required to trek chimpanzees and a limited number are available each day. It is essential to book well in advance to secure your trekking permit.
in Tanzania is at its best during the dry season running from June through October. November and the onset of the rains can still be good while December through March see the most moisture. It’s great for seeing the forest at its most lush and photography is excellent with crystal clear skies, but the trekking is more challenging and the chimps can be harder to see. We do not recommend chimp trekking in April and May.
Chimpanzee trekking
Uganda chimp trekking safaris can take place all year however, we think the best time to visit is during the dry months of December through February and again from June through August.
Overall, we prefer chimp trekking in the dry season to avoid the challenges of muddy trails. to find the right time for your trek.
What to Wear
Chimp trekking takes place in dense forest. We recommend that travelers wear long-sleeved shirts and pants in neutral colors when trekking, not only for protection from vegetation but also from the sun and insects. Hiking boots or sturdy trekking shoes with long socks are a must, and we like to wear a pair of gaiters to keep moisture and insects from getting in our shoes or pants. Gardening gloves can also be handy to avoid hurting your hands when grabbing vegetation to support yourself as you move through the forest.
Bring along insect repellent, sunglasses, sunblock, a hat, rain jacket and a fleece. You’ll want a small pack, preferably waterproof, to accommodate all of these items along with your camera, phone, water, etc.
What it Costs
Chimpanzee trekking permits range from $100 – $300 per person per day depending on the country and park you choose.
Where Can I Trek Chimps?
Our favorite places for chimpanzee trekking are in remote Western Tanzania at , or in Uganda’s and Kyambura Gorge in Queen Elizabeth National Park. Chimps can also be seen in Rwanda’s Nyungwe National Park and Gishwati Mukura National Park.
Gombe Stream National Park and Mahale Mountains National Park
Kibale National Park
Chimp trekking can range from gentle and undulating terrain to steep gorge and mountain climbs depending on where you choose to trek. You will be guided by an expert who spends most days in the forest with the chimps and who has expertise on finding the apes, as well as interpreting their behavior. They will also be able to point out other interesting forest species you may see along the way. to determine which park is the right fit for your customized chimpanzee trekking safari.
How Old Do I Have to Be?
The minimum age for chimpanzee trekking in both and ranges from 12 to 15, as different parks have different regulations. This is both for travelers’ safety as well as the chimps – younger guests are more likely to transmit disease and illness to the chimps who are especially vulnerable to human ailments.

Emerald Bay
Showcasing beautiful Fallen Leaf lake, Cascade Lake, Taylor Creek, and Pope Beach, this tour heads to breathtaking Emerald Bay. Surrounded by granite cathedrals and fed by Eagle falls, the lake's only true bay is named for its emerald green waters.
Book Now
10mins, $120/person, 2 person minimum
Zephyr Cove
This tour encompasses the entire south shore of Lake Tahoe, starting with a trip up the east shore into Nevada. Witness the beautiful indigo blue waters and teal shorelines as you fly to Zephyr Cove. After circling Zephyr Cove, the tour heads west along the south shoreline past Fallen Leaf Lake and Cascade Lake to Emerald Bay.
20mins, $180/person, 2 person minimum
Sand Harbor
One of Lake Tahoe's most visited beaches, Sand Harbor, is known for its gorgeous sand beaches and multi-hued waters. Fly over some of the locals' best kept secrets, the hidden beaches and bays along the east shoreline: Glenbrook Bay, Secret Harbor, Skunk Harbor, and Chimney Beach. After reaching Sand Harbor, we climb up for a look at Marlette Lake, at 7,841 feet above sea level!
30mins, $300/person, 2 person minimum
Lakes and Waterfalls
Starting at South Tahoe Airport, this 30 minute tour first embarks to Emerald Bay, then south along the mountains over Cascade Lake, past Mount Tallac, and over the shoreline of Fallen Leaf lake. Head west over Glen Alpine Creek, with Glen Alpine Falls below, climbing towards Pyramid Peak, at an elevation of 9,984 feet! The area is scattered with myriad lakes and waterfalls. Fly over Lake Aloha and past Horsetail Falls, dropping nearly 500 feet. The tour concludes by flying over upper and lower Echo Lake before returning to the airport.
*Please note: While the lakes are always present, seasonal snow and rainfall, as well as time of year, affect the size of waterfalls in the area.
*The area in which this tour operates is prone to turbulence due to the topography of the area and frequently subject to route change for this reason. The alternative in the event of excessive turbulence is the Sand Harbor tour, equally as beautiful, and also 30 minutes.
30 mins, $300/person, 2 person minimum
Circle the Lake
This 45 minute ride follows Lake Tahoe's pristine 72 mile shoreline, shimmering in shades of green and blue. While most of the shoreline is visible from the roads and highways circling the lake, nothing can compare to the view from a helicopter! Start by flying to Emerald Bay, then continue your journey around Lake Tahoe to witness the many stunning views Lake Tahoe has to offer.
45mins, $420/person, 2 person minimum
Lake Tahoe Sunset
With a limited number of sunsets to see in our lifetime, it's important to miss as few as possible. Lake Tahoe sunsets are some of the most breathtaking in the world, and sunset in Lake Tahoe from a helicopter, is second to none.

Discover the Fun of Fishing in St. Petersburg
EXPLORE CHARTERS
Welcome to Bay Reef Fishing Charters in St Peterburg, Florida!
Bay Reef Fishing Charters is located in St Petersburg, Florida, the center of fishing action in Tampa Bay!
Being located in St. Pete, we're fortunate to have access to Tampa Bay - the largest bay and open-water estuary in all of Florida. Tampa Bay is also home to more than 200 species of fish and we’re going after the best of them!
From the backcountry flats to the bay reefs, Tampa Bay is home to several varieties of , and plenty more species we love to catch including
Snook, Redfish, Black Drum, Flounder, Spotted Sea Trout, Tripletails, Kingfish, Tarpon,
Snapper and Grouper
Sharks!
Inshore Reef Fishing in Tampa Bay, Nearshore Fishing in the Gulf of America, Backcounty Sport Fishing, Shark Fishing and Night Fishing Trips.
Our St Petersburg Fishing Charters include:
Night Fishing in St. Pete
Available all Autumn in 2025
Autumn is a great time for night fishing in St. Pete! Water visibility is very good in the autumn months and migrating schools of bait fish are entering Tampa Bay and attracting big redfish, snook and other species we love to catch. We’re sight casting for fish with underwater lights and around dock lights in residential canals where we can cast directly on them. Night fishing is a great way to target monster Snook and Redfish!
Book a St Petersburg Night Fishing Trip in Tampa Bay with Bay Reef Fishing Charters for an exciting and unique fishing adventure!
Learn More
Fishing Charters in St Petersburg, Florida
with Bay Reef Fishing Charters
Charters depart just minutes from St Petersburg, St Pete Beach and Treasure Island!
Night Fishing in St Petersburg, Florida
Discover Night Fishing in Tampa Bay with Captain Dmitri!
For a truly different kind of fishing experience, book a Night Fishing charter with Captain Dmitri. We’ll sight cast along the shores and navigation canals of Tampa Bay using underwater lights to spot monster Redfish and Snook. We may encounter other species often active at night including Sharks!
Backcountry Sport Fishing in St Petersburg, Florida
Tampa Bay has one of the largest and most diverse estuaries in all of Florida.
You’ll fish the grassy flats and mangroves of the extensive Tampa Bay estuary for the Southeast’s favorite inshore catches including Redfish, Flounder, Black Drum, Spanish Mackerel and Spotted Sea Trout (Speckled Trout).
There’s also plenty of Snook, a favorite inshore saltwater species of Central and South Florida. You may also encounter Tarpon on a backcountry fishing trip with Captain Dmitri.
Inshore Reef Fishing in St Petersburg, Florida
The deeper waters of Tampa Bay offer great coastal bottom fishing!
We’ll bottom fish the re
efs and shipping channels of Tampa Bay in up to 50 feet of water for bottom dwelling saltwater species such as Red Grouper, Gag Grouper, Mangrove Snapper and Lane Snapper. Tampa Bay is also home to King Mackerel, Jack Crevalle and even TripleTails!
An Inshore Reef Fishing Charter is a great way to experience true saltwater coastal fishing but in calmer waters than fishing offshore.
Nearshore Offshore Fishing in St Petersburg, Florida
Bottom reef fishing in the Gulf of America up to 9 miles offshore.
On a Nearshore Reef Fishing charter with Captain Dmitri you’ll find many of the same species found in Tampa Bay including Red Grouper, Gag Grouper, Mangrove Snapper, Lane Snapper, Grunts, Spanish Mackerel, Kingfish, TripleTail and Jacks. Nearshore there are many more reefs to fish and the fish are often bigger and more plentiful.
Shark Fishing in St Petersburg, Florida
Experience Shark Fishing Right Here in Tampa Bay!
You don’t have to go far from St Petersburg for a fun filled shark fishing trip! Tampa Bay is home to many shark species including Blacktip Sharks, Atlantic Sharpnose Sharks, Bonnetheads, Spinners, Lemon and Nurse Sharks and even dangerous Bull Sharks.
Sharks are plentiful in Tampa Bay and catching one of these hard fighting predators is always a thrill.
Family Friendly Fishing Charters
Kids are Welcome on Every Trip with Captain Dmitri!
Captain Dmitiri is a friendly and patient fishing guide who works great with children of all ages. Captain Dmitri loves showing everyone on board, and especially first timers, how much fun fishing can be.
Your kids will have the biggest smiles and the best memories of their Florida vacation fishing in St Petesburg with Captain Dmitri and Bay Reef Fishing Charters.

Captain Dmitri has fished the Gulf Coast from South Texas to South Florida and brings over 30 years of fishing experience and passion to Tampa Bay. His highly rated fishing guide service, Bay Reef Fishing Charters, is located in Saint Petersburg, Florida. Located at the mouth of Tampa Bay, St Petersburg is just minutes away from great fishing in Tampa Bay and the Gulf of America.
Captain Dmitri enjoys sharing his passion for fishing with all skill levels and ages of anglers! As your captain and fishing guide, Captain Dmitri will do his best to make sure everyone on board has a fun and memorable time fishing in Tampa Bay.

Experience a Spectacular Sunset Dinner Cruise in Maui!
Join us aboard the Calypso, a spacious and stable triple-deck catamaran departing from the conveniently located Ma’alaea Harbor. Experience a leisurely two-hour sunset dinner cruise, offering ample time to savor a delicious meal, explore the vessel’s amenities, enjoy live island-style music, and witness the breathtaking sunset from the water’s edge.
The Calypso comfortably accommodates groups of all sizes, from couples to families to large corporate events. Choose from various seating options, including tables for two, four, eight, and ten, as well as cozy enclaves scattered throughout the boat for relaxation or mingling with fellow guests.
Explore all three decks at your leisure, finding the perfect spot in the sun or shade. Restrooms are conveniently located on the lowest deck, while the front of the boat offers unobstructed views but can be breezy, so be prepared with a secure hat and leave your fake eyelashes ashore, as one guest humorously suggested.
Indulge in complimentary fizzy sodas, tropical juices, or island-themed adult beverages, with two free drinks included in your cruise package. Once the catamaran sets sail, additional alcoholic beverages can be purchased from the friendly onboard crew.
Feast on a delectable main meal featuring juicy prime rib, mahi-mahi, teriyaki chicken, steamed vegetables, roasted potatoes, and decadent chocolate cake. Throughout the meal, attentive crew members ensure your comfort and cleanliness, keeping the ocean environment pristine.
As you dine, admire the distant islands of Kaho’olawe and Lana’i, and keep an eye out for humpback whales during their seasonal visits from Alaska. The captain and crew are eager to share insights about these magnificent marine mammals, enhancing your dining experience with engaging whale conversations.
Relish this unforgettable time at sea with your loved ones, basking in the warmth of the sun, enjoying great food, and creating cherished memories aboard the Calypso sunset dinner cruise.

=== PAGE: https://www.neworleansstylefishingcharters.com/what-to-bring-on-a-new-orleans-fishing-charter/
TITLE: What to Bring on a New Orleans Fishing Charter - New Orleans Style Fishing Charters
What should I bring on my fishing charter?
This is probably one of the most common questions that I’ve gotten over the years of being a fishing guide. Many new anglers hire a guide to learn and experience firsthand the techniques of the sport from a professional. In my experience, most groups I take out have at least one novice fisherman with in them. Everyone starts somewhere so I don’t mind teaching customers the ins and outs of what I know.
What’s the weather like?
“What to bring” on your will vary from trip to trip, depending on the weather, what your fishing guide provides, and location. Typically, I advise customers to dress according to the weather at hand. Remember that you can always take it off, if need be, in the winter months. Also bring any snacks, food, or drinks that you may want while on the water, sun block, sunglasses, hats, and bug spray. If you think it will make your fishing experience better, bring it. I supply all rod and reels, bait, tackle, ice, and fuel needed for our charter.
charter
Are we going to get wet?
I also recommend bringing packable rain gear. Here in the south, the weather changes hourly at times and rain gear can be the difference of a good day on the water or misery. Even if there isn’t rain in the forecast rain gear can act as a wind breaker, bug stopper, or even keep you dry in the foggy mornings. I’ve owned all types of rain gear from some of the cheapest to some of the most expensive out there. No matter what the cost it can serve a purpose that will make your fishing charter a better experience. It’s better to have it and not need it than to need it and not have it.
What rain gear do I use?
I have been through quite a few makes and models of rain gear over the years as a Louisiana fishing guide. I find the best all around gear for what I do is made by Sitka. The “Dew Point” jacket and pants have 3 Layers of Gore-Tex water proofing. This set of rain gear is very light weight and comfortable, it also has a durable construction designed for the active outdoorsmen. You can find this gear at some local distributors, or you can visit . This set up has kept me dry in some of the nastiest weather.
SITKA Gear
“COME FISH A ‘NAWLINS GOOD TIME!” I’m booking trips daily so feel free to give me a call with any questions or to schedule your fishing charter today.

=== PAGE: https://www.sunsetsailsalem.com/cancellation-policy
TITLE: Cancellation Policy
Cancellation policy
Booking
When you book through Sunset Sail Salem, you should receive an email or phone confirmation of your reservation. Please have your credit card ready to place a deposit to hold your reservation.
Cancellation Policy
When you reserve a charter, a significant amount of effort goes toward preparing the vessel for your trip. We understand there are times when you may have to cancel a charter.
As long as you give us at least 48 hours, it is minimally disruptive. No shows, especially at the time of launch, or last-minute cancellations make it difficult for us to keep our prices competitive.
For cancellations 48 hours or more in advance, we offer a full refund minus a 10% processing fee. Cancellations made less than 48 hours in advance will be charged a minimum of 20% to a maximum of full price, dependent upon the circumstances.
Weather Cancellations
Our captains and crew will not sail in unsafe weather conditions such as heavy rain, thick fog, high winds, electrical storms, and so on. We will, however, sail in intermediate sprinkles, overcast conditions, and light fog.
The decision to sail is ultimately in the hands of the captain. If the captain determines it is unsafe to run a trip, Sunset Sail Key West will do its best to reschedule your trip for another day.
If the captain cancels the trip due to unsafe weather conditions, you will be issued a full refund.
If you have a confirmed reservation and choose not to sail because of weather and the boat still sails, you will be charged a minimum of 20% up to a maximum of the full ticket price, depending on the season.

TITLE: About | Sunset Sail Salem
Memories that last a lifetime
From the stunning views of Salem Sound's off shore islands to the experience and warm hospitality of our crew, we offer unforgettable sailing experiences onboard our Historic Schooner Yacht Malabar X.
Schooner When And If
This truly classic sailing yacht was designed by renowned Boston naval architect John Alden and launched in 1939 for General George S. Patton. She was named after a quote attributed to Patton, who said "When the war is over, and if I live through it, Bea and I are going to sail her around the world"
When And If is a transoceanic cruising yacht with traditional wooden hull, teak decks, and a gorgeous rig with tall masts and a multitude of sails. She is known for her beauty, speed and exceptional sailing performance. Before World War II, Patton made just one voyage aboard - Taking delivery in Wiscasset, Maine and sailing to the Chesapeake bay, where it is said that the vessel hid in an estuary to escape the call to join the USCG picket patrol. General Patton returned briefly in the summer of 1945 and enjoyed a week's sailing out of Manchester, MA before returning to duty in Europe as acting Governor of Bavaria. He was killed in a car accident shortly after.
The Schooner When And If, operated by Sunset Sail Salem in the summers and Sunset Sail Key West in the winter months has spent much of her long life in the waters of the North Shore and surrounds: first as part of the Patton estate in the 1940s, 50s and 60s, then as part of the Landmark School at Pride’s Crossing in the 1970s and 80s, and afterwards as the darling of Vineyard Haven in the 90s.
In 2012 the yacht was restored to her original lines by then owner Doug Hazlitt and current owner Seth Salzmann as Captain and project manager. In 2016 Capt. Seth purchased the yacht, and has opened her to the public for the first time in her storied history. When And If is available for private and public sailing charters, regattas, film and photo shoots and tall ships festivals year round. With her diverse portfolio and busy schedule When And If has become a perfect example of how classic yachting can thrive in the modern age.
We are proud and happy to be running her in her home waters once again!
Schooner Malabar X
Before Schooner When And If came Schooner Malabar X: the magnum opus of John Alden’s extensive schooner portfolio. Built in 1930 by Hodgdon Bros of East Boothbay, ME, Malabar X was the last schooner Alden built for himself to win the Newport-Bermuda race which she did with flying colors, smashing records in 1932.
Malabar X was badly damaged and written off in the samestorm which pulled When And If from her mooring and sent her for her rebuild in1990. In like fashion, Malabar X was also painstakingly restored to her former glory and in 2002 was launched sparkling to begin life on the Finger Lakes, NY.
Following her sale in 2003 she spent time as aresident of the Royal Yacht Club in Barcelona and in 2023 was returned to USA to have her flag restored and begin a new chapter as a charter sailing yacht with Sunset Sail Salem.
With her light and elegant silhouette, silver sprung teakdecks, soaring rig and gorgeous interior, Malabar X is the perfect choice foryour Summer sailing charter. She is USCG certified for 37 guests on deck for daysailing, and for overnight trips she accommodates 4 guests in 2 commodious cabins, each with a double berth. A twin V berth in the fo’c’sle and a pilot bunk house the crew.
Come sailing and be part of Malabar’s new life back home in America as we build her a foothold in the classic yachting industry, working to keep these glorious vessels on the high seas for years to come!
About us
We sail all summer long, rain or shine out of Salem, MA running award-winning sailing tours in the beautiful waters of the North Shore. With a full schedule of morning, afternoon and sunset sailing plus unlimited options for private charters, we’re sure to be able to bring you out on your perfect sailing trip this summer. Would you like to add an extra hour or two? Do you need your trip catered? Call us to make your dream sail come true!
When and If and Malabar X sail fast and smoothly. As the fastest sailboats on the sound we cover a lot of ground wherever the wind takes us and - depending where the wind takes us - on different days can glide by lighthouses, islands, the coastline of Cape Ann, the skyline of Boston. TITLE: General Sailing Charter Terms & Conditions | Gone Sailing Adventures
General Sailing Charter Terms & Conditions
Effective March 17, 2026
All guests must arrive 20 minutes before the scheduled departure for check-in procedures. All charters depart promptly at the stated times. You are responsible for arriving at the correct location specified in your confirmation email. Gone Sailing Adventures operates from multiple waterfront locations in Toronto. Late arrival or arrival at the incorrect marina will result in forfeiture of your charter or delayed boarding with no refund or rescheduling consideration. Please account for downtown Toronto traffic conditions, including sporting events, concerts, and ferry schedules that may affect travel time. All vessels operate under a barefoot policy, with the exception of Sky Oasis. Footwear must be removed before boarding to protect the teak decking and maintain vessel condition. For the safety of all passengers and animals, no pets are permitted aboard any Gone Sailing Adventures vessel. This policy extends to service animals as permitted under applicable provincial legislation. These restrictions are implemented to ensure both human and animal safety in the maritime environment. Gone Sailing Adventures operates in all weather conditions except those determined to be unsafe by the vessel captain. Toronto’s waterfront microclimate differs significantly from inland weather forecasts, and conditions on Lake Ontario are subject to rapid change. Guests are advised to dress appropriately for marine conditions. Lake Ontario temperatures typically register 5–10 degrees Celsius below ambient air temperature, and offshore winds can significantly affect perceived temperature. Layered clothing is recommended: a moisture-wicking base layer, an insulating mid-layer, and a weather-resistant outer layer. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and protective headwear are advised. Due to the unpredictable nature of Lake Ontario weather conditions, Gone Sailing Adventures does not cancel charters in advance. Cancellation determinations are made at departure time based on: If conditions exceed safe operating parameters (localized electrical storms, sustained winds exceeding 25 knots, or persistent heavy precipitation), clients receive a raincheck valid for rescheduling within the same sailing season. Sails may be delayed up to 60 minutes while awaiting improved conditions. Should conditions become suitable for sailing, the full sailing duration will be provided. If conditions do not improve within 60 minutes, the sail may be cancelled and a raincheck is issued. When conditions are deemed safe for operation and the client chooses not to proceed, no refund or credit is issued. Guests residing more than 50 kilometres from Toronto who have secured overnight accommodations may qualify for a refund less a $250 administrative fee for private charters or $50 for shared sails. Documentation of residence and local accommodation will be required. Lake Ontario sailing involves natural vessel motion resulting from wind and wave action. Once offshore, immediate return to dock is frequently not feasible. Captains evaluate wind speeds, wave patterns, forecast conditions, and vessel stability based on passenger dynamics before authorizing departure. Guests susceptible to motion sickness are advised to seek medical advice for remedies, check our FAQ page, or not to board. No refunds or prorated fees apply if a guest experiences seasickness after departure. When conditions permit, vessels may utilize sheltered areas near the Toronto Islands to minimize passenger discomfort. However, all routing decisions are made by the captain based on safety considerations, weather conditions, and time constraints. Captain decisions regarding vessel operations are final. Sailboat operation requires adequate wind conditions. During periods of calm or when returning to harbour against unfavourable wind direction, motor propulsion may be utilized. This represents standard sailing practice, and no fee adjustments are made when wind conditions do not permit continuous sailing. Aerosol spray products are prohibited aboard all vessels, as they damage yacht finishes. This restriction includes sunscreen spray, hairspray, and perfume aerosols. Lotion-based sunscreen formulations are permitted. Smoking, e-cigarettes, and vaping are strictly prohibited on all vessels, docks, and company equipment. This prohibition extends to all tobacco products and cannabis. Smoking may be permitted on motor yachts only in designated exterior areas, subject to the captain’s authorization. Not all captains authorize smoking on their vessels. No recreational drugs, including cannabis in any form, are permitted during charter periods. Balloons are prohibited on all vessels due to documented environmental impact on Lake Ontario aquatic ecosystems. Marine debris from balloon releases has been demonstrated to harm fish, avian species, and aquatic wildlife. Guests must possess sufficient mobility to step up, down, and forward 18 inches (50 centimetres) unassisted to safely board vessels. Boarding may be denied without refund if minimum mobility requirements are not met. Maximum passenger weight is 125 kilograms (275 pounds) to maintain vessel stability, personal safety, and ensure safe operation. Gone Sailing Adventures accepts no responsibility for items left, lost, or damaged aboard vessels or dock facilities. Guests are responsible for securing all personal valuables before departure. Prior to boarding, guests must present valid government-issued photo identification and the original credit card used for payment authorization. Failure to provide required documentation may result in denied boarding with no refund or credit. This policy prevents charter fraud and verifies payment authorization. The vessel captain maintains exclusive authority to cancel, delay, or suspend sailing operations due to: If a charter is less than 60% complete when cancelled by the captain for weather-related reasons, clients may reschedule within the same calendar season at no charge. Cash refunds are not issued under these circumstances. If the captain terminates a charter early for reasons other than weather or mechanical failure, no refund or credit is provided. This includes early termination due to passenger misconduct, intoxication, or safety violations. Gone Sailing Adventures reserves the right to substitute an equivalent or superior vessel for mechanical, scheduling, or operational requirements. “Equivalent” is defined as a vessel of comparable size and passenger capacity. Exact vessel matching is not guaranteed. Gone Sailing Adventures may adjust charter start times by up to 60 minutes with a minimum of one week’s advance notice, without compensation to the client. This accommodation allows for vessel maintenance, preceding charter delays, or operational requirements. Children must remain within arm’s length of their designated guardian at all times while aboard. Unaccompanied movement about the vessel is prohibited due to moving equipment (booms, lines), vessel heeling, and open water access. Children under 12 years of age require Transport Canada-approved personal flotation devices (PFDs) or lifejackets. These must be provided by guardians or rented from Gone Sailing Adventures at a cost of $15 per child with advance notice via . Children’s flotation devices must be worn continuously when the vessel is not anchored. Need help? Our FAQ’s offers clear, concise answers to your questions. Save time and get the answers you need now to complete your reservation with confidence.
What is your cancellation policy for individuals?
All bookings are final once confirmed subject to our severe weather rescheduling and minimum participation.
Any changes to individual ticketed sails prior to 7 days before sail are at the sole discretion of Gone Sailing Adventures and if accepted will incur a change fee of $20.00 per person (plus tax).
No changes will be accepted within 7 days of sailing except where Cancellation Protection is purchased at the time of reservation. Cancellation Protection allows for a full refund (less premium) for up to 3 days (72hrs) prior to the scheduled start of your sail.
Participation is fully transferable to another participant
What is your cancelation policy for Private Charters?
As with most travel arrangements, all reservations are final once confirmed. All sails proceed subject to dangerous sailing conditions in which case, they are rescheduled. Only the Captain can make these decisions.
We do offer Cancellation and Weather Protection for private charters.
We do offer an exception where ALL guests are from out of town. See Weather Insurance Protection.
What is your refund policy?
All reservations are final subject to our cancellation policies. Refunds are issued on an exception basis only and are reviewed by management. They are not automatic. All requests for refunds must be made in writing to info@gosailto.com

What is your weather policy for private charters?

May we bring a cake?

Can we bring our own food? If so, what will we have to bring with us?

Can we swim?
During the hot summer days we encourage a swim in the fresh Lake Ontario water. Our boats have noodles and other flotation devices.
We swim in approximately 8-20′ of water. You should be competent to swim in this depth in order enter the water.
Lifejackets provided are for onboard use only and are not to be used as a swimming aid. We do however offer a variety of noodles, flutterboards and floating saddles.
Will I get cold or wet?
On a typical sail you will probably get splashed a bit unless the weather is absolutely calm. The proper clothing will keep you warm and dry so there is no need to shiver. What mobility are requirements for participating on a sail?

Outdoor Recreation at Keesler Air Force Base is charged with providing quality outdoor recreational opportunities at affordable prices for the military population and their families. In addition to providing programming, Outdoor Recreation serves as a headquarters for equipment rentals that range from kayaks, paddleboards, and motorized boats to tables, chairs, and camping equipment.
Located on the Biloxi Back Bay, our proximity to the water allows us to enable a myriad of services through our beautiful marina pier area.

To introduce people to the benefits of Outdoor Recreation and healthy lifestyle activities by teaching meaningful skills and behaviors through top quality and innovative programming. Rental FAQs
Are pets allowed on rental boats?
No. Pets are not permitted on any rental boat. No exceptions.
Can I bring a BBQ grill on the boat?
No. BBQs and portable grills are not allowed on any rental craft. No exceptions.
Are water sports allowed?
Water sports are permitted on select boats only. Please contact Spring Lake Marina before booking if you plan to participate in water sports activities.
Who is responsible for damage to the boat?
The lessee (renter) is responsible for any loss, damage, theft, or misuse of the rental craft, equipment, and contents during the rental period.
How early should I arrive?
Please arrive 30 minutes before your scheduled departure time for check-in, paperwork, and safety orientation.
It is the customer's responsibility to arrive on time. Late arrivals will not receive rental credits, refunds, or additional time extensions.
What happens if I don't show up for my reservation?
No-show / no-call reservations are non-refundable.
Failure to arrive for your scheduled reservation without prior notice will result in the full forfeiture of all rental payments.
Where do rentals depart from?
All pontoon and tritoon rentals depart directly from Spring Lake Marina in Antioch, Illinois, with immediate access to the Chain O' Lakes.

TITLE: Spring Lake Marina FAQs | Boat Rentals, RV Sites, Marina & Diner Questions
FAQs
Frequently Asked Questions
Find answers to common questions about boat rentals, marina services, RV sites, seasonal slips, and visiting Spring Lake Marina.
WHAT ARE THE AGE/LICENSE REQUIREMENTS TO RENT A BOAT?
If you were born in the year(s) before 1998 a simple driver’s license will do. Minimum age to rent with us is 21, but if you were born after January 1st 1998 you must have a boating safety certificate as well. See
HELPFUL LINKS.
I WANT TO RENT A BOAT TODAY, HOW DO I SEE WHAT’S AVAILABLE?
Click on theat the top.
HOW DO I MAKE A RESERVATION?
All Bookings are made on-line. Click the button from our website. Click the tab to view what is still available to rent on any particular day, or tab to see our different selection of boats.
WHERE DO I PARK AND CHECK IN?
When you arrive at Spring Lake Marina, you will be pulling into a parking lot that is designated to a restaurant – PLEASE DO NOT PARK THERE. Take the road leading behind it, straight down to the parking lot on the right. The Boat Rental check in is there. Parking is limited, so please consider consolidating your group and number of cars before your departure.
IS THERE A SECURITY DEPOSIT?
No. Your boat rental is paid in full at the time of your on-line reservation.
WHY DO I NEED TO ARRIVE 30 MINUTES BEFORE MY SCHEDULED DEPARTURE?
You will need to present us with your valid Credit Card and Driver's License and sign our . You will then be given a full orientation at the desk on our lakes, rules and regulations, and safe boating tips. You will also receive a separate operating orientation on your vessel before your departure.
Rental Agreement
IS FUEL INCLUDED?
No. Your boat goes out on a full tank of gas, plenty to enjoy a full day boating, and we simply top you off when you return to the dock.
HOW MUCH WILL THE FUEL COST?
Too many variables to consider when guesstimating. It will all depend on which boat you have, how much weight is on-board, how fast/slow you go, how much time you actually operate your boat, water sport activity etc.
CAN I KEEP THE BOAT OVERNIGHT OR TO A TRANSPORT TO A DIFFERENT LAKE?
No. All our boats depart and return to our docks only. None of our rental boats may be on the lakes past dusk. You must return the boat at your originally scheduled departure time. If you would like to extend your reservation, you must inquire at the dock for availability.
WHO DRIVES THE BOAT?
You. We do not provide drivers or captains for hire. If you would like to designate someone else as the driver for your boat, please make sure they are with you during check in at the dock.

IS THERE A MILITARY DISCOUNT?

Planning a day on the water, a marina stay, or a weekend getaway? These resources can help you prepare for your visit to Spring Lake Marina and the Chain O' Lakes.
The Chain O'Lakes is a waterway system in northeast Illinois composed of 15 lakes connected by the Fox River and man-made channels. Encompassing more than 7,100 acres of water, 488 miles of shoreline and 45 miles of river, the Chain is the busiest inland recreational waterway per acre in the United States. Located on the border of Lake County and McHenry County, about an hour's drive from the cities of Chicago, Milwaukee, and Rockford, the lakes are popular with boaters and fishermen drawing weekend crowds of 30,000 and holiday crowds of 100,000 people. The Fox Waterway Agency, a special local governing body, is responsible for oversight of the Chain O’Lakes.

TITLE: FAQ – Boat Rentals NYC & Private Yacht Charters – NYC By Water
FAQ
Arrival Info:
The yacht is docked at One15 Marina in Brooklyn Bridge Park in Brooklyn. Please arrive at the marina gate no later that 15 mins before your scheduled departure time with your ENTIRE party, and the hostess on duty for your trip will escort you to the yacht. She already has your phone number and she will call you if she cannot find you. Per maritime security regulations, the hostess cannot walk in incomplete parties so please make sure everyone is at the gate 15 mins before departure. Furthermore, no one is allowed to board the boat unless the Charterer (person who actually rented the boat for the time) is present, their ID verified, and a bareboat agreement is executed. The Charterer must be over 21 years old. There are no exceptions to this rule as it’s illegal for us to allow boarding for anyone unless the Charterer is present. As this is a bareboat rental, prior to departure, the charterer should do a survey of the boat to assure themselves that there are no damages etc and familiarize themselves with all life safety equipment on board. Similarly, after the trip please do another walk around to make sure that you are returning the boat in the same condition that it was at pickup. We absolutely encourage the Charterer to do the vessel walk through before and after the trip. Please let us know if you notice any issues etc. so same can be documented.
Parking:
There are several garages offering parking by the marina. Please google the location and you will likely find a garage of your choice. the closest garage is City Parking by the marina. Here is the google maps link that you can use to find it. City Parking Brooklyn Bridge LLC
(646) 237-4122
Allowed Alcohol on Board:
We allow a maximum of one bottle of hard liquor per 6 passengers. If you bring more than that with you we will ask that you leave it on the dock and pick it up when you return. If at anytime, the crew feels that you or your guests are too intoxicated, they will return back to the dock immediately and the trip will be over. Hard seltzers or wine/beer are not included in this calculation but please don’t go crazy with the alcohol.
Captain / Crew:
Since you are renting under a Bareboat Charter Agreement, you have the option of operating the boat yourself provided you have the necessary licenses and proficiency to operate a vessel of this size. We will also require a $1 mln dollar insurance policy and a quick checkout sea-trial if you choose to operate the boat yourself. You also have an option to retain an independent captain of your own choosing provided they meet all our requirements and we approve them for the trip. In the alternative, we can offer you a choice of several Captains who are qualified to operate the boat and you can select one based on their availability for that day. Please remember, all Captain and Crew expenses must be paid separately directly to the crew upon your arrival at the marina gate and before the start of the trip. The Captain and the first mate are independent contractors and will be under your control for the duration of the trip. Importantly, we will not be able to handover the control of the boat unless unless the qualified crew chosen by you confirms they were paid and will operate the trip. A Bareboat Charter Agreement and waiver must also be executed by the Charterer and all guests prior to commencement of the trip. Also, please don’t forget to tip the captain and crew for taking care of you!
Allowed food on board:
We allow finger foods, sandwiches, cold cut platters and fruit platters. No soups, greasy foods, or anything with a chance of staining or spilling while underway. Please don’t bring fully catered meals on board we simply won’t be able to serve them and you will end up being disappointed. Moreover, no gas / heat warmers or open flame of any kind is allowed on board. Similarly, no cooking is allowed by anyone on day trips aside from the Hostess warming up something in a microwave. If the boat is left a mess after the trip you will be subjected to a $250-$500 cleaning fee. If you are bringing food, drinks, decorations etc. you must make sure to take it with you after the trip is done. Let’s keep things neat and everyone will enjoy the trip a ton more!
Departure time:
Departure time is set at booking and is a strict deadline. If you are running late on the day of the trip, we cannot extend your time rental of the boat due to your lateness. We are extremely busy through November and more often than not have 2-3 rentals in one day.
Safety onboard the yacht:
No riding, sitting, walking on the bow or the outside swim platform while the boat is underway and in gear. “Bowriding” is illegal in NYC and we will not allow it under any circumstances. You must at all times keep your feet, arms, head etc in the boat to avoid an accident. That means no sitting on rails, seats, side of the boat with feet dangling, and other whacky ideas many people have while on a boat. We take the safety of all the passengers extremely seriously and we take pride in being accident free. Rest assured You will have plenty of opportunities to anchor and freely walk around, take pics etc.
Glass bottles:
No glass champagne bottle “popping” on the boat. The hostess/server is the only one opening bottles and pouring drinks. Guests are not allowed to walk around the vessel with any glass bottles. This is for your safety and that of your crew. Our boat is in immaculate condition, and we like to keep it that way for everyone‘s enjoyment.
Smoking Policy:
Smoking is allowed only on the aft lower deck and absolutely no cigars or hookahs.
No shoes policy:
No street shoes on board - trust us, you will be a lot more comfortable barefoot or in socks. After all, you’re on a boat!
General behavior on board:
All guests must obey all captain’s and hostess’ orders. Even though the captain you have chosen is under your control for the trip, if the Captain feels that the passengers are creating an unsafe environment, they reserve the right to return to the dock at once.

TITLE: Dungeness Crab Charter Seattle | Puget Sound Crabbing | Seattle Nautic
› Crabbing Charter
Dungeness crabbing
Puget Sound Dungeness are among the best crab anywhere. The season is short, the rules are strict, and we handle all of it.
The season is short and specific
Puget Sound crabbing is not open whenever you feel like it. WDFW sets it each year, area by area, and it frequently runs only on .
For is open , and crabbing is permitted — closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
The dates above are for 2026. Always confirm the current rules with WDFW, or call us at and we will tell you what is open on your date.
The rules, plainly
Rule
Puget Sound Dungeness
Daily limit
5 crab
Sex
Males only — females go back
Condition
Hard-shell only
Minimum size
6¼ inches across the carapace
Required
Fishing licence, Puget Sound Crab Endorsement, and a catch record card
Every crabber in the Puget Sound Management Area needs the crab endorsement and a catch record card . Completed summer catch record cards must be reported to WDFW by , whether or not you kept a single crab. People forget this and it carries a penalty.
Sexing and measuring a crab correctly takes practice — get it wrong and it is a citation. On our boat, we do it with you, so you learn it properly.
Why go with a charter instead of a public pier
You can absolutely drop a pot off a public dock. But pressure near shore is heavy, and the crab that survive there are often undersized or soft-shell. Getting to grounds with good structure and less traffic is the difference between five keepers and a bucket of crab you have to throw back.
We supply the pots, the bait, the licence guidance, and the boat that gets you to water worth fishing. You supply the cooler.
What Dungeness are worth
A limit of five hard-shell Dungeness is a serious amount of excellent crab meat. At market prices, the trip often pays for a meaningful share of itself — and it is fresher than anything you can buy, because it was in the water that morning.
When is crab season in Puget Sound?
It varies by year and marine area. In 2026, Marine Area 9 (Admiralty Inlet) is open July 2 through September 7, Thursday through Monday only. Always confirm current WDFW rules.
What is the Dungeness crab limit in Puget Sound?
Five crab per day, males only, hard-shell, minimum 6.25 inches across the carapace.
Do I need a special permit to crab in Puget Sound?
Yes. Every crabber, regardless of age, needs a fishing licence, a Puget Sound Crab Endorsement, and a catch record card. Summer catch cards must be reported to WDFW by October 1.
How do you tell a male crab from a female?
By the shape of the abdominal flap on the underside — narrow and pointed on males, broad and rounded on females. We show you how to do it correctly on the boat.

Thailand tours
Canal cruises through Bangkok. Swimming by the Phi Phi Islands. Your dream tour of Thailand starts here—get going for just $99 and flexible monthly payments.†
With more than 70 million people, Thailand is one of the more populous nations in Southeast Asia. Surprisingly, most Thai people live in rural areas, especially in the country’s northeast region. More than 90% of them practice Theravada Buddhism—an integral part of Thai daily life and cherished customs.
In Bangkok, soaring skyscrapers meet wooden stilt houses and more than 400 temples. Here, the contrasts between tradition and modernity, floating markets and tuk-tuk-filled streets, feel like a celebration of living. Bite into the city—and into some of the best street food in the world.
Why are Thai people so friendly? It might have something to do with “mai pen rai”, or, “no problem”—the Thai tradition of not sweating the small stuff and going with the flow.
A trip to Thailand is for you if you don’t want to have to choose between island-hopping, cultural immersion, wildlife encounters, or dazzling skylines. Our Thailand tours whisk you from electric cities to limestone cliffs and gilded Buddhas to buzzy bazaars.
Snack your way through a night market, learn to whip up Thai delicacies, snorkel off the Phi Phi Islands, and lend a helping hand at an elephant sanctuary.

TITLE: Highlights of Vietnam: Hanoi, Hạ Long Bay & Saigon  | EF Go Ahead Tours
12 days | 15 days with Phú Quốc Island and Hô Chi Minh City extension |
Savor Vietnam’s rich cultural history, lush landscapes, and electrifying flavors
See Vietnam’s unique makeup unfold before your eyes as you tour Hanoi’s prismatic French, Chinese, and Southeast Asian heritage before cruising between the colossal cliffs of Hạ Long Bay. You'll experience the timeless charm of Vietnam in Huế and Hội An, where ancient imperial grandeur meets lantern-lit streets, offering a journey through history and culture. Trace the steps of Vietnamese independence in Hô Chi Minh City—Vietnam's largest city—still known as Saigon to locals and travelers. Along the way, you’ll examine Vietnam War era sites, traverse verdant rice fields, and learn about Vietnamese traditions—like pearl farming—all while treating your taste buds to the spicy, tangy, sweet, and herbal complexity of Vietnamese cuisine. Extend your trip to tropical Phú Quốc and experience island life like no other—with flavors you won’t find anywhere else—before diving into colorful, dense coral reefs on a snorkeling cruise.
1 cooking demonstration
Hỏa Lò Prison
Welcome to Vietnam! Transfer to your hotel to settle in. If you need an invigorating pick-me-up, remember that Vietnamese coffee, or cà phê, is typically brewed strong and sweetened with condensed milk.
Pass Ba Đình Square, where Hồ Chí Minh—the revolutionary leader and president of North Vietnam—read the Proclamation of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.
Wander through the 11th-century Temple of Literature, a walled complex that’s dedicated to the Chinese philosopher Confucius and site of Vietnam’s first university.
Visit the site of Hỏa Lò Prison—the notorious “Hanoi Hilton”—where late U.S. Senator John McCain was held as a prisoner of war (POW) for more than five years during the Vietnam War.
Board a bicycle rickshaw and ride through the busy Old Quarter, an area that’s rich with Vietnamese architecture—picture wooden shutters and wrought-iron balconies—as well as hidden courtyards and gardens, locally owned shops, and street food vendors.
Pass Đồng Xuân Market (one of the largest wholesale markets in the north of Vietnam), the Hanoi Opera House (inspired by the Second Empire architecture of the Palais Garnier in Paris), and Hoàn Kiếm Lake (its name, which translates to Lake of the Restored Sword, derives from a 15th century Vietnamese legend).
Get to know your Tour Director and fellow travelers during this afternoon's welcome lunch, served with beer.
Vietnamese culture places a strong emphasis on sharing meals with guests. Add an optional excursion to enjoy a home-hosted dinner of Vietnamese specialties with a local family. Up to exploring on your own? Use your free time today to go back to Hanoi’s French Quarter or take a cyclo—a cycle rickshaw—ride through the city’s narrow streets for the ultimate way of getting around
From $105 CAD per person
Experience the dramatic emerald valleys and towering seaside cliffs of Vietnam on an optional excursion. Bask in these views from a row boat on an optional excursion to Ninh Bình’s Tam Cốc village where you'll sail past rice paddies and limestone mountains.
Not joining the excursion? Use your free day in Hanoi to take in a traditional water puppet performance showcasing Vietnamese folklore and culture, visit the Vietnam Fine Art Museum or sit down with locals at one of Hanoi’s atmospheric cafes.
From $165 CAD per person
Day 5: Hạ Long Bay cruise
Transfer to Hạ Long Bay and embark on a luxurious, overnight cruise. As you explore the emerald waters of this striking setting and UNESCO World Heritage Site by boat, you’ll pass by many of its nearly 2,000 limestone islands and islets, most of which are uninhabited and unaffected by human presence.
Cruise past notable natural features, including Fighting Cocks Islet’s pair of limestone islets—shaped like a rooster and a hen—as well as Thien Cung Cave, and Dau Go Cave.
Climb aboard a small tender with a guide from your ship and motor across the water to Sung Sot Cave—the largest and, according to many, most beautiful cave in the bay. Discovered in 1901, the cave’s stalagmites and stalactites are lit by multicolored lights.
Get back on board your tender for a ride to your next stop, Tung San Pearl Farm—pearl farming is an important source of livelihood for local communities—where you’ll learn how pearls are grown using traditional Vietnamese methods and new Japanese technology.
Hội An
Day 6: Ti Top Island & flight to Hội An
Join a sunrise lesson in Tai Chi—a gentle form of exercise that originated in China as a martial art—on the ship this morning, if you’re up for it. Then, hop into a small boat and make your way to Ti Top Island for time spent swimming or hiking to the top of the island—summit height is about 360 feet or 110 meters—to enjoy panoramic views of Hạ Long Bay’s island-dotted waters.
After enjoying an included lunch, disembark your cruise ship and board a flight to Da Nang. Then, transfer to your hotel in Hội An.
Freshen up at your hotel and gather with your fellow travelers this evening for an included dinner served with beer.
Day 7: Sightseeing tour of Hội An & rice farm visit
Explore Hội An on a guided tour to shop its markets where you’ll be sure to find the perfect Vietnamese keepsake to bring home.
Discover the city’s landmarks, including the ornate Japanese covered bridge and Old Town, which has retained its charm as a major trading port and is now a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site.
Pass by the quaint Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai pedestrian shopping street and its colorful, eye-catching stalls.
Walk the town’s cobblestone streets to see the 18th century Quan Thang Ancient House with its majestic wooden carvings and silk lantern shop.
This afternoon, pay a visit to Cẩm Thanh village, known as the Coconut Village, located in the Bay Mau coconut forest.
Visit a farm to learn how Vietnamese farmers grow rice in the fields.
Sit down for a family-style lunch at the farm.
Interact with a rice farmer and watch water buffalo plow the fields while enjoying a tea tasting.
After sampling Vietnamese delicacies, how about trying your hand at preparing them yourself? Add an optional excursion to take a hands-on cooking class or return to Hội An and enjoy a free evening in the city perusing a night market or relaxing by the river.
Hội An Vietnamese Cooking Class & Dinner
From $89 CAD per person
Huế
Day 8: Transfer to Huế & sightseeing tour
Travel through the Hài Vân Pass as you make your way to Huế, famous for imperial and colonial history, all set along the peaceful “Perfume River”.
Explore the Thiên Mụ Pagoda, Vietnam’s tallest religious building. Built in 1601, it’s been preserved, expanded, and enhanced for generations to become the unofficial symbol of Huế.
Visit the fortress and palace known as the Imperial City, surrounded by massive stone walls that stretch for 1.5 miles and punctuated with large gateways and protective moats.
Cross the historic Thanh Toan Bridge, an ornate covered wooden footbridge built in the 18th century, and explore its adjacent Agricultural Tools Exhibition where traditional farming implements showcase the region's rich agricultural heritage that has sustained Vietnamese rural life for centuries.
Enjoy an included dinner with beer this evening with your group.
Day 9: Free day in Huế & evening flight to Hô Chi Minh City
With your free day in Huế today, add an optional excursion that further delves into Nguyễn dynasty emperors and their impressive tombs. If you’re heading off on your own, ask your Tour Director for a recommendation. We suggest continuing to explore the traditional houses in the city center, checking out the treasures in the Huế Royal Antiquities Museum, and of course, try local specialties like Huế-style crepes and sweet dessert soups.
Later, board your flight to Hô Chi Minh City. Hô Chi Minh City was officially renamed from Saigon on April 30, 1975, the same day Saigon fell to North Vietnamese

Frequently asked questions
Everything you need to know before you fly. Still curious? — phone reservations are available 24/7.
Give us a call
The 800' flight is $95 per person and non-flying passengers are $40 per person at most locations — see each location page for exact rates and current deals. No added taxes or booking fees; everything is included. You decide how high you want to go when you check in.
Flights range from 8 to 10 minutes.

No. The captain and mate do all the work — if you can sit, you can fly.

Only if you want to. Near the end of the flight the captain can slow the boat and dip your feet in the water for a refreshing splash — or keep you completely dry. Just let us know.
For your safety, pregnant women are not able to parasail or ride on the boat. Please come back and see us next year.

Flyers must be at least 5 years old and 45 lbs. Guests under 18 must have an adult sign them in. The oldest person we've flown was 102 — parasailing is safe and exciting for all ages.
Yes — we offer tandem and triple flights, side by side in the same chute. If combined weight is over 500 lbs, the captain makes the call based on conditions.
Minimum combined weight is 180 lbs; maximum combined is 450 lbs, at the captain's discretion depending on wind conditions.
You can change your mind, but the fare isn't refunded. It rarely happens — more often observers see how gentle it is and ask to fly.

Quite the opposite — it's serene and peaceful. Takeoffs and landings are slow and gradual, so there's nothing frightening about it.

Flyers descend slowly and safely into the water, where mandatory life jackets keep them afloat until they're pulled back onto the boat. The parasail won't sink or come down over your head. The captain gives every group a full safety briefing before flight.
Dress for the weather — long sleeves if it's cool or you're sun-sensitive. Bathing suits and beach attire are always good, plus towels, water, and sunblock. Leave behind anything water-sensitive, expensive, or hard to replace; we're not responsible for damaged or lost items.
At your own discretion — consider the height and water risk. Disposable cameras are best, or grab our digital photo package.
30 photos of your adventure. The crew documents your entire flight on a high-quality digital camera, and you take the memory card home for bragging rights.

Three ways: book online through our reservation pages, call anytime (phone reservations are available 24/7), or walk up to any of our ticket offices.
Yes — a great gift for special occasions. We'll have them ready for pickup or mail them at no extra charge. They never expire and are valid at all of our California locations.
