How much do Lightning Lane passes cost? Answer
  • Multi Pass: A Lightning Lane Multi Pass starts at $34 USD per ticket per day. Prices and availability vary by date.
  • Single Pass: Prices for Lightning Lane Single Passes vary by date and attraction. This option may be purchased individually for up to 2 different Lightning Lane Single Pass attractions each day.
  • Premier Pass: Prices for Lightning Lane Premier Passes vary by date and demand. Prices will be displayed in the Disneyland app up to 7 days in advance of your park visit.

Purchasing is subject to limited availability.

Valid Admission and Park Reservations Required
In order to purchase and use a Lightning Lane pass, you must have valid park admission and a park reservation for the theme park you plan to visit. To visit more than one park, your park admission must include Park Hopper benefits.

Important Information
Products and services are fulfilled in the Disneyland app. App is intended for use in the US only. Currently, the app is only available in English.

What are the photo perks included with Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Lightning Lane Premier Pass?

Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Lightning Lane Premier Pass include the following photo perks:

  • Get unlimited downloads of Disney PhotoPass digital photos from your park day—including attraction photos and snapshots taken by select in-park photographers.
  • Unlock Disney PhotoPass Lenses, which let you transform your photos with Disney-themed, augmented-reality effects.

Disney PhotoPass digital photo downloads exclude separately priced Disney PhotoPass packages and products offered at select locations. Disney PhotoPass service is subject to the Disney PhotoPass Terms and Conditions and expiration policy. Online registration required.

Does Lightning Lane Multi Pass include access to Lightning Lane Single Pass attractions?

No. When you purchase a Lightning Lane Multi Pass, you can choose from a variety of eligible multi pass attractions.

For single pass attractions, Lightning Lane entry is only available with the purchase of a Lightning Lane Single Pass or Lightning Lane Premier Pass.

I’m visiting with a Walt Disney Travel Company package, when can I purchase Lightning Lane Premier Pass?

Guests visiting with a Walt Disney Travel Company package are welcome to purchase Lightning Lane Premier Pass when they receive their park tickets 2 days in advance of their arrival, subject to availability. For questions, call (714) 520-6222.

How do Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Lightning Lane Single Pass differ from Disney Genie+ service and individual Lightning Lane entry?

Disney Genie+ service was renamed to Lightning Lane Multi Pass, and individual Lightning Lane entrance access was renamed to Lightning Lane Single Pass. Lightning Lane Premier Pass was introduced as another pass option, to provide added convenience and flexibility.

Besides the updated names for the services, there were no changes to the redemption or queue experience.

Using Lightning Lane Passes How can I make the most of my Lightning Lane Multi Pass?

Here are some tips for using your Lightning Lane Multi Pass:

Get Started
As soon as you enter a theme park, use the Disneyland app to choose a Lightning Lane Multi Pass attraction and book the next available time to ride it.

Unlock Adventures All Day
Once you've redeemed your selection (or after 2 hours have passed since you made your selection), you can book your next Lightning Lane Multi Pass attraction. You can make Lightning Lane selections one at a time throughout the day.

Modify Your Plans
Changed your plans… or your mind? You can modify your Lightning Lane selections via the Disneyland app.

Can I use a Lightning Lane Multi Pass and a Lightning Lane Single Pass on the same day? Yes. You may purchase a Lightning Lane Multi Pass and a Lightning Lane Single Pass for the same day, subject to availability. How long do I have to wait before I can select a new Lightning Lane Multi Pass attraction? Lightning Lane Multi Pass selections can only be made one at a time. Once you’ve redeemed your selection (or after 2 hours have passed since you made your selection), you can book your next Lightning Lane Multi Pass attraction. Can a Lightning Lane Multi Pass and a Lightning Lane Premier Pass be used in both Disneyland Resort theme parks on the same day?

Yes. Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Lightning Lane Premier Pass can be used for entry to Lightning Lane attraction queues at both Disneyland Park and Disney California Adventure Park in the same day, during regular park hours.

Just be sure your valid park admission includes the Park Hopper benefit.

If you have a 1-park ticket, then your Lightning Lane Multi Pass or Lightning Lane Premier Pass can only be used in the theme park that you visit that day. The price of a Lightning Lane pass does not vary based on the number of theme parks you visit that day; it cannot be discounted or refunded.

How do I keep track of my Lightning Lane passes and available experiences?

On the day of your visit, use the Disneyland app to view your passes—and keep track of the fun! Just tap the ≡ menu in the Disneyland app, then select "My Plans" to view your passes—as well as selected attractions and arrival windows (if applicable).

What Are the Best Deep Sea Fishing Techniques to Increase Your Catch and Have More Successful Trips?
Success offshore comes from matching the right technique to the species, depth, and conditions. Technique determines how you present bait and where you position the boat. Trolling covers wide areas to find roaming pelagics, bottom fishing targets reefs and wrecks, jigging provokes reaction strikes from suspended fish, and chumming brings feeding fish in close. Each method delivers different results: trolling finds tuna and other pelagics when baitfish are spread out, while jigging and bottom rigs produce snapper and grouper when you’re on structure. Below are captain-tested, easy-to-follow tips you can use on North Myrtle Beach charters to raise bite rates and spend more time on productive water.
The most reliable approaches focus on speed, rigging, and presentation. Start broad with trolling or sonar to locate fish, then switch to jigging or bottom baits when you mark structure or active fish. Combine these tactics and you’ll quickly see how local tweaks make a big difference.
Trolling, bottom fishing, and jigging are the core offshore methods for boosting catch rates and targeting trophy fish.
Matching speed, lure size, and bait presentation to the species drastically improves hookups and landing rates.
Switching methods when you see sonar marks or bird activity often turns an average day into a productive one.
These steps explain how to run each method on a charter and transition smoothly when conditions change, using captain positioning to maximize results.
Before diving into advanced strategies, make sure you’ve mastered the that form the foundation of successful offshore angling. These fundamentals work hand in hand with the tactical approaches we’ll discuss here.

How Does Trolling Help You Catch More Fish in Myrtle Beach with Proven Strategies?
Trolling raises your odds by covering large areas to find roaming predators like tuna and billfish. The method works by presenting moving lures or bait at speeds that mimic schooling forage. Typical trolling speeds run 5–10 knots depending on the species and lure: slower for big, slow-moving lures aimed at cobia or amberjack, faster for small skirted lures when chasing tuna. Run a spread of teasers, plugs, and a bait off the stern to create multiple strike zones, and stagger depths with downriggers or weighted lines. Watch for diving birds, current lines, and bait schools — when you see those signs, slow down and add live-bait rigs to turn locating into hookups and more landed fish.
Trolling spreads and rig choices change with the morning bite and sea state, so adjust as you learn local patterns or follow the captain’s lead. A good troll can quickly lead to live-bait work when fish are keyed to surface schools.
What Are Effective Bottom Fishing and Jigging Methods for Landing Trophy Fish?
Bottom fishing and jigging put your bait where fish hang — reefs, wrecks, edges, and other hard structure — and match sink rate and action to how the species feed. For bottom rigs use a fish-finder or high-low setup with breakaway sinkers sized to hold bottom in the current; pick sinker weight so your bait stays near structure. Jigging is all about cadence: lift the rod 2–3 feet, then let the jig fall on a slack line to trigger reaction strikes from amberjack, snapper, and groupers. Vary lift speed and pause time until fish respond.
Use sonar marks and depth contours to position the boat up-current of your target, then drift or anchor as conditions allow to present baits in the strike zone. Clean rigging and correct cadence reduce lost fish and improve hookup strength — and they set you up to pick the right live and artificial baits for trophy targets.
Which Bait and Lures Work Best for Trophy-Worthy Deep Sea Catches?
Right bait or lure choice directly affects strike quality. Pick baits by target species, depth, and what forage is in the water. Live bait like menhaden or pilchards sparks natural strikes from tuna and kingfish; cut or strip baits sit well on bottom rigs for grouper and snapper. Artificial options — skirted trolling lures, metal jigs, and large soft plastics — work when they match local baitfish size and action or when flash and contrast provoke reaction strikes. What Live Baits Work Best for Trophy Species in Myrtle Beach?
Match live bait to local forage to get natural strikes. Pilchards are great for surface-feeding pelagics; small threadfin or croaker work well for bottom species. Hook live bait through the back or lips so it swims naturally and keep sinkers light enough to let the bait move in midwater or at the surface. For bigger fish like tuna use a small hook with a short fluorocarbon leader to cut visibility; switch to heavier leaders and circle hooks for toothy, bottom-oriented species. What is inshore fishing in Tampa Bay?

What is the best time of year for inshore fishing in Tampa Bay?
Tampa Bay offers productive inshore fishing throughout the year. Your private charter includes the boat, captain, rods, reels, tackle, bait, and fishing equipment needed for the trip. Guests should bring weather-appropriate clothing, sun protection, food and drinks they would like during the trip, and any personal items they may need.
Should I choose an inshore or deep sea fishing charter in Tampa?
Inshore fishing is ideal for anglers who want to fish Tampa Bay’s flats, mangroves, passes, and protected waters for species such as snook, redfish, and trout. generally involves traveling farther into the Gulf to target offshore species such as grouper and snapper. TITLE: Winter Tampa Fishing Charters (Dec, Jan, Feb)
Winter Tampa Fishing Charters (Dec. –Feb.)
As winter approaches and the water temperatures begin to drop, a thrilling transformation occurs in the world of fishing. It’s like nature is putting on a spectacular show just for anglers, with the Trout bite turning sizzling hot and the Redfish eagerly waving their tails as they forage for delectable morsels. If that’s not enough to get you excited, the scrumptious Sheepshead make their grand entrance, swarming the area’s reefs and canal systems. What a fantastic time to be an angler!
This is the perfect season to experiment with artificial lures or try your hand at fly fishing, as the fish are more active and eager to bite. Captain Tim, an expert in sight fishing, is your go-to guide for these exhilarating angling adventures. With his trusty skiff and exceptional skills at poling the flats, Captain Tim will lead you on a thrilling hunt for Redfish in their natural habitats.
But wait, there’s more! You may also find yourself cruising the area’s creeks and rivers on a spacious bay boat, where you’ll have the opportunity to reel in a variety of amazing catches. From Sheepshead, Redfish, and Trout to Snook and even the occasional juvenile Tarpon, you’ll be in for a fishing experience like no other.
To make the most of this incredible time of year, we suggest booking a 4 or 6-hour trip with Captain Tim. You’ll not only enjoy a memorable day out on the water, but also learn valuable tips and techniques that will elevate your angling skills to new heights.
So don’t let the winter chill keep you away from the water. Embrace the season, grab your fishing gear, and join Captain Tim for a remarkable fishing adventure that you’ll cherish for years to come!

=== PAGE: https://www.swiftfishcharters.com/spring-tampa-fishing-charters/
TITLE: Spring Tampa Fishing Charters (Mar, Apr, May)
As the warm embrace of spring caresses the waters, the flats come alive with a vibrant display of marine life. It’s an exciting time as the snook make their way out of the canals, creeks, and rivers, eager to feast on scrumptious sardines in preparation for their summer spawning. The anticipation is palpable, and you can almost hear the underwater symphony as the snook’s appetite grows.
Meanwhile, redfish gather in ever-increasing numbers, ready to put on a show for any eager angler. And let’s not forget the big gator trout – these voracious predators are on a mission, devouring everything that crosses their path. It’s a thrilling time to be on the water, as every cast could bring the catch of a lifetime.
As late spring blossoms, the flats welcome even more visitors. The Spanish mackerel, kingfish, and cobia make their grand entrance, adding to the already bustling underwater scene. These pelagic species join the party, offering a thrilling challenge for any angler up to the task.
Most of this exhilarating action is best experienced from the comfort of a Bay Boat. However, don’t think you’re limited to just live bait! The fish are more than happy to chomp down on artificials, making it a fantastic time for those who enjoy tossing plastics. The versatile Bay Boat allows you to get up close and personal with these majestic creatures while casting your favorite lures.
For the optimal fishing adventure, we recommend embarking on a 6 or 8-hour trip. This will give you plenty of time to soak in the beautiful surroundings, immerse yourself in the vibrant marine life, and, of course, reel in some unforgettable catches. As you set out on this exhilarating journey, you’ll soon understand why this magical time of year is truly a fisherman’s dream come true. So grab your gear, gather your friends, and join us for an unforgettable experience on the water!

=== PAGE: https://www.swiftfishcharters.com/summer-tampa-fishing-charters/
TITLE: Summer Tampa Fishing Charters (Jun, Jul, Aug)
Summer Tampa Fishing Charters (June-Aug.)
As the temperature rises, so does the activity in the bay, making it a perfect time for anglers to try their luck. Currently, schools of mackerel are foraging all over the bay, providing plenty of opportunities for some enjoyable fishing. These feisty fish are known to target bait schools, making them an exciting catch for those using light tackle. With their aggressive strikes and spirited action, mackerel offer a satisfying experience for anglers of all ages and abilities.
For the more seasoned fisherman or those looking to cross a big catch off their bucket list, the Tarpon run is also underway. This fishing endeavor is not for those simply looking to fill their cooler or catch a large number of fish. Rather, it’s an opportunity to test one’s patience and skill, as anglers often spend long periods waiting for that perfect moment to strike.
When the time comes, be prepared for a challenging battle, as these impressive game fish put up a strong fight. Overcoming the physical demands of reeling in a Tarpon will make the victory even more rewarding.
To fully take advantage of this season’s offerings, consider booking a 4 or 6-hour trip based on your fishing preferences. This is the perfect opportunity to create lasting memories on the water while experiencing the thrill of the catch.

TITLE: Accelerated Multi-Engine Flight Training in Florida
Accelerated multi-engine training is one of the fastest ways to level up your flying and get closer to airline goals. In South Florida, consistent VFR days, long daylight, and busy airspace give you a lot of quality learning in a short window. When you match that environment with a clear plan, you can move from first lesson to checkride efficiently and with confidence.
At our South Florida bases, we use a structured, airline-style approach so motivated pilots can finish a multi-engine rating in weeks instead of months. In this guide, we will walk through a practical timeline, a sample weekly syllabus, how flight blocks work, why stage checks matter, and how to turn time-building flights into focused checkride prep. We will also explain how our limited-time $100 off promo for multi-engine training in Florida, available through August 15, fits into a bigger airline pathway plan.
A realistic accelerated plan usually looks like one of these:
Full-time: about 7, 14 days of focused training
Part-time: around 3, 4 weeks with several flights each week
To get the most from this pace, you should already have:
At least a private pilot certificate, ideally with an instrument rating
A current medical and recent flight time
Comfortable basic instrument skills and radio work
The training flow generally moves in this order:
Aircraft and systems orientation, performance and limitations
Basic VFR maneuvers in the twin
Engine-out procedures and single-engine handling
IFR and abnormal operations in a multi-engine setting
Final checkride polishing, both oral and flight
We schedule early-morning flights to stay ahead of heat and afternoon storms. Midday is perfect for ground lessons on systems, performance, and procedures while the weather is unsettled. When useful, we add evening simulator sessions to run through engine failures, IFR scenarios, and checklists in a low-stress setting.
This progression follows the same kind of order you see in airline training: learn the airplane, add abnormal situations step by step, then tie everything together with good decision-making and crew-style habits.
Here is how a two-week accelerated plan often looks.
Week 1 focuses on getting comfortable in the twin and learning the basics:
Multi-engine systems and performance
VMC awareness and aerodynamics
Takeoffs, landings, and pattern work
Basic engine-out drills and directional control
A typical day in Week 1 might include:
A 2 to 3 hour flight block in the morning
Short preflight brief to set goals and review procedures
Focused debrief right after landing with notes for self-study
Week 2 builds on that base and adds more complex situations:
Advanced engine-out scenarios, including at altitude and near the airport
Single-engine instrument approaches
Emergency procedures and checklist discipline
Mock checkrides, both oral and flight, to bring everything together
Flight block scheduling keeps your day predictable:
Set AM or PM blocks so you can plan rest, meals, and study
Dedicated time windows for briefing and debriefing
Space for self-study, chair flying, and checklist practice
Flexible re-booking when South Florida weather offers learning chances like real in-flight deviations or IFR work
Our instructors watch your performance in each block and adjust the intensity. If a maneuver is not yet at Airman Certification Standards level, we use quick reviews and short “micro-checks” at the start of the next flight to clean it up before adding new tasks.
In an accelerated course, it is easy to feel like everything is happening fast. Stage checks help keep that speed from turning into stress. A stage check is a structured progress check with a different instructor. The goal is to spot weak spots early and make sure there are no surprises on the practical test.
Typical stage check points include:
After initial maneuvers and basic multi-engine handling
After main engine-out training and single-engine operations
Final mock oral and mock flight just before the checkride
Each stage check gives you clear feedback on:
Airwork: steep turns, slow flight, stalls in the twin
Engine-out skills: identification, feathering, directional control
Systems understanding: fuel, electrical, props, performance
Checklist use, situational awareness, and cockpit communication
The notes from the stage check shape your next few days. You might see:
A focused remedial flight on one or two weak maneuvers
Extra ground time on a system you are not fully comfortable with
Repetition of previously weak items until they feel routine
This stage-check rhythm is similar to airline and crew training, where independent checks are normal and expected. It encourages a professional attitude and helps you think like a multi-crew pilot, even when you are flying with just one instructor.
If you need multi-engine hours for airline or Part 135 goals, you do not want to just “burn gas.” Cross-country time-building can double as targeted checkride prep when it is planned well.
Good time-building legs around South Florida might include:
Coastal cross-country routes that mix busy airspace with smoother segments
Real-world IFR when appropriate, including clearances and approach work
Fuel planning and performance calculations that account for weight, balance, and hot weather
On these flights, instructors can weave in:
Engine-out simulations at safe altitudes
Emergency checklist practice and systems discussions
Single-engine approaches under the hood or in real IMC when suitable
Constant cockpit resource management, including workload sharing and briefings
After you earn the rating, our fleet and rental options give you ways to keep building quality multi time. TITLE: Florida Flight School Tour Checklist for Beginners
Training in Florida sounds pretty great. Lots of flying days, long daylight hours, and busy airspace that keeps you sharp. That is exactly why picking the right aviation school in Florida matters so much. You are not just choosing airplanes; you are choosing the habits, safety mindset, and support system that will shape you as a pilot.
This checklist is built to help you walk into any school tour with confidence. We will walk through what to ask on the tour, what to look for in aircraft maintenance records, and how to compare instructor availability and scheduling. When you visit schools, look for a clear, professional setup, like what we aim for at our South Florida campus: structured programs, organized operations, and a team that welcomes your questions.
Go into your tour with questions ready. You are not being picky, you are doing your homework.
For training structure and safety culture, ask things like:
How is training laid out from discovery flight to advanced ratings and airline-track options?
What standard operating procedures do students follow on every flight?
How often will someone review your progress with you, and what do stage checks look like?
You want to hear that safety is built into every lesson, not just a poster on the wall. Ask how they teach risk management from day one and how they expect students to speak up about concerns.
For fleet quality, availability, and weather readiness, try questions such as:
How many training aircraft are there compared with the number of active students?
In late summer, when Florida gets busy and stormy, how long do students usually wait for a booking?
What kind of avionics do the airplanes have, and how does that support your long-term goals, like airline or corporate flying?
Florida afternoons can bring storms and high heat. Ask how they plan the schedule around early mornings, mid-day breaks, and fast-changing conditions.
For student support and campus environment, ask:
Do they offer ground school, tutoring, or checkride prep?
Are there quiet places to study and good transportation or housing options nearby?
Can you meet current students and instructors and ask them about communication, feedback, and overall culture?
You should walk away with a clear picture of how it will feel to train there day after day.
You do not need to be a mechanic to spot basic clues in maintenance records. Ask to see:
Airframe and engine logbooks
Entries for annual inspections and 100-hour inspections
Notes about major repairs or parts replacements
Learn a few key terms:
required every 12 calendar months
required for aircraft used for training or hire every 100 flight hours
proof that Airworthiness Directives from the authorities have been addressed
A professional aviation school in Florida should be glad to walk you through these pages at your pace and explain what you are seeing.
Look for green flags like:
Recent, steady inspection entries without big gaps
Clear signatures and certificate numbers from mechanics
Specific notes that show ADs have been handled, not just “checked OK”
Watch for red flags, for example:
Long gaps between inspections or unclear dates
The same system, like brakes or radios, breaking again and again
Messy, vague notes that are hard to read or understand
Also ask how the school handles squawks, which are issues students or instructors report after flights. Good questions include:
How do we report a problem with an aircraft?
How fast are aircraft taken out of service when there is a concern?
Who decides when an airplane is ready to return to training?
Well-maintained airplanes usually mean fewer last-minute cancellations. Ask about their past cancellation rates for maintenance and weather, especially during storm season, and what backup plans they have if several aircraft are down.
Your relationship with your instructor and the schedule you can keep will shape your progress more than almost anything else.
Ask about instructor loads and availability:
How many students does a typical instructor handle?
What does a normal training week look like for a student who flies two or three times per week?
Are instructors available in the evenings or on weekends if you work or go to school?
Continuity matters, so ask if you will stay with one main instructor from discovery flight up to the checkride, and what happens if that instructor leaves for another job.
Then look at the scheduling system itself. Ask to see the actual app or platform they use. Check:
Is aircraft and instructor availability shown in real time?
Are cancellation and no-show policies easy to understand?
How far ahead can you book, change, or cancel, especially during late summer when schedules fill fast?
Instructor turnover and communication habits can also affect your training. Good questions include:
How often do instructors move on, and how are students supported when that happens?
If an instructor leaves, how do you get matched with a new one and brought up to speed?
Who will be your main point of contact for planning and questions?
Pay attention to how quickly they reply to your emails or calls when setting up the tour. That is usually the same level of response you will get once you are a student.
Money and time both matter, so get a clear picture before you commit.
To understand total training cost, ask for written estimates for each phase, such as:
Private Pilot
Make sure the estimate explains what is included:
Aircraft rental and instructor time
Ground instruction and briefings
Exam fees and checkride fees
Any extra costs like books, headsets, charts, or simulator time
Ask how they adjust estimates if things like fuel or insurance change so you are not surprised later.
For financing, payment options, and refund policies, ask:
Are there financing programs, scholarships, or payment plans for full-time or airline-track students?
Do you pay as you go, or do they ask for funds in advance?
If you need to pause training because of life events or weather, how are balances handled?
Timelines are just as important. Ask about average completion times for each rating at that school and how Florida weather fits into those plans. Good follow-ups include:
How do you keep students on track when afternoons are stormy?
What is the plan during busy seasons or when big weather systems affect flying?
How many lessons per week do you recommend to build skills quickly and avoid backtracking?
Look for a school that is honest about the work it takes but also ready with strategies to keep you moving.
Bring a photo ID, a notebook or a digital device for notes, a list of questions, and comfortable clothes and shoes for walking around the ramp and hangars. If you want a discovery flight, ask ahead about any extra items they might need.
Many students earn a Private Pilot License in a few months when they can train two or three times a week and stay consistent with study. The exact timeline depends on your schedule, weather, and how steady your training rhythm is.
Yes, as long as the school respects weather limits. Good schools plan more flights in the morning and use radar and forecasts to avoid storms. They should never pressure you to fly in conditions you are not comfortable with.
Visiting at least two or three schools helps you compare culture, aircraft condition, instructor access, and scheduling systems. Seeing different campuses makes it easier to notice what feels organized and supportive for you.

About Myrtle Beach Segway
Myrtle Beach Segway is an authorized dealer and service center for the Segway Personal Transporter (PT), and your source for Segway PT products and services in the Carolinas. Our goal is to make these areas Segway PT friendly while offering the latest in eco-friendly transportation. Our customers are our number one priority.
For your pleasure we offer a variety of PT and suited to your needs.

Advance purchase is highly recommended for our Segway PT Tours! Come out and ride today. The Eco-Friendly way to play!

Come and join us for a Segway PT Glide at one of the Grand Strand’s nicest venues. We are located at the North Myrtle Beach Park & Sports Complex. This complex offers a variety of sports venues as well as fun activities for the whole family. The Segway PT Experience includes a brief training session to assure that all patrons are fully versed as to the function and safety while riding a Segway PT. Then off on the glide, starting with a cruise around the complex for some fun “gliding”, and then into the woods we go for some nature, shade and photo ops! This is a great family activity and is fun to do. Back in the woods is somewhat challenging and fun. Experienced riders will enjoy this course.

Limited to eight patrons on each tour. With advanced notice, we can handle larger groups. Please call for details.
Come and join us for a Segway PT Glide at one of the Grand Strand’s most beautiful wetland and wildlife preserves. Nature lovers will enjoy the park’s Environmental Education Center and the chance to see loggerhead turtles and other endangered plant and animal species up close. The park’s freshwater lake along the causeway is a sure-fire place to see alligators basking in the sun, a variety of bird species like Anhingas and Ospreys. Known for its natural beauty, Huntington Beach State Park was the former winter home of Anna Hyatt and Archer Huntington, sculptress and philanthropist, respectively, who left the park and adjacent Brookgreen Gardens as their legacy. There’s also Atalaya, the picturesque, Moorish-style castle which was their residence and sculpting studios. This tour is around two hours in length with training. Still plenty of time to enjoy the beach and relax before or after your “Segway PT Experience”. If you plan on enjoying the park before or after, pack a lunch. There are no food facilities in the park.

FAQ’s
Do I have to purchase tickets in advance?
Advance purchase is strongly recommended, as tours often sell out quickly. To maximize your chance of getting the day and time you prefer, please book well in advance. You can do this online or over the phone using only Visa, Mastercard, Discover or American Express.
Who can ride the Segway PT?
Although riding a Segway PT is relatively easy, a minimum of about 70 pounds is needed to stop the machine. Also, riders should have the ability to make motions such as climbing and descending stairs without assistance. The Segway PT is not appropriate for those weighing under 70 pounds or over 300 pounds. Those with physical impairments should use caution as the Segway PT is not meant for everyone. Please call before booking to inquire if you are able to ride.
I have children in my group that are under 12 years old. Can they still come on the tour?
Call us and we will do our best to accommodate your group. An adult or guardian must accompany children under 18.
When should I arrive?
We ask that you arrive at our location 20-30 minutes prior to your tour start time for preparation and paperwork.
How much time of the tour is actually spent on a Segway PT?
The majority of your time will be on the Segway PT. We will start off with a short training session and then be on the Segway PT for the remainder of the time. There are stops along the way to rest and take pictures.
How do I learn to ride a Segway PT?
All customers are required to take a hands-on training session to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. Riders are trained on Segway PT operation and safety. All riders are required to wear a safety helmet. You can bring your own.
What happens if it rains?
We maintain contact with the patrons for weather issues. The tours can be done in light rain.
What if I have to cancel?
Purchased tickets are non-refundable since your space is being guaranteed on the tour. If you think you can’t make your scheduled tour time, give us a call and we can reschedule you subject to availability.
Do I have to sign a waiver?
All Segway PT riders must sign a liability waiver before participating. Riders under the age of 18 must have a parent or guardian sign for them.
Do Segway PTs have the ability to store bags or purses?
We have the ability to transport necessary items i.e. cameras, phones, drinks, etc. These can be carried in the Segway PT bag on each unit.
What to wear and what to bring?
Always wear comfortable clothes and footwear. Closed toe shoes are preferred. Bring drinks with you, especially during the Summer months. Tips for your guide!
Are restrooms available?
Yes, restrooms are available at the meeting location, but there are no easily accessible restroom stops along the tour route. If you should need to stop, please let us know and we will try to accommodate you.
What is the Segway Personal Transporter (PT)?
The Segway Personal Transporter (PT) is the first self-balancing, electric-powered transportation device. With dimensions no larger than the average adult body and the ability to emulate human balance, the Segway PT uses the same space as a pedestrian, and can go wherever a person can walk.
How fast do the Segway PTs go?
Segway PTs have a top speed of 12.5 mph. Myrtle Beach Segway does not limit your speed. The Segway PTs were designed to have fun and we love to have fun. Just look at the customer ratings!
How safe is the Segway PT?
The utmost care and research has gone into ensuring that the Segway PT is safe. The Segway PT’s balancing technology is truly revolutionary and provides an exceptional riding experience. The Segway PT has redundant systems and sophisticated alerts built into its design, and many thousands of hours of use have demonstrated that the Segway PT is safe when used appropriately. It is important that Segway PT riders understand their responsibility to ride safely. Proper skill level and understanding of the Segway PT prevents injuries caused by loss of control or misuse.
How does the Segway PT work?
This breakthrough technology, termed “dynamic stabilization,” is the essence of the Segway PT. Dynamic stabilization enables the Segway PT to work seamlessly with the body’s movements. Gyroscopes and tilt sensors in the unit monitor a rider’s center of gravity at about 100 times a second. When the rider leans slightly forward, the Segway PT moves forward. When the rider leans slightly back, the Segway PT moves backward.
Are Segway PT rentals available through Myrtle Beach Segway?
No. We only offer guided tours.
Can I arrange for a private/corporate/business event?
Yes, we offer private group tours, up to 25 Segway PTs, for corporate functions and private events. For more information, please contact Myrtle Beach Segway at 843-477-0800 or email .

Some of the Amazing Sites at the Oregon Coast
Here are just some of the amazing sites to see from the air once we take flight from our Seaside launch pad:
Tillamook Lighthouse
Tillamook Rock Light is a deactivated lighthouse on the northern Oregon Coast of the United States. It is located approximately 1.2 miles offshore from Tillamook Head, and 20 miles south of the mouth of the Columbia River near Astoria, situated on less than an acre of basalt rock in the Pacific Ocean.
Haystack Rock
Haystack Rock is a 235 ft-tall (72 m) sea stack in Cannon Beach, Oregon. It is often stated locally to be the third-tallest such intertidal structure in the world, but there are no supporting credible references for this claim. A popular tourist destination on the Oregon Coast, the monolithic rock is adjacent to the beach and accessible by foot at low tide. The Haystack Rock tide pools are home to many intertidal animals, including starfish, sea anemone, crabs, chitons, limpets, and sea slugs. The rock is also a nesting site for many sea birds, including terns and puffins.
Astoria Column
The Astoria Column is a tower in the northwest United States, overlooking the mouth of the Columbia River on Coxcomb Hill in Astoria, Oregon. Built in 1926, the concrete and steel structure is part of a 30-acre (12 ha) city park. The 125-foot (38 m)-tall column has a 164-step spiral staircase ascending to an observation deck at the top and was added to the National Register of Historic Places on May 2, 1974.
Coast Range Summit
The Oregon Coast Range, often called simply the Coast Range and sometimes the Pacific Coast Range, is a mountain range, in the Pacific Coast Ranges physiographic region, in the U.S. state of Oregon along the Pacific Ocean. This north-south running range extends over 200 miles (320 km) from the Columbia River in the north on the border of Oregon and Washington, south to the middle fork of the Coquille River. It is 30 to 60 miles (48 to 97 km) wide and averages around 1,500 feet (460 m) in elevation above sea level. The coast range has three main sections, a Northern, Central, and Southern.
Private Beaches
The Oregon Coast is a coastal region of the U.S. state of Oregon. It is bordered by the Pacific Ocean to its west and the Oregon Coast Range to the east, and stretches approximately 362 miles (583 km) from the California state border in the south to the Columbia River in the north. The region is not a specific geological, environmental, or political entity, and includes the Columbia River Estuary.
Remote Sea Lions
Access to the lighthouse is severely limited, with a helicopter landing the only practical way to access the rock, and it is off-limits even to the owners during the seabird nesting season. The structure was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1981[10] and is part of the Oregon Islands National Wildlife Refuge. The lighthouse’s rock is now frequently visited by thousands of sea lions, seals, and sea birds.
In April 2022, Eternity at Sea announced that the property was for sale. The buildings were said to be in need of complete renovation due to damage from storms, nesting birds and sea lions.
Columbia River Forts
Fort Stevens was an American military installation that guarded the mouth of the Columbia River in the state of Oregon. Built near the end of the American Civil War, it was named for Civil War general and former Washington Territory governor, Isaac I. Stevens. The fort was an active military reservation from 1863–1947.It is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Today the site is an Oregon state park just northwest of Warrenton.
Gearhart Golf Course
Gearhart Golf Links is The Oldest Golf Course West of the Mississippi River and shares the early spotlight with such courses as Victoria Golf Club (1893), Tacoma Country and Golf Club (1894) and Del Monte Golf Club (1897). From its original three holes, Gearhart Golf Links has stayed true to its Scottish roots and offers a pleasurable round (now 18 holes) for all golfers. To this day, the course retains that classic links-style flavor, with a hint of traditional Northwest design features. A rich history, but with an eye to a glorious future.

en , una estilizada adaptación digital del aclamado juego de mesa. Dirige un ejército de hormigas, saltamontes y otros bichos para rodear a la abeja reina de tu oponente antes de que seas tú quien caiga con la misma estrategia. Cada ficha hexagonal que juegas va creando el tablero sobre la marcha; además, las fichas se mueven según las reglas de cada bicho (por ejemplo, los saltamontes saltan en línea recta sobre otras piezas). ¡Define la mejor estrategia, supera a tu rival y apodérate de la colmena!
cualquier insecto puede cambiar el rumbo del juego. Activa trampas a distancia con las hormigas. Bloquea casillas con los escarabajos de ralentización. Las reglas son sencillas, pero su profundidad es impresionante.
las abejas reina pueden moverse una casilla para evadir el avance de tus fuerzas, pero poner a un escarabajo sobre la reina de tu oponente evitará que escape.
GiantStep, con sede en Budapest, se apoyó en su experiencia en la creación de algoritmos para desarrollar a RustyBlade, el oponente de IA de , que puede ser indulgente o implacable según los ajustes que apliques. === PAGE: https://www.bigcanoepoa.org/property-owners/public-safety/weather-event-procedures/
TITLE: Weather Event Procedures - Big Canoe POA
Staying safe in Big Canoe during weather events
REGISTER TO GET THE CALL OR TEXT
The most critical step for preparing for impending bad weather is to sign up to receive notifications from the county, which will take the lead role in notifying Big Canoe Property Owners of impending weather events. Reminder: Big Canoe Public Safety is a support organization for the County's leadership.
In a weather emergency event, Big Canoe Communications will be re-distributing the county's messaging using all our available communication channels. Still, the primary communication will come from the county EMA via their alert systems.
Big Canoe Communications
To receive email communications from Big Canoe POA, make sure you have updated your email and phone number in your profile. If you are not receiving POA email, click below and send an ASKTHEPOA to update your information.
Follow us on our official social media channels.
@bigcanoeevents&happenings
Winter Weather Preparedness Check List
Gather supplies before the weather hits. Have a 72-hour supply of food and water stocked in your home, but a week’s supply is recommended. Make sure to have your prescriptions ﬁlled as well as a good supply of over-the-counter meds and ﬁrst-aid provisions.
Protect your pipes from freezing by allowing them to drip continuously until the weather warms up.
WINTERIZING YOUR HOME TIPS
Backup power and heat are recommended. This could mean a backup generator or alternative heat source, such as a ﬁreplace, that can be used if the power fails.
If you have a wood ﬁreplace, stock up on wood as soon as possible, and use ﬁreplace safety best practices.
Avoid traveling as much as possible, even when roads appear clear. Black ice, especially on our hills, is a nearly invisible and highly dangerous hazard.
Have multiple ﬂashlights ready, which you should also test. If you use candlelight, watch the ﬂame carefully to avoid a surprise ﬁre.
In the event of a power outage, check the Amicalola Outage Map to determine if your area has been identified: https://outages.amicalolaemc.com/ (If your area is not included, please call Amicalola EMC at 706-253-0359.)
If you use a space heater, be sure to keep it at least three feet away from furniture and drapes. Electric space heaters with automatic shut-oﬀ switches and non-glowing elements are the safest.
If you see Public Safety vehicles traveling with ease, it’s likely because we have installed heavy-duty tire chains or are in a track-equipped vehicle. Do not try to follow a Public Safety vehicle unless you are told to do so.
Consider stocking up on foods that do not require cooking.
Be sure to have a manual can opener on hand.
If you must travel, a good idea is to have a cell phone charger that you keep fully charged, boots for cold and wet weather, snacks, food, water, and blankets in your vehicle in case you become stranded.
When driving through Big Canoe, be aware that our rapid elevation changes mean that some areas in Big Canoe are colder than others. While it may be raining at the North Gate, it could be snowing on Cox Mountain Drive.
If you are stranded in our community, try to ﬁnd a nearby home to stay in while you wait for help. Public Safety will attempt to access anyone stuck in a bad place, but they can’t guarantee a quick arrival if the conditions are an issue.
Please be patient! Big Canoe has a large ﬂeet of road-clearing equipment to make roads passable as quickly as possible; however, due to our elevation and temperatures, if the roads are plowed and cleared too soon, an icy ﬁlm will freeze, resulting in black ice.

From the moment you drive through the Main Gate and across our historic covered bridge, you know you’ve been transported to a special place that you won’t soon forget.
DINING IN BIG CANOE
Enjoy the mountains and lake views as you dine at the Clubhouse, or have a leisurely patio meal at Duffer's Grab and Go or Beach Club. A variety of meals are available.
There are many water activities to enjoy at Lake Petit. Your first stop should be The Marina where you can rent a boat or kayak, or purchase a fishing permit with rods and tackle. We have everything you need for a great day on Lake Petit.
Cool off and make a splash at The Beach Club! Enjoy the pool, lake swimming with an inflatable waterpark and a sandy beach front. Paddleboats, canoes, kayaks, paddleboards are available with our famous 200-foot rockslide.
Big Canoe offers golf courses - Cherokee, Choctaw, and Creek. Rental clubs are available and tee times must be booked up to four days in advance. Visit our Golf Pro Shop located in the lower level of the Clubhouse at Lake Sconti for any golfing needs during your visit.
RACQUET SPORTS
The Racquet Club has eight outdoor hard couts with six Har-Tru clay courts, two hard courts, four lighted pickleball courts, and two indoor tennis courts. Racquetball is also available at the Wellness Center. Equipment may be rented or purchased in these areas from the fully stocked Pro Shop!
The Racquet Club has eight outdoor hard couts with six Har-Tru clay courts, two hard courts, four lighted pickleball courts, and two indoor tennis courts. Racquetball is also available at the Wellness Center. Equipment may be rented in these areas.
TRAILS & PARKS
The trails of Big Canoe offer 25-miles of hiking with breath taking views, maintained by the Big Canoe Trails Committee, each have their own unique appeal and standout features. If you're lucky, you might see wildlife along the way.
Big Canoe is a Recognized Nature Preserve by the Georgia Audubon. Guests are strongly advised to review the guidelines designed to maintain our community’s natural beauty and ensure everyone’s safety.

TITLE: Ultimate Offshore Fishing Guide: Best Charters in Pompano
Offshore fishing is not just a pastime; it's an adventure that brings excitement and relaxation together. Pompano Beach, one of Florida's prime fishing destinations, offers thrilling opportunities for both new and seasoned anglers. This guide will equip you with essential tips for choosing the best fishing charter, what to anticipate on your trip, and effective techniques to land the biggest catch.
Why Choose Pompano Beach for Offshore Fishing?
Pompano Beach, situated along Florida's southeastern coast, is renowned for its fishing bounty. The proximity to the Gulf Stream makes it a hotspot for species like sailfish, tuna, and dolphin. For example, during peak seasons, anglers have reported up to a 85% success rate in catching large game fish. The warm waters teeming with marine life provide an incredible backdrop for any fishing adventure.
When choosing Pompano Beach, you’re not only selecting a fishing site but also immersing yourself in the scenic beauty of the ocean and enjoying a unique coastal vibe. With a variety of fishing charters available, you'll find numerous options that suit your preferences.
What to Look for in a Fishing Charter
Finding the right fishing charter can enhance your overall experience. Here’s what to consider:
Experience and Reputation
: Opt for charters that feature seasoned captains and crews with good track records. Look at online reviews; a charter with an average rating above 4.5 stars can be a good sign of quality service.
Type of Fishing
: Charters may focus on specific fishing types. If you want to target snapper, for instance, ensure the charter specializes in bottom fishing, which can increase your chances of success for those species.
Equipment and Amenities
: Look for charters that provide quality fishing gear. For example, charters that offer state-of-the-art fishing rods and reels can make a significant difference in your catch rate.
Group Size and Private Charters
: Decide if you prefer a more social setting with a shared trip or a private charter for a more intimate experience. For example, a private charter for up to 6 people can be perfect for a family outing or a very personalized experience. Most of the time for 2 people it is worth paying the extra to book the full boat and not fight over fish.
Pricing and Packages
: Compare the costs carefully. Some charters offer half-day trips (approximately 4 hours) for around $500-$1,600 while full-day excursions (8 hours) can range from $1,200 to $2,500 depending on the amenities provided.
Preparing for Your Fishing Trip
Preparation promotes a more enjoyable offshore fishing trip. Here’s how to get ready:
Dress Appropriately
: Wear breathable clothing that protects you from the sun and sea splashes. Bring along essential items like a hat, polarizing sunglasses, good sunscreen, and a good rain jacket incase it rains.
Bring the Essentials
: Stay hydrated during the trip by packing enough water. Snacks like trail mix or energy bars can keep your energy levels up while you're waiting for a bite.
Know the Rules
: Understand the local fishing regulations in advance. For instance, the legal size for harvesting certain fish can vary significantly. Your charter crew will guide you, but awareness is key.
Stay Flexible
: Offshore fishing can be hit or miss, influenced by weather and fish behavior. Embrace the unpredictability and enjoy the day, regardless of how many fish you catch, fishing changes day to day even hour to hour sometimes.
The Adventure Begins: What to Expect on the Water
Once you board your selected fishing charter, the adventure truly begins. Here’s what typically happens during your offshore fishing trip:
Setting Off
: As the boat departs, take in the breathtaking views of the coast. The journey to the fishing grounds can be as enjoyable as the fishing itself.
Fishing Techniques
: The captain will explain various fishing techniques you'll use. If trolling for larger species, you might learn about specific lures that are most effective in Pompano Beach waters.
Catching Fish
: The moment you feel a tug on your line is electrifying. The adrenaline rush of reeling in a fish adds excitement to the trip. Many anglers report the thrill of catching a 50-pound sailfish as one of their most memorable moments.
An eager angler with a large Sailfish catch off Pompano Beach, showcasing the joys of fishing.
Post-Fishing Fun
: Many charters allow you to take photos with your catch and may even offer to clean it for you. Sharing your success on social media becomes part of the fun. Don't forget to tag your charter guide as it helps show other people how much fun you had with them.
Post-Trip Considerations: Enjoying Your Catch
After a rewarding fishing trip, consider the following options for your catch:
Cooking at Home
: Simple recipes can make your fresh fish truly special. Grilling mahi or preparing a tuna poke bowl can be a delightful way to relive your day on the water.
Local Restaurants
: Numerous Pompano Beach restaurants offer a "catch and cook" option. For example, some local spots will prepare the fish you bring in, giving you a restaurant-quality meal.
Sharing with Friends
: Consider hosting a seafood barbecue to celebrate your fishing success. This not only provides a delicious meal but also a great chance to reminisce about your adventure.
Catch and Release
: If you're passionate about conservation, practicing catch and release helps sustain fish populations for future generations. Many charters are advocates of this approach.
Embrace the Thrill of Offshore Fishing
Offshore fishing in Pompano Beach offers exciting adventures, relaxation, and lasting memories. With thorough preparation, a reputable fishing charter, and the right mindset, you can enjoy a fantastic day on the open sea.

Tips for a Successful Fishing Charter
Booking a fishing charter is the first step toward an exciting and memorable experience on the water. Whether you're heading out for deep sea fishing in Pompano Beach or exploring Florida’s nearshore reefs, knowing what to expect—and how to prepare—can make all the difference. This guide will help you get the most out of your charter fishing trip.
Before You Book Your Fishing Charter
Choosing the right charter service is essential. Do your homework by reading reviews, checking licenses, and confirming that the captain has a strong local reputation.
Tips for Choosing a Charter in Pompano Beach
Look for captains with experience fishing the waters off Pompano Beach.
Ask what type of fish are in season and what techniques they use.
Make sure the boat is well-equipped and properly maintained.

Choose a charter that fits your group—family-friendly, sport fishing, or offshore big game.
What to Bring on Your Fishing Trip
Your charter will supply most essentials, but here are a few items you should bring to stay comfortable and safe:
Sunscreen (reef-safe)
Hat and polarized sunglasses
Non-slip shoes
Food and drinks (no glass bottles)
Camera or smartphone
Motion sickness medication (if needed)
Keep in mind that South Florida weather can change quickly, so bringing a light rain jacket is also a good idea.
Bottom Fishing
Great for catching snapper, grouper, and other reef-dwelling fish. You'll often do this over shipwrecks and reefs.
Understanding the Fishing Techniques Used
Kite Fishing
A specialty technique in South Florida, especially for sailfish. The kite keeps the bait suspended at the water's surface, which mimics natural movement.
Fishing Charter Etiquette
Respect the captain, the crew, and the ocean. Arrive early, follow instructions, and keep the boat tidy. Tipping your crew is customary—typically 15–20% of the trip cost.
Trolling
Trolling is commonly used in Pompano Beach deep sea fishing to target fast-moving species like kingfish, tuna, mahi-mahi, and sailfish.
Frequently Asked Questions (Fishing Charter FAQs)
What fish are in season in Pompano Beach?
Fish species vary by season. Winter months are ideal for sailfish and kingfish. Spring and summer bring mahi-mahi, tuna, and wahoo. Grouper and snapper are available year-round.
What happens if the weather is bad?
Safety is the priority. If weather conditions are unsafe, the charter will be rescheduled or canceled with a refund or credit. Always check with the captain the day before.
Do I need a fishing license for a charter in Florida?
No. When you book a licensed fishing charter like Just Right Florida Charters, your fishing license is included for the duration of your trip.
Is deep sea fishing safe for kids and families?
Absolutely. Just Right Florida Charters offers family-friendly trips that are both safe and fun. Shorter, calmer nearshore trips are perfect for young anglers.
What’s the best time of year to book a fishing charter in Pompano Beach?
The best time depends on your target species. Winter through early spring is excellent for billfish, while summer offers fantastic offshore action for mahi-mahi and tuna. Year-round reef and wreck fishing is also productive.
How long are typical fishing charters?
Trips typically range from 4-hour half-day charters to full-day 8-hour offshore excursions. Custom durations are also available.
What should I wear on a fishing trip in Florida?
Wear lightweight, breathable clothing, a hat, and sunglasses. Sunscreen and non-marking boat shoes are essential. A long-sleeved shirt helps protect against sunburn.
What is the best bait for fishing in Pompano Beach?
Live bait such as goggle eyes, pilchards, or ballyhoo is often used for larger gamefish. Dead bait and artificial lures may be used depending on the target species.
Can I keep the fish I catch?
Yes, as long as the fish meets Florida state regulations. The crew will clean and fillet your legal catch for you to take home.
Do I need experience to go on a charter fishing trip?
Not at all. Fishing charters are great for beginners and experienced anglers alike. The crew will teach you everything you need to know.

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

limb aboard our classic yacht and take in Seattle’s waterfront views of beautiful Lake Union and adjoining waterways.
